## Managed PostgreSQL Database Create

<a id="opIdpostDatabasesPostgreSQLInstances"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/databases/postgresql/instances \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_list": [
      "203.0.113.1/32",
      "192.0.1.0/24"
    ],
    "cluster_size": 3,
    "encrypted": false,
    "engine": "postgresql/13.2",
    "label": "example-db",
    "region": "us-east",
    "replication_commit_type": "local",
    "replication_type": "semi_synch",
    "ssl_connection": true,
    "type": "g6-dedicated-2"
  }'
```

`POST /databases/postgresql/instances`

Provision a Managed PostgreSQL Database.

Restricted Users must have the `add_databases` grant to use this command.

New instances can take approximately 15 to 30 minutes to provision.

The `allow_list` is used to control access to the Managed Database.

* IP addresses and ranges in this list can access the Managed Database. All other sources are blocked.

* If `0.0.0.0/0` is a value in this list, then all IP addresses can access the Managed Database.

* Entering an empty array (`[]`) blocks all connections (both public and private) to the Managed Database.

All Managed Databases include automatic, daily backups. Up to seven backups are automatically stored for each Managed Database, providing restore points for each day of the past week.

All Managed Databases include automatic patch updates, which apply security patches and updates to the underlying operating system of the Managed PostgreSQL Database during configurable maintenance windows.

* If your database cluster is configured with a single node, you will experience downtime during this maintenance window when any updates occur. It's recommended that you adjust this window to match a time that will be the least disruptive for your application and users. You may also want to consider upgrading to a high availability plan to avoid any downtime due to maintenance.

* **The database software is not updated automatically.** To upgrade to a new database engine version, consider deploying a new Managed Database with your preferred version. You can then migrate your databases from the original Managed Database cluster to the new one.

* To modify update the maintenance window for a Database, use the **Managed PostgreSQL Database Update** ([PUT /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}](/docs/api/databases/#managed-postgresql-database-update)) command.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_list": [
    "203.0.113.1/32",
    "192.0.1.0/24"
  ],
  "cluster_size": 3,
  "encrypted": false,
  "engine": "postgresql/13.2",
  "label": "example-db",
  "region": "us-east",
  "replication_commit_type": "local",
  "replication_type": "semi_synch",
  "ssl_connection": true,
  "type": "g6-dedicated-2"
}
```

<h3 id="managed-postgresql-database-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DatabasePostgreSQLRequest](#schemadatabasepostgresqlrequest)|true|Information about the Managed PostgreSQL Database you are creating.|
|» allow_list|body|[string(ipv4/prefix_length)]|false|A list of IP addresses that can access the Managed Database. Each item can be a single IP address or a range in CIDR format.<br><br>By default, this is an empty array (`[]`), which blocks all connections (both public and private) to the Managed Database.<br><br>If `0.0.0.0/0` is a value in this list, then all IP addresses can access the Managed Database.<br>|
|» cluster_size|body|integer|false|The number of Linode Instance nodes deployed to the Managed Database.<br><br>Choosing 3 nodes creates a high availability cluster consisting of 1 primary node and 2 replica nodes.<br>|
|» encrypted|body|boolean|false|Whether the Managed Databases is encrypted.|
|» engine|body|string|true|The Managed Database engine in engine/version format.|
|» label|body|string|true|A unique, user-defined string referring to the Managed Database.|
|» region|body|string|true|The [Region](/docs/api/regions/) ID for the Managed Database.|
|» replication_commit_type|body|string|false|The synchronization level of the replicating server.<br><br>Must be `local` or `off` for the `asynch` replication type.<br><br>Must be `on`, `remote_write`, or `remote_apply` for the `semi_synch` replication type.<br>|
|» replication_type|body|string|false|The replication method used for the Managed Database.<br><br>Defaults to `none` for a single cluster and `semi_synch` for a high availability cluster.<br><br>Must be `none` for a single node cluster.<br><br>Must be `asynch` or `semi_synch` for a high availability cluster.<br>|
|» ssl_connection|body|boolean|false|Whether to require SSL credentials to establish a connection to the Managed Database.<br><br>Use the **Managed PostgreSQL Database Credentials View** ([GET /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}/credentials](/docs/api/databases/#managed-postgresql-database-credentials-view)) command for access information.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The Linode Instance type used by the Managed Database for its nodes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cluster_size|1|
|» cluster_size|3|
|» replication_commit_type|on|
|» replication_commit_type|local|
|» replication_commit_type|remote_write|
|» replication_commit_type|remote_apply|
|» replication_commit_type|off|
|» replication_type|none|
|» replication_type|asynch|
|» replication_type|semi_synch|

```json
    "203.0.113.1/32",

  ],

  "created": "2022-01-01T00:01:01",
  "encrypted": false,
  "engine": "postgresql",
  "hosts": {
    "primary": "lin-0000-000-pgsql-primary.servers.linodedb.net",
    "secondary": "lin-0000-000-pgsql-primary-private.servers.linodedb.net"
  },
  "id": 123,
  "label": "example-db",
  "port": 3306,
```

## Managed PostgreSQL Database Update

<a id="opIdputDatabasesPostgreSQLInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/databases/postgresql/instances/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_list": [
      "203.0.113.1/32",
      "192.0.1.0/24"
    ],
    "label": "example-db",
    "updates": {
      "day_of_week": 1,
      "duration": 3,
      "frequency": "weekly",
      "hour_of_day": 0,
      "week_of_month": null
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}`

Update a Managed PostgreSQL Database.

Requires `read_write` access to the Database.

The Database must have an `active` status to perform this command.

Updating addresses in the `allow_list` overwrites any existing addresses.

* IP addresses and ranges in this list can access the Managed Database. All other sources are blocked.

* If `0.0.0.0/0` is a value in this list, then all IP addresses can access the Managed Database.

* Entering an empty array (`[]`) blocks all connections (both public and private) to the Managed Database.

* **Note**: Updates to the `allow_list` may take a short period of time to complete, making this command inappropriate for rapid successive updates to this property.

All Managed Databases include automatic patch updates, which apply security patches and updates to the underlying operating system of the Managed PostgreSQL Database. The maintenance window for these updates is configured with the Managed Database's `updates` property.

* If your database cluster is configured with a single node, you will experience downtime during this maintenance window when any updates occur. It's recommended that you adjust this window to match a time that will be the least disruptive for your application and users. You may also want to consider upgrading to a high availability plan to avoid any downtime due to maintenance.

* **The database software is not updated automatically.** To upgrade to a new database engine version, consider deploying a new Managed Database with your preferred version. You can then migrate your databases from the original Managed Database cluster to the new one.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_list": [
    "203.0.113.1/32",
    "192.0.1.0/24"
  ],
  "label": "example-db",
  "updates": {
    "day_of_week": 1,
    "duration": 3,
    "frequency": "weekly",
    "hour_of_day": 0,
    "week_of_month": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="managed-postgresql-database-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|instanceId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Managed PostgreSQL Database.|
|body|body|object|true|Updated information for the Managed PostgreSQL Database.|
|» allow_list|body|[string(ipv4/prefix_length)]|false|A list of IP addresses that can access the Managed Database. Each item can be a single IP address or a range in CIDR format.<br><br>By default, this is an empty array (`[]`), which blocks all connections (both public and private) to the Managed Database.<br><br>If `0.0.0.0/0` is a value in this list, then all IP addresses can access the Managed Database.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|A unique, user-defined string referring to the Managed Database.|
|» updates|body|object|false|Configuration settings for automated patch update maintenance for the Managed Database.|
|» » day_of_week|body|integer|false|The day to perform maintenance. 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, etc.|
|» » duration|body|integer|false|The maximum maintenance window time in hours.|
|» » frequency|body|string|false|Whether maintenance occurs on a weekly or monthly basis.|
|» » hour_of_day|body|integer|false|The hour to begin maintenance based in UTC time.|
|» » week_of_month|body|integer \| null|false|The week of the month to perform `monthly` frequency updates. Defaults to `null`.<br><br>* Required for `monthly` frequency updates.<br><br>* Must be `null` for `weekly` frequency updates.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » frequency|weekly|
|» » frequency|monthly|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "allow_list": [
    "203.0.113.1/32",
    "192.0.1.0/24"
  ],
  "cluster_size": 3,
  "created": "2022-01-01T00:01:01",
  "encrypted": false,
  "engine": "postgresql",
  "hosts": {
    "primary": "lin-0000-000-pgsql-primary.servers.linodedb.net",
    "secondary": "lin-0000-000-pgsql-primary-private.servers.linodedb.net"
  },
  "id": 123,
  "label": "example-db",
  "port": 3306,
  "region": "us-east",
  "replication_commit_type": "local",
  "replication_type": "semi_synch",
  "ssl_connection": true,
  "status": "active",
  "type": "g6-dedicated-2",
  "updated": "2022-01-01T00:01:01",
  "updates": {
    "day_of_week": 1,
    "duration": 3,
    "frequency": "weekly",
    "hour_of_day": 0,
    "week_of_month": null
  },
  "version": "13.2"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

`GET /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}/backups`

Display all backups for an accessible Managed PostgreSQL Database.

The Database must not be provisioning to perform this command.

Database `auto` type backups are created every 24 hours at 0:00 UTC. Each `auto` backup is retained for 7 days.

Database `snapshot` type backups are created by accessing the **Managed PostgreSQL Database Backup Snapshot Create** ([POST /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}/backups](/docs/api/databases/#managed-postgresql-database-backup-snapshot-create)) command.

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "db-snapshot",
    "target": "primary"
  }'
```

`POST /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}/backups`

Creates a snapshot backup of a Managed PostgreSQL Database.

Requires `read_write` access to the Database.

Up to 3 snapshot backups for each Database can be stored at a time. If 3 snapshots have been created for a Database, one must be deleted before another can be made.

Backups generated by this command have the type `snapshot`. Snapshot backups may take several minutes to complete, after which they will be accessible to view or restore.

The Database must have an `active` status to perform this command. If another backup is in progress, it must complete before a new backup can be initiated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "db-snapshot",
  "target": "primary"
}
```

<h3 id="managed-postgresql-database-backup-snapshot-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|instanceId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Managed PostgreSQL Database.|
|body|body|[DatabaseBackupSnapshot](#schemadatabasebackupsnapshot)|false|Information about the snapshot backup to create.|
|» label|body|string|true|The label for the Database snapshot backup.<br><br>* Must include only ASCII letters or numbers.<br>* Must be unique among other backup labels for this Database.<br>|
|» target|body|string|false|The Database cluster target.<br>If the Database is a high availability cluster, choosing `secondary` creates a snapshot backup of a replica node.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» target|primary|
|» target|secondary|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="managed-postgresql-database-backup-snapshot-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Database snapshot backup request successful.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="managed-postgresql-database-backup-snapshot-create-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

## Managed PostgreSQL Database Patch

<a id="opIdpostDatabasesPostgreSQLInstancePatch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/databases/postgresql/instances/0/patch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}/patch`

Apply security patches and updates to the underlying operating system of the Managed PostgreSQL Database. This function runs during regular maintenance windows, which are configurable with the **Managed PostgreSQL Database Update** ([PUT /databases/postgresql/instances/{instanceId}](/docs/api/databases/#managed-postgresql-database-update)) command.

Requires `read_write` access to the Database.

The Database must have an `active` status to perform this command.

**Note**

* If your database cluster is configured with a single node, you will experience downtime during this maintenance. Consider upgrading to a high availability plan to avoid any downtime due to maintenance.

* **The database software is not updated automatically.** To upgrade to a new database engine version, consider deploying a new Managed Database with your preferred version. You can then migrate your databases from the original Managed Database cluster to the new one.


<h3 id="managed-postgresql-database-patch-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|instanceId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Managed PostgreSQL Database.|

```json
{}
```

```json
}
```

## Domain Create

<a id="opIdcreateDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "axfr_ips": [],
    "description": null,
    "domain": "example.org",
    "expire_sec": 300,
    "group": null,
    "master_ips": [],
    "refresh_sec": 300,
    "retry_sec": 300,
    "soa_email": "admin@example.org",
    "status": "active",
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ],
    "ttl_sec": 300,
    "type": "master"
  }'
```

`POST /domains`

Adds a new Domain to Linode's DNS Manager. Linode is not a registrar, and you must own the domain before adding it here. Be sure to point your registrar to Linode's nameservers so that the records hosted here are used.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "axfr_ips": [],
  "description": null,
  "domain": "example.org",
  "expire_sec": 300,
  "group": null,
  "master_ips": [],
  "refresh_sec": 300,
  "retry_sec": 300,
  "soa_email": "admin@example.org",
  "status": "active",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "ttl_sec": 300,
  "type": "master"
}
```

<h3 id="domain-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the domain you are registering.|
|» axfr_ips|body|[string(ip)]|false|The list of IPs that may perform a zone transfer for this Domain. The total combined length of all data within this array cannot exceed 1000 characters.<br><br>**Note**: This is potentially dangerous, and should be set to an empty list unless you intend to use it.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A description for this Domain. This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» domain|body|string|true|The domain this Domain represents. Domain labels cannot be longer than 63 characters and must conform to [RFC1035](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1035). Domains must be unique on Linode's platform, including across different Linode accounts; there cannot be two Domains representing the same domain.<br>|
|» expire_sec|body|integer|false|The amount of time in seconds that may pass before this Domain is no longer<br>authoritative.<br><br>* Valid values are<br>0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br><br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br><br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 1209600.<br>|
|» group|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** The group this Domain belongs to.  This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» master_ips|body|[string(ip)]|false|The IP addresses representing the master DNS for this Domain. At least one value is required for `type` slave Domains. The total combined length of all data within this array cannot exceed 1000 characters.<br>|
|» refresh_sec|body|integer|false|The amount of time in seconds before this Domain should be refreshed.<br><br>* Valid values are<br>0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br><br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br><br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 14400.<br>|
|» retry_sec|body|integer|false|The interval, in seconds, at which a failed refresh should be retried.<br><br>* Valid values are<br>0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br><br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br><br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 14400.<br>|
|» soa_email|body|string(email)|false|Start of Authority email address. This is required for `type` master Domains.<br>|
|» status|body|string|false|Used to control whether this Domain is currently being rendered.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to this object.  Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|» ttl_sec|body|integer|false|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers.<br>* Valid values are 0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 86400.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|Whether this Domain represents the authoritative source of information for the domain it describes ("master"), or whether it is a read-only copy of a master ("slave").<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|disabled|
|» status|active|
|» type|master|
|» type|slave|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "axfr_ips": [],
  "description": null,
  "domain": "example.org",
  "expire_sec": 300,
  "group": null,
  "id": 1234,
  "master_ips": [],
  "refresh_sec": 300,
  "retry_sec": 300,
  "soa_email": "admin@example.org",
  "status": "active",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "ttl_sec": 300,
  "type": "master"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Domain Import

<a id="opIdimportDomain"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/domains/import \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "domain": "example.com",

  }'
```

`POST /domains/import`

Imports a domain zone from a remote nameserver.
Your nameserver must allow zone transfers (AXFR) from the following IPs:

  - 96.126.114.97
  - 96.126.114.98
  - 2600:3c00::5e
  - 2600:3c00::5f


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "domain": "example.com",
  "remote_nameserver": "examplenameserver.com"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Information about the Domain to import.|
|» domain|body|string|true|The domain to import.<br>|
|» remote_nameserver|body|string|true|The remote nameserver that allows zone transfers (AXFR).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "axfr_ips": [],
  "description": null,
  "domain": "example.org",
  "expire_sec": 300,
  "group": null,
  "id": 1234,
  "master_ips": [],
  "refresh_sec": 300,
  "retry_sec": 300,
  "soa_email": "admin@example.org",
  "status": "active",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",

  ],
  "ttl_sec": 300,
  "type": "master"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
```

## Domain Record Create

<a id="opIdcreateDomainRecord"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/domains/0/records \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "test",
    "port": 80,
    "priority": 50,
    "protocol": null,
    "service": null,
    "tag": null,
    "target": "192.0.2.0",
    "ttl_sec": 604800,
    "type": "A",
    "weight": 50
  }'
```

`POST /domains/{domainId}/records`

Adds a new Domain Record to the zonefile this Domain represents.

Each domain can have up to 12,000 active records.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "test",
  "port": 80,
  "priority": 50,
  "protocol": null,
  "service": null,
  "tag": null,
  "target": "192.0.2.0",
  "ttl_sec": 604800,
  "type": "A",
  "weight": 50
}
```

<h3 id="domain-record-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domainId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Domain we are accessing Records for.|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the new Record to add.<br>|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends<br>on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The hostname or FQDN of the Record.<br><br>`NS`: The subdomain, if any, to use with the Domain of the Record. Wildcard NS records (`*`) are not supported.<br><br>`MX`: The mail subdomain. For example, `sub` for the address `user@sub.example.com` under the `example.com`<br>Domain. Must be an empty string (`""`) for a Null MX Record.<br><br>`CNAME`: The hostname. Must be unique. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The hostname.<br><br>`SRV`: Unused. Use the `service` property to set the service name for this record.<br><br>`CAA`: The subdomain. Omit or enter an empty string (`""`) to apply to the entire Domain.<br><br>`PTR`: See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br>|
|» port|body|integer|false|The port this Record points to. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|
|» priority|body|integer|false|The priority of the target host for this Record. Lower values are preferred. Only valid for<br>MX and SRV record requests. Required for SRV record requests.<br><br>Defaults to `0` for MX record requests. Must be `0` for Null MX records.<br>|
|» protocol|body|string \| null|false|The protocol this Record's service communicates with. An underscore (`_`) is prepended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid for SRV record requests.<br>|
|» service|body|string \| null|false|The name of the service. An underscore (`_`) is prepended and a period (`.`) is appended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|
|» tag|body|string \| null|false|The tag portion of a CAA record. Only valid and required for CAA record requests.<br>|
|» target|body|string|false|The target for this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends<br>on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The IP address. Use `[remote_addr]` to submit the IPv4 address of the request. Required.<br><br>`NS`: The name server. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`MX`: The mail server. Must be a valid domain unless creating a Null MX Record. To create a<br>[Null MX Record](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7505), first<br>[remove](/docs/api/domains/#domain-record-delete) any additional MX records, create an MX record with empty strings<br>(`""`) for the `target` and `name`. If a Domain has a Null MX record, new MX records cannot be created. Required.<br><br>`CNAME`: The alias. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The value. Required.<br><br>`SRV`: The target domain or subdomain. If a subdomain is entered, it is automatically used with the Domain.<br>To configure for a different domain, enter a valid FQDN. For example, the value `www` with a Domain for<br>`example.com` results in a target set to `www.example.com`, whereas the value `sample.com` results in a<br>target set to `sample.com`. Required.<br><br>`CAA`: The value. For `issue` or `issuewild` tags, the domain of your certificate issuer. For the `iodef`<br>tag, a contact or submission URL (domain, http, https, or mailto). Requirements depend on the tag for this record:<br>  * `issue`: The domain of your certificate issuer. Must be a valid domain.<br>  * `issuewild`: Must begin with `*`.<br>  * `iodef`: Must be either (1) a valid domain, (2) a valid domain prepended with `http://` or `https://`, or (3) a valid email address prepended with `mailto:`.<br><br>`PTR`: Required. See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br><br>With the exception of A, AAAA, and CAA records, this field accepts a trailing period.<br>|
|» ttl_sec|body|integer|false|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers. Valid values are 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200 - any other value will be rounded to the nearest valid value.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of Record this is in the DNS system. For example, A records associate a domain name with an IPv4 address, and AAAA records associate a domain name with an IPv6 address. For more information, see the guides on [DNS Record Types](/docs/products/networking/dns-manager/guides/#dns-record-types).<br>|
|» weight|body|integer|false|The relative weight of this Record used in the case of identical priority. Higher values are preferred. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» tag|issue|
|» tag|issuewild|
|» tag|iodef|
|» type|A|
|» type|AAAA|
|» type|NS|
|» type|MX|
|» type|CNAME|
|» type|TXT|
|» type|SRV|
|» type|PTR|
|» type|CAA|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "id": 123456,
  "name": "test",
  "port": 80,
  "priority": 50,
  "protocol": null,
  "service": null,
  "tag": null,
  "target": "192.0.2.0",
  "ttl_sec": 604800,
  "type": "A",
  "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "weight": 50
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Domain Record Update

<a id="opIdupdateDomainRecord"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/domains/0/records/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "test",
    "port": 80,
    "priority": 50,
    "protocol": null,
    "service": null,
    "tag": null,
    "target": "192.0.2.0",
    "ttl_sec": 604800,
    "weight": 50
  }'
```

`PUT /domains/{domainId}/records/{recordId}`

Updates a single Record on this Domain.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "test",
  "port": 80,
  "priority": 50,
  "protocol": null,
  "service": null,
  "tag": null,
  "target": "192.0.2.0",
  "ttl_sec": 604800,
  "weight": 50
}
```

<h3 id="domain-record-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domainId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Domain whose Record you are accessing.|
|recordId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Record you are accessing.|
|body|body|object|true|The values to change.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends<br>on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The hostname or FQDN of the Record.<br><br>`NS`: The subdomain, if any, to use with the Domain of the Record. Wildcard NS records (`*`) are not supported.<br><br>`MX`: The mail subdomain. For example, `sub` for the address `user@sub.example.com` under the `example.com`<br>Domain. Must be an empty string (`""`) for a Null MX Record.<br><br>`CNAME`: The hostname. Must be unique. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The hostname.<br><br>`SRV`: Unused. Use the `service` property to set the service name for this record.<br><br>`CAA`: The subdomain. Omit or enter an empty string (`""`) to apply to the entire Domain.<br><br>`PTR`: See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br>|
|» port|body|integer|false|The port this Record points to. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|
|» priority|body|integer|false|The priority of the target host for this Record. Lower values are preferred. Only valid for<br>MX and SRV record requests. Required for SRV record requests.<br><br>Defaults to `0` for MX record requests. Must be `0` for Null MX records.<br>|
|» protocol|body|string \| null|false|The protocol this Record's service communicates with. An underscore (`_`) is prepended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid for SRV record requests.<br>|
|» service|body|string \| null|false|The name of the service. An underscore (`_`) is prepended and a period (`.`) is appended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|
|» tag|body|string \| null|false|The tag portion of a CAA record. Only valid and required for CAA record requests.<br>|
|» target|body|string|false|The target for this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends<br>on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The IP address. Use `[remote_addr]` to submit the IPv4 address of the request. Required.<br><br>`NS`: The name server. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`MX`: The mail server. Must be a valid domain unless creating a Null MX Record. To create a<br>[Null MX Record](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7505), first<br>[remove](/docs/api/domains/#domain-record-delete) any additional MX records, create an MX record with empty strings<br>(`""`) for the `target` and `name`. If a Domain has a Null MX record, new MX records cannot be created. Required.<br><br>`CNAME`: The alias. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The value. Required.<br><br>`SRV`: The target domain or subdomain. If a subdomain is entered, it is automatically used with the Domain.<br>To configure for a different domain, enter a valid FQDN. For example, the value `www` with a Domain for<br>`example.com` results in a target set to `www.example.com`, whereas the value `sample.com` results in a<br>target set to `sample.com`. Required.<br><br>`CAA`: The value. For `issue` or `issuewild` tags, the domain of your certificate issuer. For the `iodef`<br>tag, a contact or submission URL (domain, http, https, or mailto). Requirements depend on the tag for this record:<br>  * `issue`: The domain of your certificate issuer. Must be a valid domain.<br>  * `issuewild`: Must begin with `*`.<br>  * `iodef`: Must be either (1) a valid domain, (2) a valid domain prepended with `http://` or `https://`, or (3) a valid email address prepended with `mailto:`.<br><br>`PTR`: Required. See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br><br>With the exception of A, AAAA, and CAA records, this field accepts a trailing period.<br>|
|» ttl_sec|body|integer|false|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers. Valid values are 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200 - any other value will be rounded to the nearest valid value.<br>|
|» weight|body|integer|false|The relative weight of this Record used in the case of identical priority. Higher values are preferred. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|

|---|---|
|» tag|issue|
|» tag|issuewild|
|» tag|iodef|

## Image Upload

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/images/upload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "This is an example image in the docs.",
    "label": "my-image-label",
    "region": "eu-central"
  }'
```

`POST /images/upload`

Initiates an Image upload.

This endpoint creates a new private Image object and returns it along
with the URL to which image data can be uploaded.

- Image data must be uploaded within 24 hours of creation or the
upload will be cancelled and the image deleted.

- Image uploads should be made as an HTTP PUT request to the URL returned in the `upload_to`
response parameter, with a `Content-type: application/octet-stream` header included in the
request. For example:

      curl -v \
        -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
        --upload-file example.img.gz \
        $UPLOAD_URL \
        --progress-bar \
        --output /dev/null

- Uploaded image data should be compressed in gzip (`.gz`) format. The uncompressed disk should be in raw
disk image (`.img`) format. A maximum compressed file size of 5GB is supported for upload at this time.

**Note:** To initiate and complete an Image upload in a single step, see our guide on how to [Upload an Image](/docs/products/tools/images/guides/upload-an-image/) using Cloud Manager or the Linode CLI `image-upload` plugin.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "This is an example image in the docs.",
  "label": "my-image-label",
  "region": "eu-central"
}
```

<h3 id="image-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|The uploaded Image details.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description for the uploaded Image.|
|» label|body|string|true|Label for the uploaded Image.|
|» region|body|string|true|The region to upload to. Once uploaded, the Image can be used in any region.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "image": {
    "created": "2021-08-14T22:44:02",
    "created_by": "linode",
    "deprecated": false,
    "description": "Example Image description.",
    "eol": "2026-07-01T04:00:00",
    "expiry": null,
    "id": "linode/debian11",
    "is_public": true,
    "label": "Debian 11",
    "size": 2500,
    "status": "available",
    "type": "manual",
    "updated": "2021-08-14T22:44:02",
    "vendor": "Debian"
  },
  "upload_to": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="image-upload-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Image Upload object including the upload URL and Image object.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="image-upload-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h1 id="linode-api-linode-instances">Linode Instances</h1>

Use the Linode Instances endpoints to create, configure, and manage your Linode instances. You can also manage the Linode Backup service; maintain and manage configuration profiles; create and maintain disks, intiate a host migration; view Linode Instance statistics; and more.

## Linode Create

<a id="opIdcreateLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "authorized_keys": [
      "ssh-rsa AAAA_valid_public_ssh_key_123456785== user@their-computer"
    ],
    "authorized_users": [
      "myUser",
      "secondaryUser"
    ],
    "booted": true,
    "image": "linode/debian9",
    "root_pass": "aComplexP@ssword",
    "stackscript_data": {
      "gh_username": "linode"
    },
    "stackscript_id": 10079,
    "backup_id": 1234,
    "backups_enabled": true,
    "group": "Linode-Group",
    "interfaces": [
      {
        "ipam_address": "10.0.0.1/24",
        "label": "example-interface",
        "purpose": "vlan"
      }
    ],
    "label": "linode123",
    "private_ip": true,
    "region": "us-east",
    "swap_size": 512,
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ],
    "type": "g6-standard-2"
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances`

Creates a Linode Instance on your Account. In order for this
request to complete successfully, your User must have the `add_linodes` grant. Creating a
new Linode will incur a charge on your Account.

Linodes can be created using one of the available Types. See
Types List ([GET /linode/types](/docs/api/linode-types/#types-list)) to get more
information about each Type's specs and cost.

Linodes can be created in any one of our available Regions, which are accessible from the
Regions List ([GET /regions](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list)) endpoint.

In an effort to fight spam, Linode restricts outbound connections on ports 25, 465, and 587
on all Linodes for new accounts created after November 5th, 2019. For more information,
see [Sending Email on Linode](/docs/guides/running-a-mail-server/#sending-email-on-linode).

Linodes can be created in a number of ways:

* Using a Linode Public Image distribution or a Private Image you created based on another Linode.
  * Access the Images List ([GET /images](/docs/api/images/#images-list)) endpoint with authentication to view
    all available Images.
  * The Linode will be `running` after it completes `provisioning`.
  * A default config with two Disks, one being a 512 swap disk, is created.
    * `swap_size` can be used to customize the swap disk size.
  * Requires a `root_pass` be supplied to use for the root User's Account.
  * It is recommended to supply SSH keys for the root User using the `authorized_keys` field.
  * You may also supply a list of usernames via the `authorized_users` field.
    * These users must have an SSH Key associated with your Profile first. See SSH Key Add ([POST /profile/sshkeys](/docs/api/profile/#ssh-key-add)) for more information.

* Using a StackScript.
  * See StackScripts List ([GET /linode/stackscripts](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscripts-list)) for
    a list of available StackScripts.
  * The Linode will be `running` after it completes `provisioning`.
  * Requires a compatible Image to be supplied.
    * See StackScript View ([GET /linode/stackscript/{stackscriptId}](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscript-view)) for compatible Images.
  * Requires a `root_pass` be supplied to use for the root User's Account.
  * It is recommended to supply SSH keys for the root User using the `authorized_keys` field.
  * You may also supply a list of usernames via the `authorized_users` field.
    * These users must have an SSH Key associated with your Profile first. See SSH Key Add ([POST /profile/sshkeys](/docs/api/profile/#ssh-key-add)) for more information.

* Using one of your other Linode's backups.
  * You must create a Linode large enough to accommodate the Backup's size.
  * The Disks and Config will match that of the Linode that was backed up.
  * The `root_pass` will match that of the Linode that was backed up.

* Attached to a private VLAN.
  * Review the `interfaces` property of the [Request Body Schema](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-create__request-body-schema) for details.
  * For more information, see our guide on [Getting Started with VLANs](/docs/products/networking/vlans/get-started/).

* Create an empty Linode.
  * The Linode will remain `offline` and must be manually started.
    * See Linode Boot ([POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/boot](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-boot)).
  * Disks and Configs must be created manually.
  * This is only recommended for advanced use cases.

**Important**: You must be an unrestricted User in order to add or modify
tags on Linodes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authorized_keys": [
    "ssh-rsa AAAA_valid_public_ssh_key_123456785== user@their-computer"
  ],
  "authorized_users": [
    "myUser",
    "secondaryUser"
  ],
  "booted": true,
  "image": "linode/debian9",
  "root_pass": "aComplexP@ssword",
  "stackscript_data": {
    "gh_username": "linode"
  },
  "stackscript_id": 10079,
  "backup_id": 1234,
  "backups_enabled": true,
  "group": "Linode-Group",
  "interfaces": [
    {
      "ipam_address": "10.0.0.1/24",
      "label": "example-interface",
      "purpose": "vlan"
    }
  ],
  "label": "linode123",
  "private_ip": true,
  "region": "us-east",
  "swap_size": 512,
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "type": "g6-standard-2"
}
```

<h3 id="linode-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|The requested initial state of a new Linode.|
|» authorized_keys|body|[string]|false|A list of public SSH keys that will be automatically appended<br>to the root user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|» authorized_users|body|[string]|false|A list of usernames. If the usernames have associated SSH keys, the keys will be appended to the root users `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file automatically when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|» booted|body|boolean|false|This field defaults to `true` if the Linode is created with an Image or from a Backup.<br>If it is deployed from an Image or a Backup and you wish it to remain `offline` after deployment, set this to `false`.<br>|
|» image|body|string|false|An Image ID to deploy the Linode Disk from.<br><br>Access the Images List ([GET /images](/docs/api/images/#images-list)) endpoint with authentication to view<br>all available Images. Official Linode Images start with `linode/`, while your Account's Images start with `private/`. Creating<br>a disk from a Private Image requires `read_only` or `read_write` permissions for that Image. Access the User's<br>Grant Update ([PUT /account/users/{username}/grants](/docs/api/account/#users-grants-update)) endpoint to<br>adjust permissions for an Account Image.<br>|
|» root_pass|body|string(password)|false|This sets the root user's password on a newly-created Linode Disk when deploying from an Image.<br><br>* **Required** when creating a Linode Disk from an Image, including when using a StackScript.<br><br>* Must meet a password strength score requirement that is calculated internally by the API.<br>If the strength requirement is not met, you will receive a `Password does not meet strength requirement` error.<br>|
|» stackscript_data|body|object|false|This field is required only if the StackScript being deployed requires input data from the User for successful completion. See [User Defined Fields (UDFs)](/docs/guides/writing-scripts-for-use-with-linode-stackscripts-a-tutorial/#user-defined-fields-udfs) for more details.<br><br>This field is required to be valid JSON.<br><br>Total length cannot exceed 65,535 characters.<br>|
|» stackscript_id|body|integer|false|A StackScript ID that will cause the referenced StackScript to be run during<br>deployment of this Linode. A compatible `image` is required to use a<br>StackScript. To get a list of available StackScript and their permitted Images<br>see [/stackscripts](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscripts-list).<br>This field cannot be used when deploying from a Backup or a Private Image.<br>|
|» backup_id|body|integer|false|A Backup ID from another Linode's available backups. Your User must have<br>`read_write` access to that Linode, the Backup must have a `status` of<br>`successful`, and the Linode must be deployed to the same `region` as the Backup.<br>See [GET /linode/instances/{linodeId}/backups](/docs/api/linode-instances/#backups-list)<br>for a Linode's available backups.<br><br>This field and the `image` field are mutually exclusive.<br>|
|» backups_enabled|body|boolean|false|If this field is set to `true`, the created Linode will automatically be<br>enrolled in the Linode Backup service. This will incur an additional charge.<br>The cost for the Backup service is dependent on the Type of Linode deployed.<br><br>This option is always treated as `true` if the account-wide `backups_enabled`<br>setting is `true`.  See [account settings](/docs/api/account/#account-settings-view)<br>for more information.<br><br>Backup pricing is included in the response from [/linodes/types](/docs/api/linode-types/#types-list)<br>|
|» group|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** A deprecated property denoting a group label for this Linode.<br>|
|» interfaces|body|[LinodeConfigInterfaces](#schemalinodeconfiginterfaces)|false|An array of Network Interfaces to add to this Linode's Configuration Profile.<br><br>Up to three interface objects can be entered in this array. The position in the array determines the interface to which the settings apply:<br><br>- First/0:  eth0<br>- Second/1: eth1<br>- Third/2:  eth2<br><br>When updating a Linode's interfaces, *each interface must be redefined*. An empty interfaces array results in a default public interface configuration only.<br><br>If no public interface is configured, public IP addresses are still assigned to the Linode but will not be usable without manual configuration.<br><br>**Note:** Changes to Linode interface configurations can be enabled by rebooting the Linode.<br><br>**Note:** Only Next Generation Network (NGN) data centers support VLANs. Use the Regions ([/regions](/docs/api/regions/)) endpoint to view the capabilities of data center regions.<br>If a VLAN is attached to your Linode and you attempt to migrate or clone it to a non-NGN data center,<br>the migration or cloning will not initiate. If a Linode cannot be migrated because of an incompatibility,<br>you will be prompted to select a different data center or contact support.<br><br>**Note:** See the [VLANs Overview](/docs/products/networking/vlans/#technical-specifications) guide to view additional specifications and limitations.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|The Linode's label is for display purposes only. If no label is provided for a Linode,<br>a default will be assigned.<br><br>Linode labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * Must begin and end with an alphanumeric character.<br>  * May only consist of alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`) or periods (`.`).<br>  * Cannot have two dashes (`--`), underscores (`__`) or periods (`..`) in a row.<br>|
|» private_ip|body|boolean|false|If true, the created Linode will have private networking enabled and assigned a private IPv4 address.<br>|
|» region|body|string|true|The [Region](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list) where the Linode will be located.<br>|
|» swap_size|body|integer|false|When deploying from an Image, this field is optional, otherwise it is ignored. This is used to set the swap disk size for the newly-created Linode.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to this object.  Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The [Linode Type](/docs/api/linode-types/#types-list) of the Linode you are creating.<br>|

## Linode Update

<a id="opIdupdateLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -X PUT \

    },
    "backups": {
      "schedule": {
        "day": "Saturday",
        "window": "W22"
      }
    },
    "group": "Linode-Group",
    "label": "linode123",
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ],
    "watchdog_enabled": true
  }'
```

`PUT /linode/instances/{linodeId}`

Updates a Linode that you have permission to `read_write`.

**Important**: You must be an unrestricted User in order to add or modify tags on Linodes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alerts": {
    "cpu": 180,
    "io": 10000,
    "network_in": 10,
    "network_out": 10,
    "transfer_quota": 80
  },
  "backups": {
    "schedule": {
      "day": "Saturday",
      "window": "W22"
    }
  },
  "group": "Linode-Group",
  "label": "linode123",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "watchdog_enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="linode-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to look up|
|body|body|[Linode](#schemalinode)|true|Any field that is not marked as `readOnly` may be updated. Fields that are marked `readOnly` will be ignored. If any updated field fails to pass validation, the Linode will not be updated.<br>|
|» alerts|body|object|false|none|
|» » cpu|body|integer|false|The percentage of CPU usage required to trigger an alert.<br>If the average CPU usage over two hours exceeds this value, we'll send you an alert.<br>Your Linode's total CPU capacity is represented as 100%, multiplied by its number of<br>cores.<br><br>For example, a two core Linode's CPU capacity is represented as 200%. If you want<br>to be alerted at 90% of a two core Linode's CPU capacity, set the alert value to `180`.<br><br>The default value is 90% multiplied by the number of cores.<br><br>If the value is set to `0` (zero), the alert is disabled.<br>|
|» » io|body|integer|false|The amount of disk IO operation per second required to trigger an alert. If the average disk IO over two hours exceeds this value, we'll send you an alert. If set to `0` (zero), this alert is disabled.<br>|
|» » network_in|body|integer|false|The amount of incoming traffic, in Mbit/s, required to trigger an alert. If the average incoming traffic over two hours exceeds this value, we'll send you an alert. If this is set to `0` (zero), the alert is disabled.<br>|
|» » network_out|body|integer|false|The amount of outbound traffic, in Mbit/s, required to trigger an alert. If the average outbound traffic over two hours exceeds this value, we'll send you an alert. If this is set to `0` (zero), the alert is disabled.<br>|
|» » transfer_quota|body|integer|false|The percentage of network transfer that may be used before an alert is triggered. When this value is exceeded, we'll alert you. If this is set to `0` (zero), the alert is disabled.<br>|
|» backups|body|object|false|Information about this Linode's backups status. For information about available backups, see [/linode/instances/{linodeId}/backups](/docs/api/linode-instances/#backups-list).<br>|
|» » schedule|body|object|false|none|
|» » » day|body|string \| null|false|The day of the week that your Linode's weekly Backup is taken.<br>If not set manually, a day will be chosen for you. Backups<br>are taken every day, but backups taken on this day are<br>preferred when selecting backups to retain for a longer period.<br><br><br>If not set manually, then when backups are initially enabled, this<br>may come back as `Scheduling` until the `day` is automatically selected.<br>|
|» » » window|body|string \| null|false|The window in which your backups will be taken, in UTC. A<br>backups window is a two-hour span of time in which the backup<br>may occur.<br><br><br>For example, `W10` indicates that your backups should be<br>taken between 10:00 and 12:00. If you do not choose a backup<br>window, one will be selected for you automatically.<br><br><br>If not set manually, when backups are initially enabled this<br>may come back as `Scheduling` until the `window` is automatically selected.<br>|
|» group|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** A deprecated property denoting a group label for this Linode.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|The Linode's label is for display purposes only. If no label is provided for a Linode,<br>a default will be assigned.<br><br>Linode labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * Must begin and end with an alphanumeric character.<br>  * May only consist of alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`) or periods (`.`).<br>  * Cannot have two dashes (`--`), underscores (`__`) or periods (`..`) in a row.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to this object.  Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|» watchdog_enabled|body|boolean|false|The watchdog, named Lassie, is a Shutdown Watchdog that monitors your Linode and will reboot it if it powers off unexpectedly. It works by issuing a boot job when your Linode powers off without a shutdown job being responsible.<br>To prevent a loop, Lassie will give up if there have been more than 5 boot jobs issued within 15 minutes.<br>|

## Linode Delete

<a id="opIddeleteLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /linode/instances/{linodeId}`

Deletes a Linode you have permission to `read_write`.

**Deleting a Linode is a destructive action and cannot be undone.**

Additionally, deleting a Linode:

  * Gives up any IP addresses the Linode was assigned.
  * Deletes all Disks, Backups, Configs, etc.
  * Stops billing for the Linode and its associated services. You will be billed for time used
    within the billing period the Linode was active.

Linodes that are in the process of [cloning](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-clone) or [backup restoration](/docs/api/linode-instances/#backup-restore) cannot be deleted.


<h3 id="linode-delete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to look up|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Delete successful|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "config_id": null
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/boot`

Boots a Linode you have permission to modify. If no parameters are given, a Config profile
will be chosen for this boot based on the following criteria:

* If there is only one Config profile for this Linode, it will be used.
* If there is more than one Config profile, the last booted config will be used.
* If there is more than one Config profile and none were the last to be booted (because the
  Linode was never booted or the last booted config was deleted) an error will be returned.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config_id": null
}
```

<h3 id="linode-boot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Linode to boot.|
|body|body|object|false|Optional configuration to boot into (see above).|
|» config_id|body|integer|false|The Linode Config ID to boot into.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="linode-boot-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Boot started.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="linode-boot-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

## Linode Clone

<a id="opIdcloneLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0/clone \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "backups_enabled": true,
    "configs": [
      23456
    ],
    "disks": [
      25674
    ],
    "group": "Linode-Group",
    "label": "cloned-linode",
    "linode_id": 124,
    "private_ip": true,
    "region": "us-east",
    "type": "g6-standard-2"
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/clone`

You can clone your Linode's existing Disks or Configuration profiles to
another Linode on your Account. In order for this request to complete
successfully, your User must have the `add_linodes` grant. Cloning to a
new Linode will incur a charge on your Account.

If cloning to an existing Linode, any actions currently running or
queued must be completed first before you can clone to it.

Up to five clone operations from any given source Linode can be run concurrently.
If more concurrent clones are attempted, an HTTP 400 error will be
returned by this endpoint.

Any [tags](/docs/api/tags/#tags-list) existing on the source Linode will be cloned to the target Linode.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "backups_enabled": true,
  "configs": [
    23456
  ],
  "disks": [
    25674
  ],
  "group": "Linode-Group",
  "label": "cloned-linode",
  "linode_id": 124,
  "private_ip": true,
  "region": "us-east",
  "type": "g6-standard-2"
}
```

<h3 id="linode-clone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to clone.|
|body|body|object|true|The requested state your Linode will be cloned into.|
|» backups_enabled|body|boolean|false|If this field is set to `true`, the created Linode will<br>automatically be enrolled in the Linode Backup service. This<br>will incur an additional charge. Pricing is included in the<br>response from<br>[/linodes/types](/docs/api/linode-types/#types-list).<br><br>* Can only be included when cloning to a new Linode.<br>|
|» configs|body|[integer]|false|An array of configuration profile IDs.<br>* If the `configs` parameter **is not provided**, then **all configuration profiles and their associated disks will be cloned** from the source Linode. Any disks specified by the `disks` parameter will also be cloned.<br>* **If an empty array is provided** for the `configs` parameter, then **no configuration profiles (nor their associated disks) will be cloned** from the source Linode. Any disks specified by the `disks` parameter will still be cloned.<br>* **If a non-empty array is provided** for the `configs` parameter, then **the configuration profiles specified in the array (and their associated disks) will be cloned** from the source Linode. Any disks specified by the `disks` parameter will also be cloned.<br>|
|» disks|body|[integer]|false|An array of disk IDs.<br>* If the `disks` parameter **is not provided**, then **no extra disks will be cloned** from the source Linode. All disks associated with the configuration profiles specified by the `configs` parameter will still be cloned.<br>* **If an empty array is provided** for the `disks` parameter, then **no extra disks will be cloned** from the source Linode. All disks associated with the configuration profiles specified by the `configs` parameter will still be cloned.<br>* **If a non-empty array is provided** for the `disks` parameter, then **the disks specified in the array will be cloned** from the source Linode, in addition to any disks associated with the configuration profiles specified by the `configs` parameter.<br>|
|» group|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** A label used to group Linodes for display. Linodes are not required to have a group.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|The label to assign this Linode when cloning to a new Linode.<br>* Can only be provided when cloning to a new Linode.<br>* Defaults to "linode".<br>|
|» linode_id|body|integer|false|If an existing Linode is the target for the clone, the ID of that Linode. The existing Linode must have enough resources to accept the clone.<br>|
|» private_ip|body|boolean|false|If true, the created Linode will have private networking enabled and assigned a private IPv4 address.<br>* Can only be provided when cloning to a new Linode.<br>|
|» region|body|string|false|This is the Region where the Linode will be deployed.<br>To view all available Regions you can deploy to see [/regions](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list).<br>* Region can only be provided and is required when cloning to a new Linode.<br>|
|» type|body|string|false|A Linode's Type determines what resources are available to<br>it, including disk space, memory, and virtual cpus. The<br>amounts available to a specific Linode are returned as<br>`specs` on the Linode object.<br><br>To view all available Linode Types you can deploy with<br>see [/linode/types](/docs/api/linode-types/#types-list).<br><br>* Type can only be provided and is required when cloning to a new Linode.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "alerts": {
    "cpu": 180,
    "io": 10000,
    "network_in": 10,
    "network_out": 10,
    "transfer_quota": 80
  },
  "backups": {
    "available": true,

    "203.0.113.1",
    "192.0.2.1"
  ],
```

<h3 id="configuration-profile-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to look up Configuration profiles for.|
|body|body|object|true|The parameters to set when creating the Configuration profile.<br>This determines which kernel, devices, how much memory, etc. a Linode boots with.<br>|
|» comments|body|string \| null|false|Optional field for arbitrary User comments on this Config.|
|» devices|body|[Devices](#schemadevices)|true|A dictionary of device disks to use as a device map in a Linode's configuration profile.<br>* An empty device disk dictionary or a dictionary with empty values for device slots is allowed.<br>* If no devices are specified, booting from this configuration will hold until a device exists that allows the boot process to start.<br>|
|» helpers|body|object|false|Helpers enabled when booting to this Linode Config.|
|» » devtmpfs_automount|body|boolean|false|Populates the /dev directory early during boot without udev.  Defaults to false.<br>|
|» » distro|body|boolean|false|Helps maintain correct inittab/upstart console device.|
|» » modules_dep|body|boolean|false|Creates a modules dependency file for the Kernel you run.|
|» » network|body|boolean|false|Automatically configures static networking.|
|» » updatedb_disabled|body|boolean|false|Disables updatedb cron job to avoid disk thrashing.|
|» interfaces|body|[LinodeConfigInterfaces](#schemalinodeconfiginterfaces)|false|An array of Network Interfaces to add to this Linode's Configuration Profile.<br><br>Up to three interface objects can be entered in this array. The position in the array determines the interface to which the settings apply:<br><br>- First/0:  eth0<br>- Second/1: eth1<br>- Third/2:  eth2<br><br>When updating a Linode's interfaces, *each interface must be redefined*. An empty interfaces array results in a default public interface configuration only.<br><br>If no public interface is configured, public IP addresses are still assigned to the Linode but will not be usable without manual configuration.<br><br>**Note:** Changes to Linode interface configurations can be enabled by rebooting the Linode.<br><br>**Note:** Only Next Generation Network (NGN) data centers support VLANs. Use the Regions ([/regions](/docs/api/regions/)) endpoint to view the capabilities of data center regions.<br>If a VLAN is attached to your Linode and you attempt to migrate or clone it to a non-NGN data center,<br>the migration or cloning will not initiate. If a Linode cannot be migrated because of an incompatibility,<br>you will be prompted to select a different data center or contact support.<br><br>**Note:** See the [VLANs Overview](/docs/products/networking/vlans/#technical-specifications) guide to view additional specifications and limitations.<br>|
|» kernel|body|string|false|A Kernel ID to boot a Linode with. Defaults to "linode/latest-64bit".|
|» label|body|string|true|The Config's label is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» memory_limit|body|integer|false|Defaults to the total RAM of the Linode.<br>|
|» root_device|body|string|false|The root device to boot.<br>* If no value or an invalid value is provided, root device will default to `/dev/sda`.<br>* If the device specified at the root device location is not mounted, the Linode will not boot until a device is mounted.<br>|
|» run_level|body|string|false|Defines the state of your Linode after booting. Defaults to `default`.<br>|
|» virt_mode|body|string|false|Controls the virtualization mode. Defaults to `paravirt`.<br>* `paravirt` is suitable for most cases. Linodes running in paravirt mode<br>  share some qualities with the host, ultimately making it run faster since<br>  there is less transition between it and the host.<br>* `fullvirt` affords more customization, but is slower because 100% of the VM<br>  is virtualized.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» run_level|default|
|» run_level|single|
|» run_level|binbash|
|» virt_mode|paravirt|
|» virt_mode|fullvirt|

<h3 id="configuration-profile-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Linode whose Configuration profile to look up.|
|configId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Configuration profile to look up.|
|body|body|[LinodeConfig](#schemalinodeconfig)|true|The Configuration profile parameters to modify.|
|» comments|body|string \| null|false|Optional field for arbitrary User comments on this Config.|
|» devices|body|[Devices](#schemadevices)|false|A dictionary of device disks to use as a device map in a Linode's configuration profile.<br>* An empty device disk dictionary or a dictionary with empty values for device slots is allowed.<br>* If no devices are specified, booting from this configuration will hold until a device exists that allows the boot process to start.<br>|
|» helpers|body|object|false|Helpers enabled when booting to this Linode Config.|
|» » devtmpfs_automount|body|boolean|false|Populates the /dev directory early during boot without udev.  Defaults to false.<br>|
|» » distro|body|boolean|false|Helps maintain correct inittab/upstart console device.|
|» » modules_dep|body|boolean|false|Creates a modules dependency file for the Kernel you run.|
|» » network|body|boolean|false|Automatically configures static networking.|
|» » updatedb_disabled|body|boolean|false|Disables updatedb cron job to avoid disk thrashing.|
|» interfaces|body|[LinodeConfigInterfaces](#schemalinodeconfiginterfaces)|false|An array of Network Interfaces to add to this Linode's Configuration Profile.<br><br>Up to three interface objects can be entered in this array. The position in the array determines the interface to which the settings apply:<br><br>- First/0:  eth0<br>- Second/1: eth1<br>- Third/2:  eth2<br><br>When updating a Linode's interfaces, *each interface must be redefined*. An empty interfaces array results in a default public interface configuration only.<br><br>If no public interface is configured, public IP addresses are still assigned to the Linode but will not be usable without manual configuration.<br><br>**Note:** Changes to Linode interface configurations can be enabled by rebooting the Linode.<br><br>**Note:** Only Next Generation Network (NGN) data centers support VLANs. Use the Regions ([/regions](/docs/api/regions/)) endpoint to view the capabilities of data center regions.<br>If a VLAN is attached to your Linode and you attempt to migrate or clone it to a non-NGN data center,<br>the migration or cloning will not initiate. If a Linode cannot be migrated because of an incompatibility,<br>you will be prompted to select a different data center or contact support.<br><br>**Note:** See the [VLANs Overview](/docs/products/networking/vlans/#technical-specifications) guide to view additional specifications and limitations.<br>|
|» kernel|body|string|false|A Kernel ID to boot a Linode with. Defaults to "linode/latest-64bit".|
|» label|body|string|false|The Config's label is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» memory_limit|body|integer|false|Defaults to the total RAM of the Linode.<br>|
|» root_device|body|string|false|The root device to boot.<br>* If no value or an invalid value is provided, root device will default to `/dev/sda`.<br>* If the device specified at the root device location is not mounted, the Linode will not boot until a device is mounted.<br>|
|» run_level|body|string|false|Defines the state of your Linode after booting. Defaults to `default`.<br>|
|» virt_mode|body|string|false|Controls the virtualization mode. Defaults to `paravirt`.<br>* `paravirt` is suitable for most cases. Linodes running in paravirt mode<br>  share some qualities with the host, ultimately making it run faster since<br>  there is less transition between it and the host.<br>* `fullvirt` affords more customization, but is slower because 100% of the VM<br>  is virtualized.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|» run_level|single|
|» run_level|binbash|
|» virt_mode|paravirt|
|» virt_mode|fullvirt|

## Disk Create

<a id="opIdaddLinodeDisk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0/disks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "authorized_keys": [
      "ssh-rsa AAAA_valid_public_ssh_key_123456785== user@their-computer"
    ],
    "authorized_users": [
      "myUser",
      "secondaryUser"
    ],
    "filesystem": "ext4",
    "image": "linode/debian9",
    "label": "Debian 9 Disk",
    "root_pass": "aComplexP@ssword",
    "size": 48640,
    "stackscript_data": {
      "gh_username": "linode"
    },
    "stackscript_id": 10079
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/disks`

Adds a new Disk to a Linode.

* You can optionally create a Disk from an Image or an Empty Disk if no Image is provided with a request.

* When creating an Empty Disk, providing a `label` is required.

* If no `label` is provided, an `image` is required instead.

* When creating a Disk from an Image, `root_pass` is required.

* The default filesystem for new Disks is `ext4`. If creating a Disk from an Image, the filesystem
of the Image is used unless otherwise specified.

* When deploying a StackScript on a Disk:
  * See StackScripts List ([GET /linode/stackscripts](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscripts-list)) for
    a list of available StackScripts.
  * Requires a compatible Image to be supplied.
    * See StackScript View ([GET /linode/stackscript/{stackscriptId}](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscript-view)) for compatible Images.
  * It is recommended to supply SSH keys for the root User using the `authorized_keys` field.
  * You may also supply a list of usernames via the `authorized_users` field.
    * These users must have an SSH Key associated with their Profiles first. See SSH Key Add ([POST /profile/sshkeys](/docs/api/profile/#ssh-key-add)) for more information.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authorized_keys": [
    "ssh-rsa AAAA_valid_public_ssh_key_123456785== user@their-computer"
  ],
  "authorized_users": [
    "myUser",
    "secondaryUser"
  ],
  "filesystem": "ext4",
  "image": "linode/debian9",
  "label": "Debian 9 Disk",
  "root_pass": "aComplexP@ssword",
  "size": 48640,
  "stackscript_data": {
    "gh_username": "linode"
  },
  "stackscript_id": 10079
}
```

<h3 id="disk-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to look up.|
|body|body|object|true|The parameters to set when creating the Disk.<br>|
|» authorized_keys|body|[string]|false|A list of public SSH keys that will be automatically appended<br>to the root user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|» authorized_users|body|[string]|false|A list of usernames. If the usernames have associated SSH keys, the keys will be appended to the root users `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file automatically when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|» filesystem|body|string|false|The Disk filesystem can be one of:<br><br>  * raw - No filesystem, just a raw binary stream.<br>  * swap - Linux swap area.<br>  * ext3 - The ext3 journaling filesystem for Linux.<br>  * ext4 - The ext4 journaling filesystem for Linux.<br>  * initrd - initrd (uncompressed initrd, ext2, max 32 MB).<br>|
|» image|body|string|false|An Image ID to deploy the Linode Disk from.<br><br>Access the Images List ([GET /images](/docs/api/images/#images-list)) endpoint with authentication to view<br>all available Images. Official Linode Images start with `linode/`, while your Account's Images start with `private/`. Creating<br>a disk from a Private Image requires `read_only` or `read_write` permissions for that Image. Access the User's<br>Grant Update ([PUT /account/users/{username}/grants](/docs/api/account/#users-grants-update)) endpoint to<br>adjust permissions for an Account Image.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|The Disk's label is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» root_pass|body|string(password)|false|This sets the root user's password on a newly-created Linode Disk when deploying from an Image.<br><br>* **Required** when creating a Linode Disk from an Image, including when using a StackScript.<br><br>* Must meet a password strength score requirement that is calculated internally by the API.<br>If the strength requirement is not met, you will receive a `Password does not meet strength requirement` error.<br>|
|» size|body|integer|true|The size of the Disk in MB.<br><br>Images require a minimum size. Access the Image View ([GET /images/{imageID}](/docs/api/images/#image-view)) endpoint to view its size.<br>|
|» stackscript_data|body|object|false|This field is required only if the StackScript being deployed requires input data from the User for successful completion. See [User Defined Fields (UDFs)](/docs/guides/writing-scripts-for-use-with-linode-stackscripts-a-tutorial/#user-defined-fields-udfs) for more details.<br><br>This field is required to be valid JSON.<br><br>Total length cannot exceed 65,535 characters.<br>|
|» stackscript_id|body|integer|false|A StackScript ID that will cause the referenced StackScript to be run during<br>deployment of this Linode. A compatible `image` is required to use a<br>StackScript. To get a list of available StackScript and their permitted Images<br>see [/stackscripts](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscripts-list).<br>This field cannot be used when deploying from a Backup or a Private Image.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» filesystem|raw|
|» filesystem|swap|
|» filesystem|ext3|
|» filesystem|ext4|
|» filesystem|initrd|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "filesystem": "ext4",
  "id": 25674,
  "label": "Debian 9 Disk",
  "size": 48640,
  "status": "ready",
  "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|default|Default|Error|Inline|

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/disks/{diskId}/clone`

Copies a disk, byte-for-byte, into a new Disk belonging to the same Linode. The Linode must have enough storage space available to accept a new Disk of the same size as this one or this operation will fail.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to look up.|
|diskId|path|integer|true|ID of the Disk to clone.|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "filesystem": "ext4",
  "id": 25674,
  "label": "Debian 9 Disk",
  "size": 48640,
  "status": "ready",
  "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Disk Resize

<a id="opIdresizeDisk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0/disks/0/resize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "size": 2048
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/disks/{diskId}/resize`

Resizes a Disk you have permission to `read_write`.

The Disk must not be in use. If the Disk is in use, the request will
succeed but the resize will ultimately fail. For a request to succeed,
the Linode must be shut down prior to resizing the Disk, or the Disk
must not be assigned to the Linode's active Configuration Profile.

If you are resizing the Disk to a smaller size, it cannot be made smaller
than what is required by the total size of the files current on the Disk.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "size": 2048
}
```

<h3 id="disk-resize-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to look up.|
|diskId|path|integer|true|ID of the Disk to look up.|
|body|body|object|true|The new size of the Disk.|
|» size|body|integer|true|The desired size, in MB, of the disk.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="disk-resize-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Resize started.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|
