## DC Migration/Pending Host Migration Initiate

<a id="opIdmigrateLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0/migrate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "region": "us-east",
    "upgrade": false
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/migrate`

Initiate a pending host migration that has been scheduled by Linode or initiate a cross data center (DC) migration.  A list of pending migrations, if any, can be accessed from [GET /account/notifications](/docs/api/account/#notifications-list). When the migration begins, your Linode will be shutdown if not already off. If the migration initiated the shutdown, it will reboot the Linode when completed.

To initiate a cross DC migration, you must pass a `region` parameter to the request body specifying the target data center region. You can view a list of all available regions and their feature capabilities from [GET /regions](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list). If your Linode has a DC migration already queued or you have initiated a previously scheduled migration, you will not be able to initiate a DC migration until it has completed.

**Note:** Next Generation Network (NGN) data centers do not support IPv6 `/116` pools or IP Failover. If you have these features enabled on your Linode and attempt to migrate to an NGN data center, the migration will not initiate. If a Linode cannot be migrated because of an incompatibility, you will be prompted to select a different data center or contact support.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "region": "us-east",
  "upgrade": false
}
```

<h3 id="dc-migrationpending-host-migration-initiate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to migrate.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» region|body|string|false|The region to which the Linode will be migrated. Must be a valid region slug. A list of regions can be viewed by using the [GET /regions](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list) endpoint. A cross data center migration will cancel a pending migration that has not yet been initiated.<br>A cross data center migration will initiate a `linode_migrate_datacenter_create` event.<br>|
|» upgrade|body|boolean|false|When initiating a cross DC migration, setting this value to true will also ensure that the Linode is upgraded to the latest generation of hardware that corresponds to your Linode's Type, if any free upgrades are available for it.<br>If no free upgrades are available, and this value is set to true, then the endpoint will return a 400 error code and the migration will not be performed.<br>If the data center set in the `region` field does not allow upgrades, then the endpoint will return a 400 error code and the migration will not be performed.<br>|

## Linode Upgrade

<a id="opIdmutateLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0/mutate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_auto_disk_resize": true
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/mutate`

Linodes created with now-deprecated Types are entitled to a free upgrade to the next generation. A mutating Linode will be allocated any new resources the upgraded Type provides, and will be subsequently restarted if it was currently running.
If any actions are currently running or queued, those actions must be completed first before you can initiate a mutate.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_auto_disk_resize": true
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to mutate.|
|body|body|object|false|Whether to automatically resize disks or not.|
|» allow_auto_disk_resize|body|boolean|false|Automatically resize disks when resizing a Linode. When resizing down to a smaller plan your Linode's data must fit within the smaller disk size.<br>|

```json
{}
```

<a id="opIdresetLinodePassword"></a>

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/password`

Resets the root password for this Linode.
* Your Linode must be [shut down](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-shut-down) for a password reset to complete.
* If your Linode has more than one disk (not counting its swap disk), use the [Reset Disk Root Password](/docs/api/linode-instances/#disk-root-password-reset) endpoint to update a specific disk's root password.
* A `password_reset` event is generated when a root password reset is successful.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "root_pass": "a$eCure4assw0rd!43v51"
}
```

|body|body|object|false|This Linode's new root password.|
|» root_pass|body|string|true|The root user's password on this Linode. Linode passwords must meet a password strength score requirement that is calculated internally by the API. If the strength requirement is not met, you will receive a Password does not meet strength requirement error.<br>|

## Linode Rebuild

<a id="opIdrebuildLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0/rebuild \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "authorized_keys": [
      "ssh-rsa AAAA_valid_public_ssh_key_123456785== user@their-computer"
    ],
    "authorized_users": [
      "myUser",
      "secondaryUser"
    ],
    "booted": true,
    "image": "linode/debian9",
    "root_pass": "aComplexP@ssword",
    "stackscript_data": {
      "gh_username": "linode"
    },
    "stackscript_id": 10079
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/rebuild`

Rebuilds a Linode you have the `read_write` permission to modify.
A rebuild will first shut down the Linode, delete all disks and configs on the Linode, and then deploy a new `image` to the Linode with the given attributes. Additionally:

  * Requires an `image` be supplied.
  * Requires a `root_pass` be supplied to use for the root User's Account.
  * It is recommended to supply SSH keys for the root User using the
    `authorized_keys` field.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authorized_keys": [
    "ssh-rsa AAAA_valid_public_ssh_key_123456785== user@their-computer"
  ],
  "authorized_users": [
    "myUser",
    "secondaryUser"
  ],
  "booted": true,
  "image": "linode/debian9",
  "root_pass": "aComplexP@ssword",
  "stackscript_data": {
    "gh_username": "linode"
  },
  "stackscript_id": 10079
}
```

<h3 id="linode-rebuild-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to rebuild.|
|body|body|object|true|The requested state your Linode will be rebuilt into.|
|» authorized_keys|body|[string]|false|A list of public SSH keys that will be automatically appended<br>to the root user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|» authorized_users|body|[string]|false|A list of usernames. If the usernames have associated SSH keys, the keys will be appended to the root users `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file automatically when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|» booted|body|boolean|false|This field defaults to `true` if the Linode is created with an Image or from a Backup.<br>If it is deployed from an Image or a Backup and you wish it to remain `offline` after deployment, set this to `false`.<br>|
|» image|body|string|true|An Image ID to deploy the Linode Disk from.<br><br>Access the Images List ([GET /images](/docs/api/images/#images-list)) endpoint with authentication to view<br>all available Images. Official Linode Images start with `linode/`, while your Account's Images start with `private/`. Creating<br>a disk from a Private Image requires `read_only` or `read_write` permissions for that Image. Access the User's<br>Grant Update ([PUT /account/users/{username}/grants](/docs/api/account/#users-grants-update)) endpoint to<br>adjust permissions for an Account Image.<br>|
|» root_pass|body|string(password)|true|This sets the root user's password on a newly-created Linode Disk when deploying from an Image.<br><br>* **Required** when creating a Linode Disk from an Image, including when using a StackScript.<br><br>* Must meet a password strength score requirement that is calculated internally by the API.<br>If the strength requirement is not met, you will receive a `Password does not meet strength requirement` error.<br>|
|» stackscript_data|body|object|false|This field is required only if the StackScript being deployed requires input data from the User for successful completion. See [User Defined Fields (UDFs)](/docs/guides/writing-scripts-for-use-with-linode-stackscripts-a-tutorial/#user-defined-fields-udfs) for more details.<br><br>This field is required to be valid JSON.<br><br>Total length cannot exceed 65,535 characters.<br>|
|» stackscript_id|body|integer|false|A StackScript ID that will cause the referenced StackScript to be run during<br>deployment of this Linode. A compatible `image` is required to use a<br>StackScript. To get a list of available StackScript and their permitted Images<br>see [/stackscripts](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscripts-list).<br>This field cannot be used when deploying from a Backup or a Private Image.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "alerts": {
    "cpu": 180,
    "io": 10000,
    "network_in": 10,
    "network_out": 10,
    "transfer_quota": 80
  },
  "backups": {
    "available": true,
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/rescue`

Rescue Mode is a safe environment for performing many system recovery and disk management tasks. Rescue Mode is based on the Finnix recovery distribution, a self-contained and bootable Linux distribution. You can also use Rescue Mode for tasks other than disaster recovery, such as formatting disks to use different filesystems, copying data between disks, and downloading files from a disk via SSH and SFTP.
* Note that "sdh" is reserved and unavailable during rescue.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "devices": {
    "sda": {
      "disk_id": 124458,
      "volume_id": null
    },
    "sdb": {
      "disk_id": 124458,
      "volume_id": null
    },
    "sdc": {
      "disk_id": 124458,
      "volume_id": null
    },
    "sdd": {

      "volume_id": null
    },

      "volume_id": null
    },
    "sdf": {
      "disk_id": 124458,
      "volume_id": null
    },
    "sdg": {
      "disk_id": 124458,
      "volume_id": null
    }
  }
}
```

|body|body|object|false|Optional object of devices to be mounted.|

## Linode Resize

<a id="opIdresizeLinodeInstance"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/instances/0/resize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "allow_auto_disk_resize": true,
    "type": "g6-standard-2"
  }'
```

`POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/resize`

Resizes a Linode you have the `read_write` permission to a different Type. If any actions are currently running or queued, those actions must be completed first before you can initiate a resize. Additionally, the following criteria must be met in order to resize a Linode:

  * The Linode must not have a pending migration.
  * Your Account cannot have an outstanding balance.
  * The Linode must not have more disk allocation than the new Type allows.
    * In that situation, you must first delete or resize the disk to be smaller.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_auto_disk_resize": true,
  "type": "g6-standard-2"
}
```

<h3 id="linode-resize-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Linode to resize.|
|body|body|object|true|The Type your current Linode will resize to, and whether to attempt to automatically resize the Linode's disks.<br>|
|» allow_auto_disk_resize|body|boolean|false|Automatically resize disks when resizing a Linode. When resizing down to a smaller plan your Linode's data must fit within the smaller disk size.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The ID representing the Linode Type.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
      "field": "fieldname",

}
```

## Kubernetes Cluster Create

<a id="opIdcreateLKECluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "control_plane": {
      "high_availability": true
    },
    "k8s_version": "1.25",
    "label": "lkecluster12345",
    "node_pools": [
      {
        "autoscaler": {
          "enabled": true,
          "max": 12,
          "min": 3
        },
        "count": 6,
        "disks": [
          {
            "size": 1024,
            "type": "ext-4"
          }
        ],
        "tags": [
          "example tag",
          "another example"
        ],
        "type": "g6-standard-4"
      }
    ],
    "region": "us-central",
    "tags": [
      "ecomm",
      "blogs"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /lke/clusters`

Creates a Kubernetes cluster. The Kubernetes cluster will be created
asynchronously. You can use the events system to determine when the
Kubernetes cluster is ready to use. Please note that it often takes 2-5 minutes before the
[Kubernetes API server endpoint](/docs/api/linode-kubernetes-engine-lke/#kubernetes-api-endpoints-list) and
the [Kubeconfig file](/docs/api/linode-kubernetes-engine-lke/#kubeconfig-view) for the new cluster
are ready.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "control_plane": {
    "high_availability": true
  },
  "k8s_version": "1.25",
  "label": "lkecluster12345",
  "node_pools": [
    {
      "autoscaler": {
        "enabled": true,
        "max": 12,
        "min": 3
      },
      "count": 6,
      "disks": [
        {
          "size": 1024,
          "type": "ext-4"
        }
      ],
      "tags": [
        "example tag",
        "another example"
      ],
      "type": "g6-standard-4"
    }
  ],
  "region": "us-central",
  "tags": [
    "ecomm",
    "blogs"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Configuration for the Kubernetes cluster|
|» control_plane|body|object|false|Defines settings for the Kubernetes Control Plane. Allows for the enabling of High Availability (HA) for Control Plane Components. Enabling High Availability for LKE is an **irreversible** change.<br>|
|» » high_availability|body|boolean|false|Defines whether High Availability is enabled for the Control Plane Components of the cluster. Defaults to `false`.<br>|
|» k8s_version|body|string|true|The desired Kubernetes version for this Kubernetes cluster in the format of &lt;major&gt;.&lt;minor&gt;, and the latest supported patch version will be deployed.<br>|
|» label|body|string|true|This Kubernetes cluster's unique label for display purposes only.<br>Labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * UTF-8 characters will be returned by the API using escape<br>    sequences of their Unicode code points. For example, the<br>    Japanese character *か* is 3 bytes in UTF-8 (`0xE382AB`). Its<br>    Unicode code point is 2 bytes (`0x30AB`). APIv4 supports this<br>    character and the API will return it as the escape sequence<br>    using six 1 byte characters which represent 2 bytes of Unicode<br>    code point (`"\u30ab"`).<br>  * 4 byte UTF-8 characters are not supported.<br>  * If the label is entirely composed of UTF-8 characters, the API<br>    response will return the code points using up to 193 1 byte<br>    characters.<br>|
|» node_pools|body|[[LKENodePoolRequestBody](#schemalkenodepoolrequestbody)]|true|none|
|» region|body|string|true|This Kubernetes cluster's location.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to the Kubernetes cluster. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "control_plane": {
    "high_availability": true
  },
  "created": "2019-09-12T21:25:30Z",
  "id": 1234,
  "k8s_version": "1.25",
  "label": "lkecluster12345",
  "region": "us-central",
  "tags": [
    "ecomm",
    "blogs"
  ],
  "updated": "2019-09-13T21:24:16Z"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Kubernetes Cluster Update

<a id="opIdputLKECluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "control_plane": {
      "high_availability": true
    },
    "k8s_version": "string",
    "label": "lkecluster12345",
    "tags": [
      "prod",
      "monitoring",
      "ecomm",
      "blog"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /lke/clusters/{clusterId}`

Updates a Kubernetes cluster.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "control_plane": {
    "high_availability": true
  },
  "k8s_version": "string",
  "label": "lkecluster12345",
  "tags": [
    "prod",
    "monitoring",
    "ecomm",
    "blog"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster to look up.|
|body|body|object|false|The fields to update the Kubernetes cluster.|
|» control_plane|body|object|false|Defines settings for the Kubernetes Control Plane. Allows for the enabling of High Availability (HA) for Control Plane Components.<br><br>Enabling High Availability for LKE is an **irreversible** change.<br><br>When upgrading pre-existing LKE clusters to use the HA Control Plane, the following changes will additionally occur:<br><br>- All nodes will be deleted and new nodes will be created to replace them.<br><br>- Any local storage (such as `hostPath` volumes) will be erased.<br><br>- The upgrade process may take several minutes to complete, as nodes will be replaced on a rolling basis.<br>|
|» » high_availability|body|boolean|false|Defines whether High Availability is enabled for the Control Plane Components of the cluster. Defaults to `false`.<br>|
|» k8s_version|body|string|false|The desired Kubernetes version for this Kubernetes cluster in the format of &lt;major&gt;.&lt;minor&gt;. New and recycled Nodes in this cluster will be installed with the latest available patch for the Cluster's Kubernetes version.<br><br>When upgrading the Kubernetes version, only the next latest minor version following the current version can be deployed. For example, a cluster with Kubernetes version 1.19 can be upgraded to version 1.20, but not directly to 1.21.<br><br>The Kubernetes version of a cluster can not be downgraded.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|This Kubernetes cluster's unique label for display purposes only.<br>Labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * UTF-8 characters will be returned by the API using escape<br>    sequences of their Unicode code points. For example, the<br>    Japanese character *か* is 3 bytes in UTF-8 (`0xE382AB`). Its<br>    Unicode code point is 2 bytes (`0x30AB`). APIv4 supports this<br>    character and the API will return it as the escape sequence<br>    using six 1 byte characters which represent 2 bytes of Unicode<br>    code point (`"\u30ab"`).<br>  * 4 byte UTF-8 characters are not supported.<br>  * If the label is entirely composed of UTF-8 characters, the API<br>    response will return the code points using up to 193 1 byte<br>    characters.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to the Kubernetes cluster. Tags are for organizational purposes only. To delete a tag, exclude it from your `tags` array.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2019-09-12T21:25:30Z",
  "k8s_version": "1.25",
  "label": "lkecluster12345",
  "region": "us-central",
  "tags": [
    "prod",
    "monitoring",
    "ecomm",
    "blog"
  ],
  "updated": "2019-09-13T21:24:16Z"
}
```

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-update-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Kubernetes cluster was created.|
|k8s_version|string|false|none|The desired Kubernetes version for this Kubernetes cluster in the format of &lt;major&gt;.&lt;minor&gt;, and the latest supported patch version will be deployed.<br>|
|label|string|false|none|This Kubernetes cluster's unique label for display purposes only.<br>Labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * UTF-8 characters will be returned by the API using escape<br>    sequences of their Unicode code points. For example, the<br>    Japanese character *か* is 3 bytes in UTF-8 (`0xE382AB`). Its<br>    Unicode code point is 2 bytes (`0x30AB`). APIv4 supports this<br>    character and the API will return it as the escape sequence<br>    using six 1 byte characters which represent 2 bytes of Unicode<br>    code point (`"\u30ab"`).<br>  * 4 byte UTF-8 characters are not supported.<br>  * If the label is entirely composed of UTF-8 characters, the API<br>    response will return the code points using up to 193 1 byte<br>    characters.<br>|
|region|string|false|none|This Kubernetes cluster's location.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags applied to the Kubernetes cluster. Tags are for organizational purposes only. To delete a tag, exclude it from your `tags` array.<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Kubernetes cluster was updated.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: lke:read_write )

## Kubernetes Cluster Delete

<a id="opIddeleteLKECluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /lke/clusters/{clusterId}`

Deletes a Cluster you have permission to `read_write`.

**Deleting a Cluster is a destructive action and cannot be undone.**

Deleting a Cluster:
  - Deletes all Linodes in all pools within this Kubernetes cluster
  - Deletes all supporting Kubernetes services for this Kubernetes
    cluster (API server, etcd, etc)
  - Deletes all NodeBalancers created by this Kubernetes cluster
  - Does not delete any of the volumes created by this Kubernetes
    cluster


<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-delete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster to look up.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-delete-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Delete successful|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-delete-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: lke:read_write )

## Kubernetes Cluster Dashboard URL View

<a id="opIdgetLKEClusterDashboard"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0/dashboard \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /lke/clusters/{clusterId}/dashboard`

Get a [Kubernetes Dashboard](https://github.com/kubernetes/dashboard) access URL for this Cluster, which enables performance of administrative tasks through a web interface.

Dashboards are installed for Clusters by default.

To access the Cluster Dashboard login prompt, enter the URL in a web browser. Select either **Token** or **Kubeconfig** authentication, then select **Sign in**.

For additional guidance on using the Cluster Dashboard, see the [Navigating the Cluster Dashboard](/docs/guides/using-the-kubernetes-dashboard-on-lke/#navigating-the-cluster-dashboard) section of our guide on [Using the Kubernetes Dashboard on LKE](/docs/guides/using-the-kubernetes-dashboard-on-lke/).

## Node Recycle

<a id="opIdpostLKEClusterNodeRecycle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0/nodes/string/recycle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /lke/clusters/{clusterId}/nodes/{nodeId}/recycle`

Recycles an individual Node in the designated Kubernetes Cluster. The Node will be deleted
and replaced with a new Linode, which may take a few minutes. Replacement Nodes are
installed with the latest available patch for the Cluster's Kubernetes Version.

**Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as "hostPath" and "emptyDir" volumes, or "local" PersistentVolumes) will be erased.**


<h3 id="node-recycle-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster containing the Node.|
|nodeId|path|string|true|ID of the Node to be recycled.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="node-recycle-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Recycle request succeeded and is in progress.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

## Node Pool Create

<a id="opIdpostLKEClusterPools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0/pools \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoscaler": {
      "enabled": true,
      "max": 12,
      "min": 3
    },
    "count": 6,
    "disks": [
      {
        "size": 1024,
        "type": "ext-4"
      }
    ],
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ],
    "type": "g6-standard-4"
  }'
```

`POST /lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools`

Creates a new Node Pool for the designated Kubernetes cluster.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoscaler": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max": 12,
    "min": 3
  },
  "count": 6,
  "disks": [
    {
      "size": 1024,
      "type": "ext-4"
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "type": "g6-standard-4"
}
```

<h3 id="node-pool-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster to look up.|
|body|body|object|true|Configuration for the Node Pool|
|» autoscaler|body|object|false|When enabled, the number of nodes autoscales within the defined minimum and maximum values.<br><br>When making a request, `max` and `min` require each other.<br>|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether autoscaling is enabled for this Node Pool. Defaults to `false`.|
|» » max|body|integer|false|The maximum number of nodes to autoscale to. Defaults to the Node Pool's `count`. Defaults to the value provided by the `count` field.<br>|
|» » min|body|integer|false|The minimum number of nodes to autoscale to. Defaults to the Node Pool's `count`.|
|» count|body|integer|true|The number of nodes in the Node Pool.|
|» disks|body|[object]|false|**Note**: This field should be omitted except for special use cases. The disks specified here are<br>partitions in *addition* to the primary partition and reduce the size of the primary partition,<br>which can lead to stability problems for the Node.<br><br>This Node Pool's custom disk layout. Each item in this array will create a new disk<br>partition for each node in this Node Pool.<br><br>  * The custom disk layout is applied to each node in this Node Pool.<br>  * The maximum number of custom disk partitions that can be configured is 7.<br>  * Once the requested disk paritions are allocated, the remaining disk space is allocated to the node's boot disk.<br>  * A Node Pool's custom disk layout is immutable over the lifetime of the Node Pool.<br>|
|» » size|body|integer|false|The size of this custom disk partition in MB.<br><br>  * The size of this disk partition must not exceed the capacity of the node's plan type.<br>|
|» » type|body|string|false|This custom disk partition's filesystem type.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to this object. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The Linode Type for all of the nodes in the Node Pool.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|raw|
|» » type|ext4|

```json
    "enabled": true,
    "max": 12,
    "min": 3
  },
  "count": 6,
  "disks": [
    {
      "size": 1024,

    }
  ],
  "id": 456,
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "123456",

      "status": "ready"
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],

}
```

```json
}
```

## Node Pool Update

<a id="opIdputLKENodePool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0/pools/0 \
  -X PUT \
```

`PUT /lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools/{poolId}`

Updates a Node Pool's count and autoscaler configuration.

Linodes will be created or deleted to match changes to the Node Pool's count.

**Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as "hostPath" and "emptyDir" volumes, or "local" PersistentVolumes) will be erased.**


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoscaler": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max": 12,
    "min": 3
  },
  "count": 6
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster to look up.|
|poolId|path|integer|true|ID of the Pool to look up|
|body|body|object|false|The fields to update|
|» autoscaler|body|object|false|When enabled, the number of nodes autoscales within the defined minimum and maximum values.<br><br>When making a request, `max` and `min` require each other.<br>|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether autoscaling is enabled for this Node Pool. Defaults to `false`.|
|» » max|body|integer|false|The maximum number of nodes to autoscale to. Defaults to the Node Pool's `count`. Defaults to the value provided by the `count` field.<br>|
|» » min|body|integer|false|The minimum number of nodes to autoscale to. Defaults to the Node Pool's `count`.|
|» count|body|integer|false|The number of nodes in the Node Pool.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "autoscaler": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max": 12,
    "min": 3
  },
  "count": 6,
  "disks": [
    {
      "size": 1024,
      "type": "ext-4"
    }
  ],
  "id": 456,
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "123456",
      "instance_id": 123458,
      "status": "ready"
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "type": "g6-standard-4"
}
```

## Node Pool Recycle

<a id="opIdpostLKEClusterPoolRecycle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0/pools/0/recycle \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /lke/clusters/{clusterId}/pools/{poolId}/recycle`

Recycles a Node Pool for the designated Kubernetes Cluster. All Linodes within the Node Pool will be deleted
and replaced with new Linodes on a rolling basis, which may take several minutes. Replacement Nodes are
installed with the latest available patch for the Cluster's Kubernetes Version.

**Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as "hostPath" and "emptyDir" volumes, or "local" PersistentVolumes) will be erased.**


<h3 id="node-pool-recycle-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the Kubernetes cluster this Node Pool is attached to.|
|poolId|path|integer|true|ID of the Node Pool to be recycled.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="node-pool-recycle-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Recycle request succeeded and is in progress.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="node-pool-recycle-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

`POST /lke/clusters/{clusterId}/recycle`

Recycles all nodes in all pools of a designated Kubernetes Cluster. All Linodes within the Cluster will be deleted
and replaced with new Linodes on a rolling basis, which may take several minutes. Replacement Nodes are
installed with the latest available [patch version](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/design-proposals/release/versioning.md#kubernetes-release-versioning) for the Cluster's current Kubernetes minor release.

**Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as "hostPath" and "emptyDir" volumes, or "local" PersistentVolumes) will be erased.**

## Kubernetes Cluster Regenerate

<a id="opIdpostLKEClusterRegenerate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/lke/clusters/0/regenerate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "kubeconfig": true,
    "servicetoken": true
  }'
```

`POST /lke/clusters/{clusterId}/regenerate`

Regenerate the Kubeconfig file and/or the service account token for a Cluster.

This is a helper command that allows performing both the [Kubeconfig Delete](#kubeconfig-delete) and the [Service Token Delete](#service-token-delete) actions with a single request.

When using this command, at least one of `kubeconfig` or `servicetoken` is required.

**Note**: When regenerating a service account token, the Cluster's control plane components and Linode CSI drivers are also restarted and configured with the new token. High Availability Clusters should not experience any disruption, while standard Clusters may experience brief control plane downtime while components are restarted.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "kubeconfig": true,
  "servicetoken": true
}
```

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-regenerate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|integer|true|ID of the target Kubernetes cluster.|
|body|body|object|false|The Kubernetes Cluster Regenerate request object.|
|» kubeconfig|body|boolean|false|Whether to delete and regenerate the Kubeconfig file for this Cluster.<br>|
|» servicetoken|body|boolean|false|Whether to delete and regenerate the service access token for this Cluster.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-regenerate-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Regenerate request successful.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="kubernetes-cluster-regenerate-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<h1 id="linode-api-longview">Longview</h1>

Longview is Linode's system-level monitoring and graphing service. Use the Longview endpoints to manage your Longview subscription and plan and to create and maintain Longview clients.

## Longview Clients List

<a id="opIdgetLongviewClients"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/longview/clients \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /longview/clients`

Returns a paginated list of Longview Clients you have access to. Longview Client is used to monitor stats on your Linode with the help of the Longview Client application.


<h3 id="longview-clients-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of a collection to return.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
```

## Longview Plan View

<a id="opIdgetLongviewPlan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/longview/plan \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /longview/plan`

Get the details of your current Longview plan. This returns a `LongviewSubscription` object for your current Longview Pro plan, or an empty set `{}` if your current plan is Longview Free.

You must have at least one of the following `global` [User Grants](/docs/api/account/#users-grants-view) in order to access this endpoint:

  - `"account_access": read_write`
  - `"account_access": read_only`
  - `"longview_subscription": true`
  - `"add_longview": true`


To update your subscription plan, send a request to [Update Longview Plan](/docs/api/longview/#longview-plan-update).


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "clients_included": 10,
  "id": "longview-10",
  "label": "Longview Pro 10 pack",
  "price": {
    "hourly": 0.06,
    "monthly": 40
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="longview-plan-view-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The Longview plan details for this account.|[LongviewSubscription](#schemalongviewsubscription)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="longview-plan-view-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: longview:read_only )
</aside>

## Longview Plan Update

<a id="opIdupdateLongviewPlan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/longview/plan \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "longview_subscription": "longview-10"
  }'
```

`PUT /longview/plan`

Update your Longview plan to that of the given subcription ID. This returns a `LongviewSubscription` object for the updated Longview Pro plan, or an empty set `{}` if the updated plan is Longview Free.

You must have `"longview_subscription": true` configured as a `global` [User Grant](/docs/api/account/#users-grants-view) in order to access this endpoint.

You can send a request to the [List Longview Subscriptions](/docs/api/longview/#longview-subscriptions-list) endpoint to receive the details, including `id`'s, of each plan.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "longview_subscription": "longview-10"
}
```

<h3 id="longview-plan-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[LongviewPlan](#schemalongviewplan)|true|Update your Longview subscription plan.|
|» longview_subscription|body|string \| null|false|The subscription ID for a particular Longview plan. A value of `null` corresponds to Longview Free.<br><br>You can send a request to the [List Longview Subscriptions](/docs/api/longview/#longview-subscriptions-list) endpoint to receive the details of each plan.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» longview_subscription|longview-3|
|» longview_subscription|longview-10|
|» longview_subscription|longview-40|
|» longview_subscription|longview-100|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "clients_included": 10,
  "id": "longview-10",
  "label": "Longview Pro 10 pack",
  "price": {
    "hourly": 0.06,
    "monthly": 40
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="longview-plan-update-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|default|Default|Error|Inline|

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

## Managed Contact Create

<a id="opIdcreateManagedContact"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/managed/contacts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "john.doe@example.org",
    "group": "on-call",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "phone": {
      "primary": "123-456-7890",
      "secondary": null
    }
  }'
```

`POST /managed/contacts`

Creates a Managed Contact.  A Managed Contact is someone Linode
special forces can contact in the course of attempting to resolve an issue
with a Managed Service.

This command can only be accessed by the unrestricted users of an account.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "john.doe@example.org",
  "group": "on-call",
  "name": "John Doe",
  "phone": {
    "primary": "123-456-7890",
    "secondary": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="managed-contact-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ManagedContact](#schemamanagedcontact)|false|Information about the contact to create.|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|The address to email this Contact to alert them of issues.<br>|
|» group|body|string \| null|false|A grouping for this Contact. This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of this Contact.<br>|
|» phone|body|object|false|Information about how to reach this Contact by phone.<br>|
|» » primary|body|string(phone) \| null|false|This Contact's primary phone number.<br>|
|» » secondary|body|string(phone) \| null|false|This Contact's secondary phone number.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "email": "john.doe@example.org",
  "group": "on-call",
  "id": 567,
  "name": "John Doe",
  "phone": {
    "primary": "123-456-7890",
    "secondary": null
  },
  "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="managed-contact-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Contact created.|[ManagedContact](#schemamanagedcontact)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» password|body|string|true|The password to use when accessing the Managed Service.<br>|
|» username|body|string|false|The username to use when accessing the Managed Service.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": 9991,
  "label": "prod-password-1",

}
```

`PUT /managed/linode-settings/{linodeId}`

Updates a single Linode's Managed settings.
This command can only be accessed by the unrestricted users of an account.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ssh": {
    "access": true,
    "ip": "203.0.113.1",
    "port": 22,
    "user": "linode"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="linodes-managed-settings-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|linodeId|path|integer|true|The Linode ID whose settings we are accessing.|
|body|body|[ManagedLinodeSettings](#schemamanagedlinodesettings)|true|The settings to update.|
|» ssh|body|object|false|The SSH settings for this Linode.<br>|
|» » access|body|boolean|false|If true, Linode special forces may access this Linode over ssh to respond to Issues.<br>|
|» » ip|body|string(ip)|false|The IP Linode special forces should use to access this Linode<br>when responding to an Issue.<br><br>By default, any of a Linode's IP addresses can be used for incident response access.<br>|
|» » port|body|integer \| null|false|The port Linode special forces should use to access this Linode<br>over ssh to respond to an Issue.<br><br>The default `null` value corresponds to port 22.<br>|
|» » user|body|string \| null|false|The specific user, if any, Linode's special forces should use when accessing this<br>Linode to respond to an issue.<br><br>The default `null` value corresponds to the root user.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "group": "linodes",
  "id": 123,
  "label": "linode123",
  "ssh": {
    "access": true,
    "ip": "203.0.113.1",
    "port": 22,
    "user": "linode"
  }
}
```

```json
  "errors": [
```

## Managed Service Create

<a id="opIdcreateManagedService"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/managed/services \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "https://example.org",
    "body": "it worked",
    "consultation_group": "on-call",
    "credentials": [
      9991
    ],
    "label": "prod-1",
    "notes": "The service name is my-cool-application",
    "region": null,
    "service_type": "url",
    "timeout": 30
  }'
```

`POST /managed/services`

Creates a Managed Service. Linode Managed will begin monitoring this
service and reporting and attempting to resolve any Issues.

This command can only be accessed by the unrestricted users of an account.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "https://example.org",
  "body": "it worked",
  "consultation_group": "on-call",
  "credentials": [
    9991
  ],
  "label": "prod-1",
  "notes": "The service name is my-cool-application",
  "region": null,
  "service_type": "url",
  "timeout": 30
}
```

<h3 id="managed-service-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Information about the service to monitor.|
|» address|body|string(url)|true|The URL at which this Service is monitored.<br><br>URL parameters such as `?no-cache=1` are preserved.<br><br>URL fragments/anchors such as `#monitor` are **not** preserved.<br>|
|» body|body|string \| null|false|What to expect to find in the response body for the Service to be considered up.<br>|
|» consultation_group|body|string|false|The group of ManagedContacts who should be notified or consulted with when an Issue is detected.<br>|
|» credentials|body|[integer]|false|An array of ManagedCredential IDs that should be used when attempting to resolve issues with this Service.<br>|
|» label|body|string|true|The label for this Service. This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» notes|body|string \| null|false|Any information relevant to the Service that Linode special forces should know when attempting to resolve Issues.<br>|
|» region|body|string|false|The Region in which this Service is located. This is required if address is a private IP, and may not be set otherwise.<br>|
|» service_type|body|string|true|How this Service is monitored.<br>|
|» timeout|body|integer|true|How long to wait, in seconds, for a response before considering the Service to be down.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» service_type|url|
|» service_type|tcp|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "https://example.org",
  "body": "it worked",
  "consultation_group": "on-call",
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "credentials": [
    9991
  ],
  "id": 9944,
  "label": "prod-1",
  "notes": "The service name is my-cool-application",
  "region": null,
  "service_type": "url",
  "status": "ok",
  "timeout": 30,
  "updated": "2018-03-01T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="managed-service-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Service created.|[ManagedService](#schemamanagedservice)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="managed-service-create-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: account:read_write )
</aside>

## Managed Stats List

<a id="opIdgetManagedStats"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/managed/stats \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /managed/stats`

Returns a list of Managed Stats on your Account in the form of x and y data points.
You can use these data points to plot your own graph visualizations. These stats
reflect the last 24 hours of combined usage across all managed Linodes on your account
giving you a high-level snapshot of data for the following:


* cpu
* disk
* swap
* network in
* network out

This command can only be accessed by the unrestricted users of an account.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cpu": [
      {
        "x": 11513761600000,
        "y": 29.94
      }
    ],
    "disk": [
      {
        "x": 11513761600000,
        "y": 29.94
      }
    ],
    "net_in": [
      {
        "x": 11513761600000,
        "y": 29.94
      }
    ],
    "net_out": [
      {
        "x": 11513761600000,
        "y": 29.94
      }
    ],
    "swap": [
      {
        "x": 11513761600000,
        "y": 29.94
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="managed-stats-list-responses">Responses</h3>

|200|OK|A list of Managed Stats from the last 24 hours.|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

<h1 id="linode-api-networking">Networking</h1>

Use the Networking endpoints to view all IP addresses on your account, reorganize assigned IPv4 addresses, update RDNS, and configure IP sharing.

## Firewalls List

## Firewall Create

<a id="opIdcreateFirewalls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/firewalls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "firewall123",
    "rules": {
      "inbound": null,
      "outbound": null
    },
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ],
    "devices": {
      "linodes": [
        123,
        456
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /networking/firewalls`

Creates a Firewall to filter network traffic.

* Use the `rules` property to create inbound and outbound access rules.

* Use the `devices` property to assign the Firewall to a service and apply its Rules to the device. Requires `read_write` [User's Grants](/docs/api/account/#users-grants-view) to the device.
Currently, Firewalls can only be assigned to Linode instances.

* A Firewall can be assigned to multiple Linode instances at a time.

* A Linode instance can have one active, assigned Firewall at a time.
Additional disabled Firewalls can be assigned to a service, but they cannot be enabled if another active Firewall is already assigned to the same service.

* A `firewall_create` Event is generated when this endpoint returns successfully.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "firewall123",
  "rules": {
    "inbound": null,
    "outbound": null
  },
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "devices": {
    "linodes": [
      123,
      456
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="firewall-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Creates a Firewall object that can be applied to a Linode service to filter the service's network traffic.|
|» label|body|string|true|The Firewall's label, for display purposes only.<br><br>Firewall labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * Must begin and end with an alphanumeric character.<br>  * May only consist of alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`) or periods (`.`).<br>  * Cannot have two dashes (`--`), underscores (`__`) or periods (`..`) in a row.<br>  * Must be between 3 and 32 characters.<br>  * Must be unique.<br>|
|» rules|body|object|true|The inbound and outbound access rules to apply to the Firewall.<br><br>A Firewall may have up to 25 rules across its inbound and outbound rulesets.<br>|
|» » inbound|body|[[FirewallRuleConfig](#schemafirewallruleconfig)]|false|The inbound rules for the firewall, as a JSON array.<br>|
|» » inbound_policy|body|string|false|The default behavior for inbound traffic. This setting can be overridden by [updating](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-rules-update) the `inbound.action` property of the Firewall Rule.<br>|
|» » outbound|body|[[FirewallRuleConfig](#schemafirewallruleconfig)]|false|The outbound rules for the firewall, as a JSON array.<br>|
|» » outbound_policy|body|string|false|The default behavior for outbound traffic. This setting can be overridden by [updating](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-rules-update) the `outbound.action` property of the Firewall Rule.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to this object. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|» devices|body|object|false|Devices to create for this Firewall.<br>When a Device is created, the Firewall is assigned to its associated service.<br>Currently, Devices can only be created for Linode instances.<br>|
|» » linodes|body|[integer]|false|An array of Linode IDs. A Firewall Device is created for each ID.<br>|
|» rules|body|object|true|none|
|» » inbound|body|object|false|none|
|» » outbound|body|object|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » inbound_policy|ACCEPT|
|» » inbound_policy|DROP|
|» » outbound_policy|ACCEPT|
|» » outbound_policy|DROP|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "id": 123,
  "label": "firewall123",
  "rules": {
    "inbound": [
      {
        "action": "ACCEPT",
        "addresses": {
          "ipv4": [
            "192.0.2.0/24"
          ],

          ]
        },
        "description": "An example firewall rule description.",

        "ports": "22-24, 80, 443",

      }

      {
        "action": "ACCEPT",
        "addresses": {
          "ipv4": [
            "192.0.2.0/24"
          ],
          "ipv6": [
            "2001:DB8::/32"
          ]
        },
        "description": "An example firewall rule description.",
        "label": "firewallrule123",
        "ports": "22-24, 80, 443",

  },
```

## Firewall Update

<a id="opIdupdateFirewall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/firewalls/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "firewall123",
    "status": "enabled",
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /networking/firewalls/{firewallId}`

Updates information for a Firewall. Some parts of a Firewall's configuration cannot
be manipulated by this endpoint:

- A Firewall's Devices cannot be set with this endpoint. Instead, use the
[Create Firewall Device](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-device-create)
and [Delete Firewall Device](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-device-delete)
endpoints to assign and remove this Firewall from Linode services.

- A Firewall's Rules cannot be changed with this endpoint. Instead, use the
[Update Firewall Rules](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-rules-update)
endpoint to update your Rules.

- A Firewall's status can be set to `enabled` or `disabled` by this endpoint, but it cannot be
set to `deleted`. Instead, use the
[Delete Firewall](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-delete)
endpoint to delete a Firewall.

If a Firewall's status is changed with this endpoint, a corresponding `firewall_enable` or
`firewall_disable` Event will be generated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "firewall123",
  "status": "enabled",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="firewall-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|firewallId|path|integer|true|ID of the Firewall to access.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|The Firewall information to update.|
|» label|body|string|false|The Firewall's label, for display purposes only.<br><br>Firewall labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * Must begin and end with an alphanumeric character.<br>  * May only consist of alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`) or periods (`.`).<br>  * Cannot have two dashes (`--`), underscores (`__`) or periods (`..`) in a row.<br>  * Must be between 3 and 32 characters.<br>  * Must be unique.<br>|
|» status|body|string|false|The status to be applied to this Firewall.<br> <br> * When a Firewall is first created its status is `enabled`.<br> * Use the [Delete Firewall](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-delete) endpoint to delete a Firewall.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to this object. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|enabled|
|» status|disabled|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "id": 123,
  "label": "firewall123",
  "rules": {
    "inbound": [
      {
        "action": "ACCEPT",
        "addresses": {
          "ipv4": [
            "192.0.2.0/24"
          ],
          "ipv6": [
            "2001:DB8::/32"
          ]
        },

        "label": "firewallrule123",
        "ports": "22-24, 80, 443",

      }
    ],
    "inbound_policy": "DROP",
    "outbound": [
      {
        "action": "ACCEPT",
        "addresses": {
          "ipv4": [
            "192.0.2.0/24"
          ],

          ]
```

<a id="opIddeleteFirewall"></a>

`DELETE /networking/firewalls/{firewallId}`

Delete a Firewall resource by its ID. This will remove all of the Firewall's Rules

## Firewall Device Create

<a id="opIdcreateFirewallDevice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/firewalls/0/devices \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": 123,
    "type": "linode"
  }'
```

`POST /networking/firewalls/{firewallId}/devices`

Creates a Firewall Device, which assigns a Firewall to a service (referred to
as the Device's `entity`) and applies the Firewall's Rules to the device.

* Currently, only Devices with an entity of type `linode` are accepted.

* A Firewall can be assigned to multiple Linode instances at a time.

* A Linode instance can have one active, assigned Firewall at a time.
Additional disabled Firewalls can be assigned to a service, but they cannot be enabled if another active Firewall is already assigned to the same service.

* A `firewall_device_add` Event is generated when the Firewall Device is added successfully.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": 123,
  "type": "linode"
}
```

<h3 id="firewall-device-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|firewallId|path|integer|true|ID of the Firewall to access.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|integer|true|The entity's ID|
|» type|body|string|true|The entity's type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|linode|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "entity": {
    "id": 123,
    "label": "my-linode",
    "type": "linode",
    "url": "/v4/linode/instances/123"
  },
  "id": 123,
  "updated": "2018-01-02T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

## Firewall Device Delete

<a id="opIddeleteFirewallDevice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/firewalls/0/devices/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /networking/firewalls/{firewallId}/devices/{deviceId}`

Removes a Firewall Device, which removes a Firewall from the Linode service it was
assigned to by the Device. This will remove all of the Firewall's Rules from the Linode
service. If any other Firewalls have been assigned to the Linode service, then those Rules
will remain in effect.

A `firewall_device_remove` Event is generated when the Firewall Device is removed successfully.

```json
{}
```

## IP Addresses Assign

<a id="opIdassignIPs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/ips/assign \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "assignments": [
      {
        "address": "192.0.2.1",
        "linode_id": 123
      }
    ],
    "region": "us-east"
  }'
```

`POST /networking/ips/assign`

Assign multiple IPv4 addresses and/or IPv6 ranges to multiple Linodes in one Region. This allows swapping, shuffling, or otherwise reorganizing IPs to your Linodes.

The following restrictions apply:
* All Linodes involved must have at least one public IPv4 address after assignment.
* Linodes may have no more than one assigned private IPv4 address.
* Linodes may have no more than one assigned IPv6 range.

[Open a Support Ticket](/docs/api/support/#support-ticket-open) to request additional IPv4 addresses or IPv6 ranges beyond standard account limits.

**Note**: Removing an IP address that has been set as a Managed Linode's `ssh.ip` causes the Managed Linode's SSH access settings to reset to their default values. To view and configure Managed Linode SSH settings, use the following commands:
* **Linode's Managed Settings View** ([GET /managed/linode-settings/{linodeId}](/docs/api/managed/#linodes-managed-settings-view))
* **Linode's Managed Settings Update** ([PUT /managed/linode-settings/{linodeId}](/docs/api/managed/#linodes-managed-settings-update))


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assignments": [
    {
      "address": "192.0.2.1",
      "linode_id": 123
    }
  ],
  "region": "us-east"
}
```

<h3 id="ip-addresses-assign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IPAddressesAssignRequest](#schemaipaddressesassignrequest)|true|Information about what IPv4 address or IPv6 range to assign, and to which Linode.<br>|
|» assignments|body|[object]|true|The list of assignments to make. You must have read_write access to all IPs being assigned and all Linodes being assigned to in order for the assignments to succeed.<br>|
|» » address|body|string(ipv4\|ipv6/prefix_length)|false|The IPv4 address or IPv6 range for this assignment.<br>* Must be an IPv4 address or an IPv6 range you can access in the Region specified.<br>* IPv6 ranges must include a prefix length of `/56` or `/64`, for example: `2001:db8:3c4d:15::/64`.<br>* Assignment of an IPv6 range to a Linode updates the route target of the range to the assigned Linode's SLAAC address.<br>* May be a public or private address.<br>|
|» » linode_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Linode to assign this address to. The IP's previous Linode will lose this address, and must end up with at least one public address and no more than one private address once all assignments have been made.<br>|
|» region|body|string|true|The ID of the Region in which these assignments are to take place. All IPs and Linodes must exist in this Region.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="ip-addresses-assign-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|All assignments completed successfully.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="ip-addresses-assign-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: ips:read_write linodes:read_write )
</aside>

## IP Addresses Share

<a id="opIdshareIPs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/ips/share \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ips": [
      "192.0.2.1",
      "2001:db8:3c4d:15::"
    ],
    "linode_id": 123
  }'
```

`POST /networking/ips/share`

Configure shared IPs.

IP sharing allows IP address reassignment (also referred to as IP failover) from one Linode to another if the primary Linode becomes unresponsive. This means that requests to the primary Linode's IP address can be automatically rerouted to secondary Linodes at the configured shared IP addresses.

IP failover requires configuration of a failover service (such as [Keepalived](/docs/guides/ip-failover-keepalived)) within the internal system of the primary Linode.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ips": [
    "192.0.2.1",
    "2001:db8:3c4d:15::"
  ],
  "linode_id": 123
}
```

<h3 id="ip-addresses-share-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IPAddressesShareRequest](#schemaipaddressessharerequest)|true|Information about what IPs to share with which Linode.|
|» ips|body|[string(ip)]|true|A list of secondary Linode IPs to share with the primary Linode.<br>* Can include both IPv4 addresses and IPv6 ranges (omit /56 and /64 prefix lengths)<br>* Can include both private and public IPv4 addresses.<br>* You must have access to all of these addresses and they must be in the same Region as the primary Linode.<br>* Enter an empty array to remove all shared IP addresses.<br>|
|» linode_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the primary Linode that the addresses will be shared with.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="ip-addresses-share-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|IP Address sharing successful.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="ip-addresses-share-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: ips:read_write linodes:read_write )
</aside>

```json
  "public": true,
  "rdns": "test.example.org",
```

## Linodes Assign IPv4s

<a id="opIdassignIPv4s"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/ipv4/assign \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "assignments": [
      {
        "address": "192.0.2.1",
        "linode_id": 123
      }
    ],
    "region": "us-east"
  }'
```

`POST /networking/ipv4/assign`

This command is equivalent to **IP Addresses Assign** ([POST /networking/ips/assign](#ip-addresses-assign)).

Assign multiple IPv4 addresses and/or IPv6 ranges to multiple Linodes in one Region. This allows swapping, shuffling, or otherwise reorganizing IPs to your Linodes.

The following restrictions apply:
* All Linodes involved must have at least one public IPv4 address after assignment.
* Linodes may have no more than one assigned private IPv4 address.
* Linodes may have no more than one assigned IPv6 range.

[Open a Support Ticket](/docs/api/support/#support-ticket-open) to request additional IPv4 addresses or IPv6 ranges beyond standard account limits.

**Note**: Removing an IP address that has been set as a Managed Linode's `ssh.ip` causes the Managed Linode's SSH access settings to reset to their default values. To view and configure Managed Linode SSH settings, use the following commands:
* **Linode's Managed Settings View** ([GET /managed/linode-settings/{linodeId}](/docs/api/managed/#linodes-managed-settings-view))
* **Linode's Managed Settings Update** ([PUT /managed/linode-settings/{linodeId}](/docs/api/managed/#linodes-managed-settings-update))


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assignments": [
    {
      "address": "192.0.2.1",
      "linode_id": 123
    }
  ],
  "region": "us-east"
}
```

<h3 id="linodes-assign-ipv4s-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IPAddressesAssignRequest](#schemaipaddressesassignrequest)|true|Information about what IPv4 address to assign, and to which Linode.<br>|
|» assignments|body|[object]|true|The list of assignments to make. You must have read_write access to all IPs being assigned and all Linodes being assigned to in order for the assignments to succeed.<br>|
|» » address|body|string(ipv4\|ipv6/prefix_length)|false|The IPv4 address or IPv6 range for this assignment.<br>* Must be an IPv4 address or an IPv6 range you can access in the Region specified.<br>* IPv6 ranges must include a prefix length of `/56` or `/64`, for example: `2001:db8:3c4d:15::/64`.<br>* Assignment of an IPv6 range to a Linode updates the route target of the range to the assigned Linode's SLAAC address.<br>* May be a public or private address.<br>|
|» » linode_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Linode to assign this address to. The IP's previous Linode will lose this address, and must end up with at least one public address and no more than one private address once all assignments have been made.<br>|
|» region|body|string|true|The ID of the Region in which these assignments are to take place. All IPs and Linodes must exist in this Region.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="linodes-assign-ipv4s-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|All assignments completed successfully.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="linodes-assign-ipv4s-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

## IPv4 Sharing Configure

<a id="opIdshareIPv4s"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/ipv4/share \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ips": [
      "192.0.2.1",
      "2001:db8:3c4d:15::"
    ],
    "linode_id": 123
  }'
```

`POST /networking/ipv4/share`

This command is equivalent to **IP Addresses Share** ([POST /networking/ips/share](#ip-addresses-share)).

Configure shared IPs.

IP sharing allows IP address reassignment (also referred to as IP failover) from one Linode to another if the primary Linode becomes unresponsive. This means that requests to the primary Linode's IP address can be automatically rerouted to secondary Linodes at the configured shared IP addresses.

IP failover requires configuration of a failover service (such as [Keepalived](/docs/guides/ip-failover-keepalived)) within the internal system of the primary Linode.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ips": [
    "192.0.2.1",
    "2001:db8:3c4d:15::"
  ],
  "linode_id": 123
}
```

<h3 id="ipv4-sharing-configure-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[IPAddressesShareRequest](#schemaipaddressessharerequest)|true|Information about what IPs to share with which Linode.|
|» ips|body|[string(ip)]|true|A list of secondary Linode IPs to share with the primary Linode.<br>* Can include both IPv4 addresses and IPv6 ranges (omit /56 and /64 prefix lengths)<br>* Can include both private and public IPv4 addresses.<br>* You must have access to all of these addresses and they must be in the same Region as the primary Linode.<br>* Enter an empty array to remove all shared IP addresses.<br>|
|» linode_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the primary Linode that the addresses will be shared with.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="ipv4-sharing-configure-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Sharing configured successfully.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="ipv4-sharing-configure-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: ips:read_write linodes:read_write )
</aside>

## IPv6 Range Create

<a id="opIdpostIPv6Range"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/ipv6/ranges \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "linode_id": 123,
    "prefix_length": 56,
    "route_target": "2001:0db8::1"
  }'
```

`POST /networking/ipv6/ranges`

Creates an IPv6 Range and assigns it based on the provided Linode or route target IPv6 SLAAC address. See the `ipv6` property when accessing the Linode View ([GET /linode/instances/{linodeId}](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-view)) endpoint to view a Linode's IPv6 SLAAC address.
  * Either `linode_id` or `route_target` is required in a request.
  * `linode_id` and `route_target` are mutually exclusive. Submitting values for both properties in a request results in an error.
  * Upon a successful request, an IPv6 range is created in the [Region](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list) that corresponds to the provided `linode_id` or `route_target`.
  * Your Linode is responsible for routing individual addresses in the range, or handling traffic for all the addresses in the range.
  * Access the IP Addresses Assign ([POST /networking/ips/assign](/docs/api/networking/#ip-addresses-assign)) endpoint to re-assign IPv6 Ranges to your Linodes.

**Note**: The following restrictions apply:
  * A Linode can only have one IPv6 range targeting its SLAAC address.
  * An account can only have one IPv6 range in each [Region](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list).
  * [Open a Support Ticket](/docs/api/support/#support-ticket-open) to request expansion of these restrictions.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "linode_id": 123,
  "prefix_length": 56,
  "route_target": "2001:0db8::1"
}
```

<h3 id="ipv6-range-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the IPv6 range to create.<br>|
|» linode_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Linode to assign this range to. The SLAAC address for the provided Linode is used as the range's `route_target`.<br><br>* **Required** if `route_target` is omitted from the request.<br><br>* Mutually exclusive with `route_target`. Submitting values for both properties in a request results in an error.<br>|
|» prefix_length|body|integer|true|The prefix length of the IPv6 range.<br>|
|» route_target|body|string(ipv6)|false|The IPv6 SLAAC address to assign this range to.<br><br>* **Required** if `linode_id` is omitted from the request.<br><br>* Mutually exclusive with `linode_id`. Submitting values for both properties in a request results in an error.<br><br>* **Note**: Omit the `/128` prefix length of the SLAAC address when using this property.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» prefix_length|56|
|» prefix_length|64|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "range": "2001:0db8::/64",
  "route_target": "2001:0db8::1"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="ipv6-range-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|IPv6 range created successfully.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="ipv6-range-create-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|range|string(ipv6/prefix_length)|false|none|The IPv6 network range, including subnet and prefix length.<br>|
|route_target|string(ipv6)|false|none|The route target IPV6 SLAAC address for this range. Does not include the prefix length.<br>|

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: ips:read_write linodes:read_write )
</aside>

## VLANs List

<a id="opIdgetVLANs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/networking/vlans \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /networking/vlans`

Returns a list of all Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) on your Account. VLANs provide
a mechanism for secure communication between two or more Linodes that are assigned to the
same VLAN and are both within the same Layer 2 broadcast domain.

VLANs are created and attached to Linodes by using the `interfaces` property for the following endpoints:

- Linode Create ([POST /linode/instances](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-create))
- Configuration Profile Create ([POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/configs](/docs/api/linode-instances/#configuration-profile-create))
- Configuration Profile Update ([PUT /linode/instances/{linodeId}/configs/{configId}](/docs/api/linode-instances/#configuration-profile-update))

There are several ways to detach a VLAN from a Linode:

- [Update](/docs/api/linode-instances/#configuration-profile-update) the active Configuration Profile to remove the VLAN interface, then [reboot](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-reboot) the Linode.
- [Create](/docs/api/linode-instances/#configuration-profile-create) a new Configuration Profile without the VLAN interface, then [reboot](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-reboot) the Linode into the new Configuration Profile.
- [Delete](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-delete) the Linode.

**Note:** Only Next Generation Network (NGN) data centers support VLANs. Use the Regions ([/regions](/docs/api/regions/)) endpoint to view the capabilities of data center regions.
If a VLAN is attached to your Linode and you attempt to migrate or clone it to a non-NGN data center,
the migration or cloning will not initiate. If a Linode cannot be migrated because of an incompatibility,
you will be prompted to select a different data center or contact support.

**Note:** See the [VLANs Overview](/docs/products/networking/vlans/#technical-specifications) to view additional specifications and limitations.


<h3 id="vlans-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|page|query|integer|false|The page of a collection to return.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|

```json
      ],
      "region": "ap-west"
    }
  ],

  "pages": 1,
  "results": 1
}
```

```json
    {
      "field": "fieldname",

    }

}
```
