## NodeBalancer Create

<a id="opIdcreateNodeBalancer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/nodebalancers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_conn_throttle": 0,
    "configs": [
      {
        "algorithm": "roundrobin",
        "check": "http_body",
        "check_attempts": 3,
        "check_body": "it works",
        "check_interval": 90,
        "check_passive": true,
        "check_path": "/test",
        "check_timeout": 10,
        "cipher_suite": "recommended",
        "nodes": [
          {
            "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
            "label": "node54321",
            "mode": "accept",
            "weight": 50
          }
        ],
        "port": 80,
        "protocol": "http",
        "proxy_protocol": "none",
        "ssl_cert": "<REDACTED>",
        "ssl_key": "<REDACTED>",
        "stickiness": "http_cookie"
      }
    ],
    "label": "balancer12345",
    "region": "us-east"
  }'
```

`POST /nodebalancers`

Creates a NodeBalancer in the requested Region.

NodeBalancers require a port Config with at least one backend Node to start serving requests.

When using the Linode CLI to create a NodeBalancer, first create a NodeBalancer without any Configs. Then, create Configs and Nodes for that NodeBalancer with the respective [Config Create](/docs/api/nodebalancers/#config-create) and [Node Create](/docs/api/nodebalancers/#node-create) commands.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_conn_throttle": 0,
  "configs": [
    {
      "algorithm": "roundrobin",
      "check": "http_body",
      "check_attempts": 3,
      "check_body": "it works",
      "check_interval": 90,
      "check_passive": true,
      "check_path": "/test",
      "check_timeout": 10,
      "cipher_suite": "recommended",
      "nodes": [
        {
          "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
          "label": "node54321",
          "mode": "accept",
          "weight": 50
        }
      ],
      "port": 80,
      "protocol": "http",
      "proxy_protocol": "none",
      "ssl_cert": "<REDACTED>",
      "ssl_key": "<REDACTED>",
      "stickiness": "http_cookie"
    }
  ],
  "label": "balancer12345",
  "region": "us-east"
}
```

<h3 id="nodebalancer-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the NodeBalancer to create.|
|» client_conn_throttle|body|integer|false|Throttle connections per second.  Set to 0 (zero) to disable throttling.<br>|
|» configs|body|[object]|false|The port Config(s) to create for this NodeBalancer.<br><br>Each Config must have a unique port and at least one Node.<br>|
|» » algorithm|body|string|false|What algorithm this NodeBalancer should use for routing traffic to backends.<br>|
|» » check|body|string|false|The type of check to perform against backends to ensure they are serving requests. This is used to determine if backends are up or down.<br>* If `none` no check is performed.<br>* `connection` requires only a connection to the backend to succeed.<br>* `http` and `http_body` rely on the backend serving HTTP, and that<br>  the response returned matches what is expected.<br>|
|» » check_attempts|body|integer|false|How many times to attempt a check before considering a backend to be down.<br>|
|» » check_body|body|string|false|This value must be present in the response body of the check in order for it to pass. If this value is not present in the response body of a check request, the backend is considered to be down.<br>|
|» » check_interval|body|integer|false|How often, in seconds, to check that backends are up and serving requests.<br><br>Must be greater than `check_timeout`.<br>|
|» » check_passive|body|boolean|false|If true, any response from this backend with a `5xx` status code will be enough for it to be considered unhealthy and taken out of rotation.<br>|
|» » check_path|body|string|false|The URL path to check on each backend. If the backend does not respond to this request it is considered to be down.<br>|
|» » check_timeout|body|integer|false|How long, in seconds, to wait for a check attempt before considering it failed.<br><br>Must be less than `check_interval`.<br>|
|» » cipher_suite|body|string|false|What ciphers to use for SSL connections served by this NodeBalancer.<br><br>* `legacy` is considered insecure and should only be used if necessary.<br>|
|» » nodes|body|[[NodeBalancerNode](#schemanodebalancernode)]|false|The NodeBalancer Node(s) that serve this Config.<br>|
|» » port|body|integer|false|The port this Config is for. These values must be unique across configs on a single NodeBalancer (you can't have two configs for port 80, for example).  While some ports imply some protocols, no enforcement is done and you may configure your NodeBalancer however is useful to you. For example, while port 443 is generally used for HTTPS, you do not need SSL configured to have a NodeBalancer listening on port 443.<br>|
|» » protocol|body|string|false|The protocol this port is configured to serve.<br><br>* The `http` and `tcp` protocols do not support `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>* The `https` protocol is mutually required with `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>Review our guide on [Available Protocols](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/protocols/) for information on protocol features.<br>|
|» » proxy_protocol|body|string|false|ProxyProtocol is a TCP extension that sends initial TCP connection information such as source/destination IPs and ports to backend devices. This information would be lost otherwise. Backend devices must be configured to work with ProxyProtocol if enabled.<br><br>* If ommited, or set to `none`, the NodeBalancer doesn't send any auxilary data over TCP connections. This is the default.<br>* If set to `v1`, the human-readable header format (Version 1) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>* If set to `v2`, the binary header format (Version 2) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>|
|» » ssl_cert|body|string(ssl-cert) \| null|false|The PEM-formatted public SSL certificate (or the combined PEM-formatted SSL<br>certificate and Certificate Authority chain) that should be served on this<br>NodeBalancerConfig's port.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>[Diffie-Hellman Parameters](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/ssl-termination/#diffie-hellman-parameters) can be included in this value to enable forward secrecy.<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|» » ssl_key|body|string(ssl-key) \| null|false|The PEM-formatted private key for the SSL certificate set in the `ssl_cert` field.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|» » stickiness|body|string|false|Controls how session stickiness is handled on this port.<br>* If set to `none` connections will always be assigned a backend based on the algorithm configured.<br>* If set to `table` sessions from the same remote address will be routed to the same<br>  backend.<br><br>* For HTTP or HTTPS clients, `http_cookie` allows sessions to be<br>  routed to the same backend based on a cookie set by the NodeBalancer.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|This NodeBalancer's label. These must be unique on your Account.<br>|
|» region|body|string|true|The ID of the Region to create this NodeBalancer in.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » algorithm|roundrobin|
|» » algorithm|leastconn|
|» » algorithm|source|
|» » check|none|
|» » check|connection|
|» » check|http|
|» » check|http_body|
|» » cipher_suite|recommended|
|» » cipher_suite|legacy|
|» » protocol|http|
|» » protocol|https|
|» » protocol|tcp|
|» » proxy_protocol|none|
|» » proxy_protocol|v1|
|» » proxy_protocol|v2|
|» » stickiness|none|
|» » stickiness|table|
|» » stickiness|http_cookie|

## NodeBalancer Delete

<a id="opIddeleteNodeBalancer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/nodebalancers/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /nodebalancers/{nodeBalancerId}`

Deletes a NodeBalancer.

**This is a destructive action and cannot be undone.**

Deleting a NodeBalancer will also delete all associated Configs and Nodes, although the backend servers represented by the Nodes will not be changed or removed. Deleting a NodeBalancer will cause you to lose access to the IP Addresses assigned to this NodeBalancer.


<h3 id="nodebalancer-delete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nodeBalancerId|path|integer|true|The ID of the NodeBalancer to access.|

```json
{}
```

|» protocol|body|string|false|The protocol this port is configured to serve.<br><br>* The `http` and `tcp` protocols do not support `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>* The `https` protocol is mutually required with `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>Review our guide on [Available Protocols](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/protocols/) for information on protocol features.<br>|
|» proxy_protocol|body|string|false|ProxyProtocol is a TCP extension that sends initial TCP connection information such as source/destination IPs and ports to backend devices. This information would be lost otherwise. Backend devices must be configured to work with ProxyProtocol if enabled.<br><br>* If ommited, or set to `none`, the NodeBalancer doesn't send any auxilary data over TCP connections. This is the default.<br>* If set to `v1`, the human-readable header format (Version 1) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>* If set to `v2`, the binary header format (Version 2) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>|
|» ssl_cert|body|string(ssl-cert) \| null|false|The PEM-formatted public SSL certificate (or the combined PEM-formatted SSL<br>certificate and Certificate Authority chain) that should be served on this<br>NodeBalancerConfig's port.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>[Diffie-Hellman Parameters](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/ssl-termination/#diffie-hellman-parameters) can be included in this value to enable forward secrecy.<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|» ssl_key|body|string(ssl-key) \| null|false|The PEM-formatted private key for the SSL certificate set in the `ssl_cert` field.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|» stickiness|body|string|false|Controls how session stickiness is handled on this port.<br>* If set to `none` connections will always be assigned a backend based on the algorithm configured.<br>* If set to `table` sessions from the same remote address will be routed to the same<br>  backend.<br><br>* For HTTP or HTTPS clients, `http_cookie` allows sessions to be<br>  routed to the same backend based on a cookie set by the NodeBalancer.<br>|

|» cipher_suite|legacy|

|» protocol|https|
|» protocol|tcp|

```json

  "check": "http_body",

  "port": 80,

}
```

|» algorithm|body|string|false|What algorithm this NodeBalancer should use for routing traffic to backends.<br>|
|» check|body|string|false|The type of check to perform against backends to ensure they are serving requests. |» check_passive|body|boolean|false|If true, any response from this backend with a `5xx` status code will be enough for it to be considered unhealthy and taken out of rotation.<br>|

For example, while port 443 is generally used for HTTPS, you do not need SSL configured to have a NodeBalancer listening on port 443.<br>|

Backend devices must be configured to work with ProxyProtocol if enabled.<br><br>* If ommited, or set to `none`, the NodeBalancer doesn't send any auxilary data over TCP connections. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>|

## Config Delete

<a id="opIddeleteNodeBalancerConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/nodebalancers/0/configs/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /nodebalancers/{nodeBalancerId}/configs/{configId}`

Deletes the Config for a port of this NodeBalancer.

**This cannot be undone.**

Once completed, this NodeBalancer will no longer respond to requests on the given port. This also deletes all associated NodeBalancerNodes, but the Linodes they were routing traffic to will be unchanged and will not be removed.


<h3 id="config-delete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nodeBalancerId|path|integer|true|The ID of the NodeBalancer to access.|
|configId|path|integer|true|The ID of the config to access.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|NodeBalancer Config deleted successfully.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

Status Code **default**

## Node Create

<a id="opIdcreateNodeBalancerNode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/nodebalancers/0/configs/0/nodes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
    "label": "node54321",
    "mode": "accept",
    "weight": 50
  }'
```

`POST /nodebalancers/{nodeBalancerId}/configs/{configId}/nodes`

Creates a NodeBalancer Node, a backend that can accept traffic for this NodeBalancer Config. Nodes are routed requests on the configured port based on their status.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
  "label": "node54321",
  "mode": "accept",
  "weight": 50
}
```

<h3 id="node-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nodeBalancerId|path|integer|true|The ID of the NodeBalancer to access.|
|configId|path|integer|true|The ID of the NodeBalancer config to access.|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the Node to create.|
|» address|body|string(ip)|true|The private IP Address where this backend can be reached. This _must_ be a private IP address.<br>|
|» label|body|string|true|The label for this node.  This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» mode|body|string|false|The mode this NodeBalancer should use when sending traffic to this backend.<br>* If set to `accept` this backend is accepting traffic.<br>* If set to `reject` this backend will not receive traffic.<br>* If set to `drain` this backend will not receive _new_ traffic, but connections already<br>  pinned to it will continue to be routed to it.<br><br>* If set to `backup`, this backend will only receive traffic if all `accept` nodes<br>  are down.<br>|
|» weight|body|integer|false|Used when picking a backend to serve a request and is not pinned to a single backend yet.  Nodes with a higher weight will receive more traffic.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|accept|
|» mode|reject|
|» mode|drain|
|» mode|backup|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
  "config_id": 4567,
  "id": 54321,
  "label": "node54321",
  "mode": "accept",
  "nodebalancer_id": 12345,
  "status": "UP",
  "weight": 50
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

|default|Default|Error|Inline|

## Node Update

<a id="opIdupdateNodeBalancerNode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/nodebalancers/0/configs/0/nodes/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
    "label": "node54321",
    "mode": "accept",
    "weight": 50
  }'
```

`PUT /nodebalancers/{nodeBalancerId}/configs/{configId}/nodes/{nodeId}`

Updates information about a Node, a backend for this NodeBalancer's configured port.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
  "label": "node54321",
  "mode": "accept",
  "weight": 50
}
```

<h3 id="node-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nodeBalancerId|path|integer|true|The ID of the NodeBalancer to access.|
|configId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Config to access|
|nodeId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Node to access|
|body|body|[NodeBalancerNode](#schemanodebalancernode)|true|The fields to update.|
|» address|body|string(ip)|false|The private IP Address where this backend can be reached. This _must_ be a private IP address.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|The label for this node.  This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» mode|body|string|false|The mode this NodeBalancer should use when sending traffic to this backend.<br>* If set to `accept` this backend is accepting traffic.<br>* If set to `reject` this backend will not receive traffic.<br>* If set to `drain` this backend will not receive _new_ traffic, but connections already<br>  pinned to it will continue to be routed to it.<br><br>* If set to `backup`, this backend will only receive traffic if all `accept` nodes<br>  are down.<br>|
|» weight|body|integer|false|Used when picking a backend to serve a request and is not pinned to a single backend yet.  Nodes with a higher weight will receive more traffic.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|accept|
|» mode|reject|
|» mode|drain|
|» mode|backup|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
  "config_id": 4567,
  "id": 54321,
  "label": "node54321",
  "mode": "accept",
  "nodebalancer_id": 12345,
  "status": "UP",
  "weight": 50
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Config Rebuild

<a id="opIdrebuildNodeBalancerConfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/nodebalancers/0/configs/0/rebuild \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "algorithm": "roundrobin",
    "check": "http_body",
    "check_attempts": 3,
    "check_body": "it works",
    "check_interval": 90,
    "check_passive": true,
    "check_path": "/test",
    "check_timeout": 10,
    "cipher_suite": "recommended",
    "port": 80,
    "protocol": "http",
    "proxy_protocol": "none",
    "ssl_cert": "<REDACTED>",
    "ssl_key": "<REDACTED>",
    "stickiness": "http_cookie",
    "nodes": [
      {
        "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
        "id": 54321,
        "label": "node54321",
        "mode": "accept",
        "weight": 50
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /nodebalancers/{nodeBalancerId}/configs/{configId}/rebuild`

Rebuilds a NodeBalancer Config and its Nodes that you have permission to modify.

Use this command to update a NodeBalancer's Config and Nodes with a single request.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm": "roundrobin",
  "check": "http_body",
  "check_attempts": 3,
  "check_body": "it works",
  "check_interval": 90,
  "check_passive": true,
  "check_path": "/test",
  "check_timeout": 10,
  "cipher_suite": "recommended",
  "port": 80,
  "protocol": "http",
  "proxy_protocol": "none",
  "ssl_cert": "<REDACTED>",
  "ssl_key": "<REDACTED>",
  "stickiness": "http_cookie",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
      "id": 54321,
      "label": "node54321",
      "mode": "accept",
      "weight": 50
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="config-rebuild-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nodeBalancerId|path|integer|true|The ID of the NodeBalancer to access.|
|configId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Config to access.|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the NodeBalancer Config to rebuild.<br>|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|What algorithm this NodeBalancer should use for routing traffic to backends.<br>|
|» check|body|string|false|The type of check to perform against backends to ensure they are serving requests. This is used to determine if backends are up or down.<br>* If `none` no check is performed.<br>* `connection` requires only a connection to the backend to succeed.<br>* `http` and `http_body` rely on the backend serving HTTP, and that<br>  the response returned matches what is expected.<br>|
|» check_attempts|body|integer|false|How many times to attempt a check before considering a backend to be down.<br>|
|» check_body|body|string|false|This value must be present in the response body of the check in order for it to pass. If this value is not present in the response body of a check request, the backend is considered to be down.<br>|
|» check_interval|body|integer|false|How often, in seconds, to check that backends are up and serving requests.<br><br>Must be greater than `check_timeout`.<br>|
|» check_passive|body|boolean|false|If true, any response from this backend with a `5xx` status code will be enough for it to be considered unhealthy and taken out of rotation.<br>|
|» check_path|body|string|false|The URL path to check on each backend. If the backend does not respond to this request it is considered to be down.<br>|
|» check_timeout|body|integer|false|How long, in seconds, to wait for a check attempt before considering it failed.<br><br>Must be less than `check_interval`.<br>|
|» cipher_suite|body|string|false|What ciphers to use for SSL connections served by this NodeBalancer.<br><br>* `legacy` is considered insecure and should only be used if necessary.<br>|
|» port|body|integer|false|The port this Config is for. These values must be unique across configs on a single NodeBalancer (you can't have two configs for port 80, for example).  While some ports imply some protocols, no enforcement is done and you may configure your NodeBalancer however is useful to you. For example, while port 443 is generally used for HTTPS, you do not need SSL configured to have a NodeBalancer listening on port 443.<br>|
|» protocol|body|string|false|The protocol this port is configured to serve.<br><br>* The `http` and `tcp` protocols do not support `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>* The `https` protocol is mutually required with `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>Review our guide on [Available Protocols](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/protocols/) for information on protocol features.<br>|
|» proxy_protocol|body|string|false|ProxyProtocol is a TCP extension that sends initial TCP connection information such as source/destination IPs and ports to backend devices. This information would be lost otherwise. Backend devices must be configured to work with ProxyProtocol if enabled.<br><br>* If ommited, or set to `none`, the NodeBalancer doesn't send any auxilary data over TCP connections. This is the default.<br>* If set to `v1`, the human-readable header format (Version 1) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>* If set to `v2`, the binary header format (Version 2) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>|
|» ssl_cert|body|string(ssl-cert) \| null|false|The PEM-formatted public SSL certificate (or the combined PEM-formatted SSL<br>certificate and Certificate Authority chain) that should be served on this<br>NodeBalancerConfig's port.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>[Diffie-Hellman Parameters](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/ssl-termination/#diffie-hellman-parameters) can be included in this value to enable forward secrecy.<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|» ssl_key|body|string(ssl-key) \| null|false|The PEM-formatted private key for the SSL certificate set in the `ssl_cert` field.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|» stickiness|body|string|false|Controls how session stickiness is handled on this port.<br>* If set to `none` connections will always be assigned a backend based on the algorithm configured.<br>* If set to `table` sessions from the same remote address will be routed to the same<br>  backend.<br><br>* For HTTP or HTTPS clients, `http_cookie` allows sessions to be<br>  routed to the same backend based on a cookie set by the NodeBalancer.<br>|
|» nodes|body|[object]|true|The NodeBalancer Node(s) that serve this Config.<br><br>Some considerations for Nodes when rebuilding a config:<br>  * Current Nodes excluded from the request body will be deleted from the Config.<br>  * Current Nodes (identified by their Node ID) will be updated.<br>  * New Nodes (included without a Node ID) will be created.<br>|
|» » address|body|string(ip)|false|The private IP Address where this backend can be reached. This _must_ be a private IP address.<br>|
|» » id|body|integer|false|The unique ID of the Node to update.|
|» » label|body|string|false|The label for this node.  This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» » mode|body|string|false|The mode this NodeBalancer should use when sending traffic to this backend.<br>* If set to `accept` this backend is accepting traffic.<br>* If set to `reject` this backend will not receive traffic.<br>* If set to `drain` this backend will not receive _new_ traffic, but connections already<br>  pinned to it will continue to be routed to it.<br><br>* If set to `backup`, this backend will only receive traffic if all `accept` nodes<br>  are down.<br>|
|» » weight|body|integer|false|Used when picking a backend to serve a request and is not pinned to a single backend yet.  Nodes with a higher weight will receive more traffic.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» algorithm|roundrobin|
|» algorithm|leastconn|
|» algorithm|source|
|» check|none|
|» check|connection|
|» check|http|
|» check|http_body|
|» cipher_suite|recommended|
|» cipher_suite|legacy|
|» protocol|http|
|» protocol|https|
|» protocol|tcp|
|» proxy_protocol|none|
|» proxy_protocol|v1|
|» proxy_protocol|v2|
|» stickiness|none|
|» stickiness|table|
|» stickiness|http_cookie|
|» » mode|accept|
|» » mode|reject|
|» » mode|drain|
|» » mode|backup|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "algorithm": "roundrobin",
  "check": "http_body",
  "check_attempts": 3,
  "check_body": "it works",
  "check_interval": 90,
  "check_passive": true,
  "check_path": "/test",
  "check_timeout": 10,
  "cipher_suite": "recommended",
  "id": 4567,
  "nodebalancer_id": 12345,
  "nodes_status": {
    "down": 0,
    "up": 4
  },
  "port": 80,
  "protocol": "http",
  "proxy_protocol": "none",
  "ssl_cert": "<REDACTED>",
  "ssl_commonname": "www.example.com",
  "ssl_fingerprint": "00:01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09:0A:0B:0C:0D:0E:0F:10:11:12:13",
  "ssl_key": "<REDACTED>",
  "stickiness": "http_cookie"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="linode-api-object-storage">Object Storage</h1>

Object Storage is Linode's S3-compatible data storage service. Use the Object Storage endpoints to create and maintaining buckets, add and remove objects from buckets, create and maintain Object Storage keys, and cancel the Object Storage service.

## Object Storage Buckets List

<a id="opIdgetObjectStorageBuckets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/object-storage/buckets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Object Storage Bucket Create

<a id="opIdcreateObjectStorageBucket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/object-storage/buckets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "acl": "private",
    "cluster": "us-east-1",
    "cors_enabled": true,
    "label": "example-bucket"
  }'
```

`POST /object-storage/buckets`

Creates an Object Storage Bucket in the specified cluster.

Accounts with negative balances cannot access this command.

If the bucket already exists and is owned by you, this endpoint returns a `200` response with that bucket as if it had just been created.

This endpoint is available for convenience. It is recommended that instead you use the more [fully-featured S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/bucketops/#put-bucket) directly.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acl": "private",
  "cluster": "us-east-1",
  "cors_enabled": true,
  "label": "example-bucket"
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Information about the bucket you want to create.<br>|
|» acl|body|string|false|The Access Control Level of the bucket using a canned ACL string. For more fine-grained control of ACLs, use the S3 API directly.<br>|
|» cluster|body|string|true|The ID of the Object Storage Cluster where this bucket should be created.<br>|
|» cors_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, the bucket will be created with CORS enabled for all origins. For more fine-grained controls of CORS, use the S3 API directly.<br>|
|» label|body|string|true|The name for this bucket. Must be unique in the cluster you are creating the bucket in, or an error will be returned. Labels will be reserved only for the cluster that active buckets are created and stored in. If you want to reserve this bucket's label in another cluster, you must create a new bucket with the same label in the new cluster.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» acl|private|
|» acl|public-read|
|» acl|authenticated-read|
|» acl|public-read-write|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "cluster": "us-east-1",
  "created": "2019-01-01T01:23:45",
  "hostname": "example-bucket.us-east-1.linodeobjects.com",
  "label": "example-bucket",
  "objects": 4,
  "size": 188318981
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Object Storage Bucket Remove

<a id="opIddeleteObjectStorageBucket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/object-storage/buckets/string/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /object-storage/buckets/{clusterId}/{bucket}`

Removes a single bucket.

Bucket objects must be removed prior to removing the bucket. While buckets containing objects _may_ be
deleted using the [s3cmd command-line tool](/docs/products/storage/object-storage/guides/s3cmd/#delete-a-bucket), such operations
can fail if the bucket contains too many objects. The recommended
way to empty large buckets is to use the [S3 API to configure lifecycle policies](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/bucketpolicy/#) that
remove all objects, then delete the bucket.

This endpoint is available for convenience. It is recommended that instead you
use the more [fully-featured S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/bucketops/#delete-bucket) directly.


<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-remove-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|string|true|The ID of the cluster this bucket exists in.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Object Storage Bucket Access Update

<a id="opIdupdateObjectStorageBucketAccess"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/object-storage/buckets/string/string/access \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "acl": "private",
    "cors_enabled": true
  }'
```

`PUT /object-storage/buckets/{clusterId}/{bucket}/access`

Allows changing basic Cross-origin Resource Sharing (CORS) and Access Control Level (ACL) settings.
Only allows enabling/disabling CORS for all origins, and/or setting canned ACLs.


For more fine-grained control of both systems, please use the more [fully-featured S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/bucketops/#put-bucket-acl) directly.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acl": "private",
  "cors_enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-access-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|string|true|The ID of the cluster this bucket exists in.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|
|body|body|object|false|The changes to make to the bucket's access controls.|
|» acl|body|string|false|The Access Control Level of the bucket, as a canned ACL string. For more fine-grained control of ACLs, use the S3 API directly.<br>|
|» cors_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, the bucket will be created with CORS enabled for all origins. For more fine-grained controls of CORS, use the S3 API directly.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» acl|private|
|» acl|public-read|
|» acl|authenticated-read|
|» acl|public-read-write|
|» acl|custom|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-access-update-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Access controls updated.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-access-update-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: object_storage:read_write )
</aside>

## Object Storage Bucket Contents List

<a id="opIdgetObjectStorageBucketContent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/object-storage/buckets/string/string/object-list \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /object-storage/buckets/{clusterId}/{bucket}/object-list`

Returns the contents of a bucket. The contents are paginated using a `marker`,
which is the name of the last object on the previous page.  Objects may
be filtered by `prefix` and `delimiter` as well; see Query Parameters for more
information.


This endpoint is available for convenience. It is recommended that instead you
use the more [fully-featured S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/objectops/#get-object) directly.


<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-contents-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|marker|query|string|false|The "marker" for this request, which can be used to paginate through large buckets. Its value should be the value of the `next_marker` property returned with the last page. Listing bucket contents *does not* support arbitrary page access. See the `next_marker` property in the responses section for more details.<br>|
|delimiter|query|string|false|The delimiter for object names; if given, object names will be returned up to the first occurrence of this character. This is most commonly used with the `/` character to allow bucket transversal in a manner similar to a filesystem, however any delimiter may be used. Use in conjunction with `prefix` to see object names past the first occurrence of the delimiter.<br>|
|prefix|query|string|false|Filters objects returned to only those whose name start with the given prefix. Commonly used in conjunction with `delimiter` to allow transversal of bucket contents in a manner similar to a filesystem.<br>|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|clusterId|path|string|true|The ID of the cluster this bucket exists in.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "etag": "9f254c71e28e033bf9e0e5262e3e72ab",
      "is_truncated": true,
      "last_modified": "2019-01-01T01:23:45",
      "name": "example",
      "next_marker": "bd021c21-e734-4823-97a4-58b41c2cd4c8.892602.184",
      "owner": "bfc70ab2-e3d4-42a4-ad55-83921822270c",
      "size": 123
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-contents-list-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|One page of the requested bucket's contents.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="object-storage-bucket-contents-list-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[[ObjectStorageObject](#schemaobjectstorageobject)]|false|none|This page of objects in the bucket.|

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: object_storage:read_only )
</aside>

## Object Storage Object URL Create

<a id="opIdcreateObjectStorageObjectURL"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/object-storage/buckets/string/string/object-url \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "content_type": null,
    "expires_in": null,
    "method": "GET",
    "name": "example"
  }'
```

`POST /object-storage/buckets/{clusterId}/{bucket}/object-url`

Creates a pre-signed URL to access a single Object in a bucket. This
can be used to share objects, and also to create/delete objects by using
the appropriate HTTP method in your request body's `method` parameter.


This endpoint is available for convenience. It is recommended that instead you
use the more [fully-featured S3 API](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/s3/)
directly.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "content_type": null,
  "expires_in": null,
  "method": "GET",
  "name": "example"
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-object-url-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|string|true|The ID of the cluster this bucket exists in.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|
|body|body|object|false|Information about the request to sign.|
|» content_type|body|string|false|The expected `Content-type` header of the request this signed URL will be valid for.  If provided, the `Content-type` header _must_ be sent with the request when this URL is used, and _must_ be the same as it was when the signed URL was created. Required for all methods *except* "GET" or "DELETE".<br>|
|» expires_in|body|integer|false|How long this signed URL will be valid for, in seconds.  If omitted, the URL will be valid for 3600 seconds (1 hour).<br>|
|» method|body|string|true|The HTTP method allowed to be used with the pre-signed URL.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the object that will be accessed with the pre-signed URL. This object need not exist, and no error will be returned if it doesn't. This behavior is useful for generating pre-signed URLs to upload new objects to by setting the `method` to "PUT".<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "url": "https://us-east-1.linodeobjects.com/example-bucket/example?Signature=qr98TEucCntPgEG%2BsZQGDsJg93c%3D&Expires=1567609905&AWSAccessKeyId=G4YAF81XWY61DQM94SE0"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-object-url-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The URL with which to access your object.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="object-storage-object-url-create-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|url|string|false|none|The signed URL to perform the request at.|

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: object_storage:read_write )
</aside>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nCERTIFICATE_INFORMATION\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
    "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nPRIVATE_KEY_INFORMATION\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
  }'
```

`POST /object-storage/buckets/{clusterId}/{bucket}/ssl`

Upload a TLS/SSL certificate and private key to be served when you visit your Object Storage bucket via HTTPS.
Your TLS/SSL certificate and private key are stored encrypted at rest.


To replace an expired certificate, [delete your current certificate](/docs/api/object-storage/#object-storage-tlsssl-cert-delete)
and upload a new one.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nCERTIFICATE_INFORMATION\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nPRIVATE_KEY_INFORMATION\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----"
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-tlsssl-cert-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clusterId|path|string|true|The ID of the cluster this bucket exists in.|
|bucket|path|string|true|The bucket name.|
|body|body|[ObjectStorageSSL](#schemaobjectstoragessl)|false|Upload this TLS/SSL certificate with its corresponding secret key.|
|» certificate|body|string|true|Your Base64 encoded and PEM formatted SSL certificate.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI)<br>|
|» private_key|body|string|true|The private key associated with this TLS/SSL certificate.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI)<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "ssl": true
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-tlsssl-cert-upload-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns whether this bucket has a corresponding TLS/SSL certificate that was uploaded by a user.|[ObjectStorageSSLResponse](#schemaobjectstoragesslresponse)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="object-storage-tlsssl-cert-upload-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: object_storage:read_write )
</aside>

## Object Storage Key Create

<a id="opIdcreateObjectStorageKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/object-storage/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "bucket_access": [
      {
        "bucket_name": "example-bucket",
        "cluster": "ap-south-1",
        "permissions": "read_only"
      }
    ],
    "label": "my-key"
  }'
```

`POST /object-storage/keys`

Provisions a new Object Storage Key on your account.

Accounts with negative balances cannot access this command.

* To create a Limited Access Key with specific permissions, send a `bucket_access` array.

* To create a Limited Access Key without access to any buckets, send an empty `bucket_access` array.

* To create an Access Key with unlimited access to all clusters and all buckets, omit the `bucket_access` array.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bucket_access": [
    {
      "bucket_name": "example-bucket",
      "cluster": "ap-south-1",
      "permissions": "read_only"
    }
  ],
  "label": "my-key"
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-key-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ObjectStorageKey](#schemaobjectstoragekey)|false|The label of the key to create. This is used to identify the created key.<br>|
|» bucket_access|body|[object]|false|Defines this key as a Limited Access Key. Limited Access Keys restrict this Object Storage key's access to only the bucket(s) declared in this array and define their bucket-level permissions.<br><br><br>  Limited Access Keys can:<br><br>  * [list all buckets](/docs/api/object-storage/#object-storage-buckets-list) available on this Account, but cannot perform any actions on a bucket unless it has access to the bucket.<br><br><br>  * [create new buckets](/docs/api/object-storage/#object-storage-bucket-create), but do not have any access to the buckets it creates, unless explicitly given access to them.<br><br><br>  **Note:** You can create an Object Storage Limited Access Key without access to any buckets.<br>  This is achieved by sending a request with an empty `bucket_access` array.<br><br><br>  **Note:** If this field is omitted, a regular unlimited access key is issued.<br>|
|» » bucket_name|body|string|false|The unique label of the bucket to which the key will grant limited access.|
|» » cluster|body|string|false|The Object Storage cluster where a bucket to which the key is granting access is hosted.|
|» » permissions|body|string|false|This Limited Access Key's permissions for the selected bucket.|
|» label|body|string|false|The label given to this key. For display purposes only.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » permissions|read_write|
|» » permissions|read_only|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_key": "KVAKUTGBA4WTR2NSJQ81",
  "bucket_access": [
    {
      "bucket_name": "example-bucket",
      "cluster": "ap-south-1",
      "permissions": "read_only"
    }
  ],
  "id": 123,
  "label": "my-key",
  "limited": true,
  "secret_key": "OiA6F5r0niLs3QA2stbyq7mY5VCV7KqOzcmitmHw"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="object-storage-key-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The new keypair.  **This is the only time** the secret key is returned.|[ObjectStorageKey](#schemaobjectstoragekey)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="object-storage-key-create-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: object_storage:read_write )
</aside>

<h1 id="linode-api-profile">Profile</h1>

Use the Profile endpoints to manage your Linode user profile preferences and security settings. This includes creating and maintaining personal access tokens, creating and maintaining SSH keys, confirming and enabling two-factor authentication, and updating user and profile preferences.

## Profile View

<a id="opIdgetProfile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/profile \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /profile`

Returns information about the current User. This can be used to see who is acting in applications where more than one token is managed. For example, in third-party OAuth applications.

This endpoint is always accessible, no matter what OAuth scopes the acting token has.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "authentication_type": "password",
  "authorized_keys": null,
  "email": "example-user@gmail.com",
  "email_notifications": true,
  "ip_whitelist_enabled": false,
  "lish_auth_method": "keys_only",
  "referrals": {
    "code": "871be32f49c1411b14f29f618aaf0c14637fb8d3",
    "completed": 0,
    "credit": 0,
    "pending": 0,
    "total": 0,
    "url": "https://www.linode.com/?r=871be32f49c1411b14f29f618aaf0c14637fb8d3"
  },
  "restricted": false,
  "timezone": "US/Eastern",
  "two_factor_auth": true,
  "uid": 1234,
  "username": "exampleUser",
  "verified_phone_number": "+5555555555"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
    "restricted": false,
    "timezone": "US/Eastern",
    "two_factor_auth": true
  }'
```

`PUT /profile`

Update information in your Profile.  This endpoint requires the "account:read_write" OAuth Scope.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authorized_keys": null,
  "email": "example-user@gmail.com",
  "email_notifications": true,
  "ip_whitelist_enabled": false,
  "lish_auth_method": "keys_only",
  "restricted": false,
  "timezone": "US/Eastern",
  "two_factor_auth": true
}
```

<h3 id="profile-update-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[Profile](#schemaprofile)|true|The fields to update.|
|» authorized_keys|body|[string(ssh-key)]|false|The list of SSH Keys authorized to use Lish for your User. This value is ignored if `lish_auth_method` is "disabled."<br>|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|Your email address.  This address will be used for communication with Linode as necessary.<br>|
|» email_notifications|body|boolean|false|If true, you will receive email notifications about account activity.  If false, you may still receive business-critical communications through email.<br>|
|» ip_whitelist_enabled|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** If true, logins for your User will only be allowed from whitelisted IPs. This setting is currently deprecated, and cannot be enabled.<br><br>If you disable this setting, you will not be able to re-enable it.<br>|
|» lish_auth_method|body|string|false|The authentication methods that are allowed when connecting to [the Linode Shell (Lish)](/docs/guides/lish/).<br>* `keys_only` is the most secure if you intend to use Lish.<br>* `disabled` is recommended if you do not intend to use Lish at all.<br>* If this account's Cloud Manager authentication type is set to a Third-Party Authentication method, `password_keys` cannot be used as your Lish authentication method. To view this account's Cloud Manager `authentication_type` field, send a request to the [View Profile](/docs/api/profile/#profile-view) endpoint.<br>|
|» restricted|body|boolean|false|If true, your User has restrictions on what can be accessed on your Account. To get details on what entities/actions you can access/perform, see [/profile/grants](/docs/api/profile/#grants-list).<br>|
|» timezone|body|string|false|The timezone you prefer to see times in. This is not used by the API directly. It is provided for the benefit of clients such as the Linode Cloud Manager and other clients built on the API. All times returned by the API are in UTC.<br>|
|» two_factor_auth|body|boolean|false|If true, logins from untrusted computers will require Two Factor Authentication.  See [/profile/tfa-enable](/docs/api/profile/#two-factor-secret-create) to enable Two Factor Authentication.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» lish_auth_method|password_keys|
|» lish_auth_method|keys_only|
|» lish_auth_method|disabled|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "authentication_type": "password",
  "authorized_keys": null,
  "email": "example-user@gmail.com",
  "email_notifications": true,
  "ip_whitelist_enabled": false,
  "lish_auth_method": "keys_only",
  "referrals": {
    "code": "871be32f49c1411b14f29f618aaf0c14637fb8d3",
    "completed": 0,
    "credit": 0,
    "pending": 0,
    "total": 0,
    "url": "https://www.linode.com/?r=871be32f49c1411b14f29f618aaf0c14637fb8d3"
  },
  "restricted": false,
  "timezone": "US/Eastern",
  "two_factor_auth": true,
  "uid": 1234,
  "username": "exampleUser",
  "verified_phone_number": "+5555555555"
}
```

> default Response

```json

  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }

}
```

## Grants List

<a id="opIdgetProfileGrants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/profile/grants \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /profile/grants`

This returns a GrantsResponse describing what the acting User has been granted access to.  For unrestricted users, this will return a  204 and no body because unrestricted users have access to everything without grants.  This will not return information about entities you do not have access to.  This endpoint is useful when writing third-party OAuth applications to see what options you should present to the acting User.

For example, if they do not have `global.add_linodes`, you might not display a button to deploy a new Linode.

Any client may access this endpoint; no OAuth scopes are required.

## Phone Number Verification Code Send

<a id="opIdpostProfilePhoneNumber"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/profile/phone-number \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "iso_code": "US",
    "phone_number": "555-555-5555"
  }'
```

`POST /profile/phone-number`

Send a one-time verification code via SMS message to the submitted phone number. Providing your phone number helps ensure you can securely access your Account in case other ways to connect are lost. Your phone number is only used to verify your identity by sending an SMS message. Standard carrier messaging fees may apply.

* By accessing this command you are opting in to receive SMS messages. You can opt out of SMS messages by using the **Phone Number Delete** ([DELETE /profile/phone-number](/docs/api/profile/#phone-number-delete)) command after your phone number is verified.

* Verification codes are valid for 10 minutes after they are sent.

* Subsequent requests made prior to code expiration result in sending the same code.

Once a verification code is received, verify your phone number with the **Phone Number Verify** ([POST /profile/phone-number/verify](/docs/api/profile/#phone-number-verify)) command.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "iso_code": "US",
  "phone_number": "555-555-5555"
}
```

<h3 id="phone-number-verification-code-send-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Enter a phone number and country code for verification.|
|» iso_code|body|string|true|The two-letter ISO 3166 country code associated with the phone number.|
|» phone_number|body|string(phone)|true|A valid phone number.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="phone-number-verification-code-send-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Phone number verification code request successful.<br>|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="phone-number-verification-code-send-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">

personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: account:read_write )
</aside>

## Phone Number Delete

<a id="opIddeleteProfilePhoneNumber"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/profile/phone-number \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /profile/phone-number`

Delete the verified phone number for the User making this request.

## Phone Number Verify

<a id="opIdpostProfilePhoneNumberVerify"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/profile/phone-number/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "otp_code": "US"
  }'
```

`POST /profile/phone-number/verify`

Verify a phone number by confirming the one-time code received via SMS message after accessing the **Phone Verification Code Send** ([POST /profile/phone-number](/docs/api/profile/#phone-number-verification-code-send)) command.

* Verification codes are valid for 10 minutes after they are sent.

* Only the same User that made the verification code request can use that code with this command.

Once completed, the verified phone number is assigned to the User making the request. To change the verified phone number for a User, first use the **Phone Number Delete** ([DELETE /profile/phone-number](/docs/api/profile/#phone-number-delete)) command, then begin the verification process again with the **Phone Verification Code Send** ([POST /profile/phone-number](/docs/api/profile/#phone-number-verification-code-send)) command.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "otp_code": "US"
}
```

<h3 id="phone-number-verify-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|Enter a phone verification code for confirmation.|
|» otp_code|body|string|true|The one-time code received via SMS message after accessing the **Phone Verification Code Send** ([POST /profile/phone-number](/docs/api/profile/#phone-number-verification-code-send)) command.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="phone-number-verify-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Phone number verification successful.<br>|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="phone-number-verify-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: account:read_write )
</aside>

`POST /profile/security-questions`

## Personal Access Token Create

<a id="opIdcreatePersonalAccessToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/profile/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expiry": null,
    "label": "linode-cli",
    "scopes": "*"
  }'
```

`POST /profile/tokens`

Creates a Personal Access Token for your User. The raw token will be returned in the response, but will never be returned again afterward so be sure to take note of it. You may create a token with _at most_ the scopes of your current token. The created token will be able to access your Account until the given expiry, or until it is revoked.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiry": null,
  "label": "linode-cli",
  "scopes": "*"
}
```

<h3 id="personal-access-token-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Information about the requested token.|
|» expiry|body|string(date-time)|false|When this token should be valid until.  If omitted, the new token will be valid until it is manually revoked.<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|This token's label.  This is for display purposes only, but can be used to more easily track what you're using each token for.<br>|
|» scopes|body|string(oauth-scope)|false|The scopes to create the token with.  These cannot be changed after creation, and may not exceed the scopes of the acting token. If omitted, the new token will have the same scopes as the acting token.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "expiry": "2018-01-01T13:46:32",
  "id": 123,
  "label": "linode-cli",
  "scopes": "*",
  "token": "abcdefghijklmnop"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="personal-access-token-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Token created successfully.|[PersonalAccessToken](#schemapersonalaccesstoken)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="personal-access-token-create-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: account:read_write )
</aside>

## Personal Access Token Revoke

<a id="opIddeletePersonalAccessToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/profile/tokens/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /profile/tokens/{tokenId}`

Revokes a Personal Access Token. The token will be invalidated immediately, and requests using that token will fail with a 401. It is possible to revoke access to the token making the request to revoke a token, but keep in mind that doing so could lose you access to the api and require you to create a new token through some other means.


<h3 id="personal-access-token-revoke-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tokenId|path|integer|true|The ID of the token to access.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h1 id="linode-api-stackscripts">StackScripts</h1>

If the request is not authenticated, only public StackScripts are returned.

## StackScript Create

<a id="opIdaddStackScript"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/linode/stackscripts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "This StackScript installs and configures MySQL\n",
    "images": [
      "linode/debian9",
      "linode/debian8"
    ],
    "is_public": true,
    "label": "a-stackscript",
    "rev_note": "Set up MySQL",
    "script": "\"#!/bin/bash\"\n"
  }'
```

`POST /linode/stackscripts`

Creates a StackScript in your Account.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "This StackScript installs and configures MySQL\n",
  "images": [
    "linode/debian9",
    "linode/debian8"
  ],
  "is_public": true,
  "label": "a-stackscript",
  "rev_note": "Set up MySQL",
  "script": "\"#!/bin/bash\"\n"
}
```

<h3 id="stackscript-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|The properties to set for the new StackScript.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description for the StackScript.<br>|
|» images|body|[string]|true|An array of Image IDs. These are the Images that can be deployed with this StackScript.<br><br>`any/all` indicates that all available Images, including private Images, are accepted.<br>|
|» is_public|body|boolean|false|This determines whether other users can use your StackScript. **Once a StackScript is made public, it cannot be made private.**<br>|
|» label|body|string|true|The StackScript's label is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» rev_note|body|string|false|This field allows you to add notes for the set of revisions made to this StackScript.<br>|
|» script|body|string|true|The script to execute when provisioning a new Linode with this StackScript.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "deployments_active": 1,
  "deployments_total": 12,
  "description": "This StackScript installs and configures MySQL\n",

    "label": "Enter the DB password",
    "name": "DB_PASSWORD"
  },
  "user_gravatar_id": "a445b305abda30ebc766bc7fda037c37",
  "username": "myuser"
}
```

```json
{

    }
  ]
}
```

|body|body|[StackScript](#schemastackscript)|false|The fields to update.|
|» description|body|string|false|A description for the StackScript.<br>|
|» images|body|[string]|false|An array of Image IDs. These are the Images that can be deployed with this StackScript.<br><br>`any/all` indicates that all available Images, including private Images, are accepted.<br>|
|» is_public|body|boolean|false|This determines whether other users can use your StackScript. **Once a StackScript is made public, it cannot be made private.**<br>|
|» label|body|string|false|The StackScript's label is for display purposes only.<br>|
|» rev_note|body|string|false|This field allows you to add notes for the set of revisions made to this StackScript.<br>|
|» script|body|string|false|The script to execute when provisioning a new Linode with this StackScript.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",

  "id": 10079,

}
```

<h1 id="linode-api-support">Support</h1>

Use the Support endpoints to open, view, and close Linode Support tickets. You can also create and manage your Support ticket replies.

## Support Tickets List

<a id="opIdgetTickets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/support/tickets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /support/tickets`

Returns a collection of Support Tickets on your Account. Support Tickets can be both tickets you open with Linode for support, as well as tickets generated by Linode regarding your Account.
This collection includes all Support Tickets generated on your Account, with open tickets returned first.


<h3 id="support-tickets-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Support Ticket Open

<a id="opIdcreateTicket"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/support/tickets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "database_id": 0,
    "description": "I'\''m having trouble setting the root password on my Linode. I tried following the instructions but something is not working and I'\''m not sure what I'\''m doing wrong. Can you please help me figure out how I can reset it?\n",
    "domain_id": null,
    "firewall_id": 0,
    "linode_id": 123,
    "lkecluster_id": 123,
    "longviewclient_id": null,
    "managed_issue": false,
    "nodebalancer_id": null,
    "region": null,
    "summary": "Having trouble resetting root password on my Linode\n",
    "vlan": null,
    "volume_id": null
  }'
```

`POST /support/tickets`

Open a Support Ticket.
Only one of the ID attributes (`linode_id`, `domain_id`, etc.) can be set on a single Support Ticket.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "database_id": 0,
  "description": "I'm having trouble setting the root password on my Linode. I tried following the instructions but something is not working and I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong. Can you please help me figure out how I can reset it?\n",
  "domain_id": null,
  "firewall_id": 0,
  "linode_id": 123,
  "lkecluster_id": 123,
  "longviewclient_id": null,
  "managed_issue": false,
  "nodebalancer_id": null,
  "region": null,
  "summary": "Having trouble resetting root password on my Linode\n",
  "vlan": null,
  "volume_id": null
}
```

<h3 id="support-ticket-open-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SupportTicketRequest](#schemasupportticketrequest)|false|Open a Support Ticket.|
|» database_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Managed Database this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|
|» description|body|string|true|The full details of the issue or question.<br>|
|» domain_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Domain this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|
|» firewall_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Firewall this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|
|» linode_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Linode this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|
|» lkecluster_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Kubernetes cluster this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|
|» longviewclient_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Longview client this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|
|» managed_issue|body|boolean|false|Designates if this ticket is related to a [Managed service](https://www.linode.com/products/managed/). If `true`, the following constraints will apply:<br>* No ID attributes (i.e. `linode_id`, `domain_id`, etc.) should be provided with this request.<br>* Your account must have a [Managed service enabled](/docs/api/managed/#managed-service-enable).<br>|
|» nodebalancer_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the NodeBalancer this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|
|» region|body|string|false|The [Region](/docs/api/regions/) ID for the associated VLAN this ticket is regarding.<br><br>Only allowed when submitting a VLAN ticket.<br>|
|» summary|body|string|true|The summary or title for this SupportTicket.<br>|
|» vlan|body|string|false|The label of the VLAN this ticket is regarding, if relevant. To view your VLANs, use the VLANs List ([GET /networking/vlans](/docs/api/networking/#vlans-list)) endpoint.<br><br>Requires a specified `region` to identify the VLAN.<br>|
|» volume_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Volume this ticket is regarding, if relevant.<br>|

## Support Ticket Attachment Create

<a id="opIdcreateTicketAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/support/tickets/0/attachments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'file=/Users/LinodeGuy/pictures/screen_shot.jpg'
```

`POST /support/tickets/{ticketId}/attachments`

Adds a file attachment to an existing Support
Ticket on your Account. File attachments are used to assist our
Support team in resolving your Ticket. Examples of attachments
are screen shots and text files that provide additional information.

The file attachment is submitted in the request as multipart/form-data.

**Note**: Accepted file extensions include: .gif, .jpg, .jpeg, .pjpg,
.pjpeg, .tif, .tiff, .png, .pdf, or .txt.


> Body parameter

```yaml
file: /Users/LinodeGuy/pictures/screen_shot.jpg
```

<h3 id="support-ticket-attachment-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ticketId|path|integer|true|The ID of the Support Ticket.|
|body|body|object|true|Add an attachment.|
|» file|body|string|true|The local, absolute path to the file you want to attach to your Support Ticket.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

```json

}
```

<h1 id="linode-api-tags">Tags</h1>

Tags allow you to organize and group your various Linode services. Use the Tags endpoints to create, assign, and delete your account tags.

## Tags List

<a id="opIdgetTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/tags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /tags`

Tags are User-defined labels attached to objects in your Account, such as Linodes. They are used for specifying and grouping attributes of objects that are relevant to the User.

This endpoint returns a paginated list of Tags on your account.


<h3 id="tags-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|The page of a collection to return.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "label": "example tag"
    }
  ],
  "page": 1,
  "pages": 1,
  "results": 1
}
```

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="tags-list-responses">Responses</h3>

## New Tag Create

<a id="opIdcreateTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "domains": [
      564,
      565
    ],
    "label": "example tag",
    "linodes": [
      123,
      456
    ],
    "nodebalancers": [
      10301,
      10501
    ],
    "volumes": [
      9082,
      10003
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /tags`

Creates a new Tag and optionally tags requested objects with it immediately.

**Important**: You must be an unrestricted User in order to add or modify Tags.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "domains": [
    564,
    565
  ],
  "label": "example tag",
  "linodes": [
    123,
    456
  ],
  "nodebalancers": [
    10301,
    10501
  ],
  "volumes": [
    9082,
    10003
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="new-tag-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|The tag to create, and optionally the objects to tag.<br>|
|» domains|body|[integer]|false|A list of Domain IDs to apply the new Tag to.  You must be allowed to `read_write` all of the requested Domains, or the Tag will not be created and an error will be returned.<br>|
|» label|body|string|true|The new Tag.<br>|
|» linodes|body|[integer]|false|A list of Linode IDs to apply the new Tag to.  You must be allowed to `read_write` all of the requested Linodes, or the Tag will not be created and an error will be returned.<br>|
|» nodebalancers|body|[integer]|false|A list of NodeBalancer IDs to apply the new Tag to. You must be allowed to `read_write` all of the requested NodeBalancers, or the Tag will not be created and an error will be returned.<br>|
|» volumes|body|[integer]|false|A list of Volume IDs to apply the new Tag to.  You must be allowed to `read_write` all of the requested Volumes, or the Tag will not be created and an error will be returned.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "label": "example tag"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```
