## Volume Create

<a id="opIdcreateVolume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/volumes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "config_id": 23456,
    "label": "my-volume",
    "linode_id": 123,
    "region": null,
    "size": 20,
    "tags": [
      "example tag",
      "another example"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /volumes`

Creates a Volume on your Account. In order for this to complete successfully, your User must have the `add_volumes` grant. Creating a new Volume will start accruing additional charges on your account.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config_id": 23456,
  "label": "my-volume",
  "linode_id": 123,
  "region": null,
  "size": 20,
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="volume-create-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|The requested initial state of a new Volume.|
|» config_id|body|integer|false|When creating a Volume attached to a Linode, the ID of the Linode Config to include the new Volume in. This Config must belong to the Linode referenced by `linode_id`. Must _not_ be provided if `linode_id` is not sent. If a `linode_id` is sent without a `config_id`, the volume will be attached:<br><br>  * to the Linode's only config if it only has one config.<br>  * to the Linode's last used config, if possible.<br><br>If no config can be selected for attachment, an error will be returned.<br>|
|» label|body|string|true|The Volume's label, which is also used in the `filesystem_path` of the resulting volume.<br>|
|» linode_id|body|integer|false|The Linode this volume should be attached to upon creation. If not given, the volume will be created without an attachment.<br>|
|» region|body|string|false|The Region to deploy this Volume in. This is only required if a linode_id is not given.<br>|
|» size|body|integer|false|The initial size of this volume, in GB.  Be aware that volumes may only be resized up after creation.<br>|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of Tags applied to this object.  Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "filesystem_path": "/dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0Linode_Volume_my-volume",
  "hardware_type": "nvme",
  "id": 12345,
  "label": "my-volume",
  "linode_id": 12346,
  "linode_label": "linode123",
  "region": "us-east",
  "size": 30,
  "status": "active",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="volume-create-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Creating Volume.<br>|[Volume](#schemavolume)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="volume-create-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: volumes:read_write )
</aside>

<a id="opIddeleteVolume"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /volumes/{volumeId}`

Deletes a Volume you have permission to `read_write`.

* **Deleting a Volume is a destructive action and cannot be undone.**

* Deleting stops billing for the Volume. You will be billed for time used within
the billing period the Volume was active.

* Volumes that are migrating cannot be deleted until the migration is finished.

## Volume Attach

<a id="opIdattachVolume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/volumes/0/attach \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "config_id": 23456,
    "linode_id": 0,
    "persist_across_boots": true
  }'
```

`POST /volumes/{volumeId}/attach`

Attaches a Volume on your Account to an existing Linode on your Account. In order for this request to complete successfully, your User must have `read_only` or `read_write` permission to the Volume and `read_write` permission to the Linode. Additionally, the Volume and Linode must be located in the same Region.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config_id": 23456,
  "linode_id": 0,
  "persist_across_boots": true
}
```

<h3 id="volume-attach-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|volumeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Volume to attach.|
|body|body|object|true|Volume to attach to a Linode.|
|» config_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the Linode Config to include this Volume in. Must belong to the Linode referenced by `linode_id`. If not given, the last booted Config will be chosen.<br>|
|» linode_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the Linode to attach the volume to.|
|» persist_across_boots|body|boolean|false|Defaults to true, if false is provided, the Volume will not be attached to the Linode Config. In this case more than 8 Volumes may be attached to a Linode if a Linode has 16GB of RAM or more. The number of volumes that can be attached is equal to the number of GB of RAM that the Linode has, up to a maximum of 64. `config_id` should not be passed if this is set to false and linode_id must be passed. The Linode must be running.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "filesystem_path": "/dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0Linode_Volume_my-volume",
  "hardware_type": "nvme",
  "id": 12345,
  "label": "my-volume",
  "linode_id": 12346,
  "linode_label": "linode123",
  "region": "us-east",
  "size": 30,
  "status": "active",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Volume Clone

<a id="opIdcloneVolume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/volumes/0/clone \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "my-volume"
  }'
```

`POST /volumes/{volumeId}/clone`

Creates a Volume on your Account. In order for this request to complete successfully, your User must have the `add_volumes` grant. The new Volume will have the same size and data as the source Volume. Creating a new Volume will incur a charge on your Account.
* Only Volumes with a `status` of "active" can be cloned.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "my-volume"
}
```

<h3 id="volume-clone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|volumeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Volume to clone.|
|body|body|object|true|The requested state your Volume will be cloned into.|
|» label|body|string|true|The Volume's label is for display purposes only.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "filesystem_path": "/dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0Linode_Volume_my-volume",
  "hardware_type": "nvme",
  "id": 12345,
  "label": "my-volume",
  "linode_id": 12346,
  "linode_label": "linode123",
  "region": "us-east",
  "size": 30,
  "status": "active",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "updated": "2018-01-01T00:01:01"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="volume-clone-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Clone started.|[Volume](#schemavolume)|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="volume-clone-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: volumes:read_write )
</aside>

## Volume Resize

<a id="opIdresizeVolume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/volumes/0/resize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "size": 30
  }'
```

`POST /volumes/{volumeId}/resize`

Resize an existing Volume on your Account. In order for this request to complete successfully, your User must have the `read_write` permissions to the Volume.
* Volumes can only be resized up.
* Only Volumes with a `status` of "active" can be resized.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "size": 30
}
```

<h3 id="volume-resize-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|volumeId|path|integer|true|ID of the Volume to resize.|
|body|body|object|true|The requested size to increase your Volume to.|
|» size|body|integer|true|The Volume's size, in GiB.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
```

<h1 id="linode-api-account-1">account</h1>

## Service Transfer Cancel

<a id="opIddeleteServiceTransfer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/account/service-transfers/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /account/service-transfers/{token}`

Cancels the Service Transfer for the provided token. Once cancelled, a transfer cannot be accepted or otherwise
acted on in any way. If cancelled in error, the transfer must be
[created](/docs/api/account/#service-transfer-create) again.

When cancelled, an email notification for the cancellation is sent to the account that created
this transfer. Transfers can not be cancelled if they are expired or have been accepted.

This command can only be accessed by the unrestricted users of the account that created this transfer.


<h3 id="service-transfer-cancel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|path|string(uuid)|true|The UUID of the Service Transfer.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "fieldname",
      "reason": "fieldname must be a valid value"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="service-transfer-cancel-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Service Transfer cancelled.<br>|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|Inline|

<h3 id="service-transfer-cancel-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **default**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|errors|[[ErrorObject](#schemaerrorobject)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
personalAccessToken, oauth ( Scopes: account:read_write )
</aside>

Managed MongoDB Databases object.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_list|[string(ipv4/prefix_length)]|false|none|A list of IP addresses that can access the Managed Database. Each item can be a single IP address or a range in CIDR format.<br><br>By default, this is an empty array (`[]`), which blocks all connections (both public and private) to the Managed Database.<br><br>If `0.0.0.0/0` is a value in this list, then all IP addresses can access the Managed Database.<br>|
|cluster_size|integer|false|none|The number of Linode Instance nodes deployed to the Managed Database.<br><br>Choosing 3 nodes creates a high availability cluster consisting of 1 primary node and 2 replica nodes.<br>|
|compression_type|string|false|none|The type of data compression for this Database.<br><br>Snappy has a lower comparative compression ratio and resource consumption rate.<br><br>Zlip has a higher comparative compression ratio and resource consumption rate.<br>|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Managed Database was created.|
|encrypted|boolean|false|none|Whether the Managed Databases is encrypted.|
|engine|string|false|read-only|The Managed Database engine type.|
|hosts|object|false|read-only|The primary and secondary hosts for the Managed Database. These are assigned after provisioning is complete.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|A unique ID that can be used to identify and reference the Managed Database.|
|label|string|false|none|A unique, user-defined string referring to the Managed Database.|
|peers|[string]|false|none|An array of peer addresses for this Database.<br>|
|port|integer|false|none|The access port for this Managed Database.|
|region|string|false|none|The [Region](/docs/api/regions/) ID for the Managed Database.|
|replica_set|string \| null|false|none|Label for configuring a MongoDB [replica set](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication/). Choose the same label on multiple Databases to include them in the same replica set.<br><br>If `null`, the Database is not included in any replica set.<br>|
|ssl_connection|boolean|false|none|Whether to require SSL credentials to establish a connection to the Managed Database.<br><br>Use the **Managed MongoDB Database Credentials View** ([GET /databases/mongodb/instances/{instanceId}/credentials](/docs/api/databases/#managed-mongodb-database-credentials-view)) command for access information.<br>|
|status|string|false|read-only|The operating status of the Managed Database.|
|storage_engine|string|false|none|The type of storage engine for this Database.<br><br>**Note:** MMAPV1 is not available for MongoDB versions 4.0 and above.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The Linode Instance type used by the Managed Database for its nodes.|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Managed Database was last updated.|
|updates|object|false|none|Configuration settings for automated patch update maintenance for the Managed Database.|
|version|string|false|read-only|The Managed Database engine version.|

```json
  ],
```

A domain zonefile in our DNS system.  You must own the domain name and tell your registrar to use Linode's nameservers in order for a domain in our system to be treated as authoritative.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|axfr_ips|[string(ip)]|false|none|The list of IPs that may perform a zone transfer for this Domain. The total combined length of all data within this array cannot exceed 1000 characters.<br><br>**Note**: This is potentially dangerous, and should be set to an empty list unless you intend to use it.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|A description for this Domain. This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|domain|string|false|none|The domain this Domain represents. Domain labels cannot be longer than 63 characters and must conform to [RFC1035](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1035). Domains must be unique on Linode's platform, including across different Linode accounts; there cannot be two Domains representing the same domain.<br>|
|expire_sec|integer|false|none|The amount of time in seconds that may pass before this Domain is no longer<br>authoritative.<br><br>* Valid values are<br>0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br><br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br><br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 1209600.<br>|
|group|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** The group this Domain belongs to.  This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This Domain's unique ID|
|master_ips|[string(ip)]|false|none|The IP addresses representing the master DNS for this Domain. At least one value is required for `type` slave Domains. The total combined length of all data within this array cannot exceed 1000 characters.<br>|
|refresh_sec|integer|false|none|The amount of time in seconds before this Domain should be refreshed.<br><br>* Valid values are<br>0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br><br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br><br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 14400.<br>|
|retry_sec|integer|false|none|The interval, in seconds, at which a failed refresh should be retried.<br><br>* Valid values are<br>0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br><br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br><br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 14400.<br>|
|soa_email|string(email)|false|none|Start of Authority email address. This is required for `type` master Domains.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|Used to control whether this Domain is currently being rendered.<br>|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags applied to this object.  Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|ttl_sec|integer|false|none|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers.<br>* Valid values are 0, 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200.<br>* Any other value is rounded up to the nearest valid value.<br>* A value of 0 is equivalent to the default value of 86400.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|Whether this Domain represents the authoritative source of information for the domain it describes ("master"), or whether it is a read-only copy of a master ("slave").<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|disabled|
|status|active|
|type|master|
|type|slave|

```json
  "weight": 50

```

A single record on a Domain.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Domain Record was created.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This Record's unique ID.|
|name|string|false|none|The name of this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends<br>on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The hostname or FQDN of the Record.<br><br>`NS`: The subdomain, if any, to use with the Domain of the Record. Wildcard NS records (`*`) are not supported.<br><br>`MX`: The mail subdomain. For example, `sub` for the address `user@sub.example.com` under the `example.com`<br>Domain. Must be an empty string (`""`) for a Null MX Record.<br><br>`CNAME`: The hostname. Must be unique. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The hostname.<br><br>`SRV`: Unused. Use the `service` property to set the service name for this record.<br><br>`CAA`: The subdomain. Omit or enter an empty string (`""`) to apply to the entire Domain.<br><br>`PTR`: See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br>|
|port|integer|false|none|The port this Record points to. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|
|priority|integer|false|none|The priority of the target host for this Record. Lower values are preferred. Only valid for<br>MX and SRV record requests. Required for SRV record requests.<br><br>Defaults to `0` for MX record requests. Must be `0` for Null MX records.<br>|
|protocol|string \| null|false|none|The protocol this Record's service communicates with. An underscore (`_`) is prepended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid for SRV record requests.<br>|
|service|string \| null|false|none|The name of the service. An underscore (`_`) is prepended and a period (`.`) is appended automatically to the submitted value for this property. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|
|tag|string \| null|false|none|The tag portion of a CAA record. Only valid and required for CAA record requests.<br>|
|target|string|false|none|The target for this Record. For requests, this property's actual usage and whether it is required depends<br>on the type of record this represents:<br><br>`A` and `AAAA`: The IP address. Use `[remote_addr]` to submit the IPv4 address of the request. Required.<br><br>`NS`: The name server. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`MX`: The mail server. Must be a valid domain unless creating a Null MX Record. To create a<br>[Null MX Record](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7505), first<br>[remove](/docs/api/domains/#domain-record-delete) any additional MX records, create an MX record with empty strings<br>(`""`) for the `target` and `name`. If a Domain has a Null MX record, new MX records cannot be created. Required.<br><br>`CNAME`: The alias. Must be a valid domain. Required.<br><br>`TXT`: The value. Required.<br><br>`SRV`: The target domain or subdomain. If a subdomain is entered, it is automatically used with the Domain.<br>To configure for a different domain, enter a valid FQDN. For example, the value `www` with a Domain for<br>`example.com` results in a target set to `www.example.com`, whereas the value `sample.com` results in a<br>target set to `sample.com`. Required.<br><br>`CAA`: The value. For `issue` or `issuewild` tags, the domain of your certificate issuer. For the `iodef`<br>tag, a contact or submission URL (domain, http, https, or mailto). Requirements depend on the tag for this record:<br>  * `issue`: The domain of your certificate issuer. Must be a valid domain.<br>  * `issuewild`: Must begin with `*`.<br>  * `iodef`: Must be either (1) a valid domain, (2) a valid domain prepended with `http://` or `https://`, or (3) a valid email address prepended with `mailto:`.<br><br>`PTR`: Required. See our guide on how to [Configure Your Linode for Reverse DNS<br>(rDNS)](/docs/guides/configure-rdns/).<br><br>With the exception of A, AAAA, and CAA records, this field accepts a trailing period.<br>|
|ttl_sec|integer|false|none|"Time to Live" - the amount of time in seconds that this Domain's records may be cached by resolvers or other domain servers. Valid values are 300, 3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 57600, 86400, 172800, 345600, 604800, 1209600, and 2419200 - any other value will be rounded to the nearest valid value.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The type of Record this is in the DNS system. For example, A records associate a domain name with an IPv4 address, and AAAA records associate a domain name with an IPv6 address. For more information, see the guides on [DNS Record Types](/docs/products/networking/dns-manager/guides/#dns-record-types).<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Domain Record was last updated.|
|weight|integer|false|none|The relative weight of this Record used in the case of identical priority. Higher values are preferred. Only valid and required for SRV record requests.<br>|

|duration|number|false|read-only|The total duration in seconds that it takes for the Event to complete.<br>|
|entity|object|false|read-only|Detailed information about the Event's entity, including ID, type, label, and URL used to access it.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The unique ID of this Event.|
|message|string \| null|false|none|Provides additional information about the event. Additional information may include, but is not limited to, a more detailed representation of events which can help diagnose non-obvious failures.<br>|
|percent_complete|integer|false|read-only|A percentage estimating the amount of time remaining for an Event.<br>Returns `null` for notification events.<br>|
|rate|string|false|read-only|The rate of completion of the Event. Only some Events will return rate; for example, migration and resize Events.<br>|
|read|boolean|false|read-only|If this Event has been read.|
|secondary_entity|object|false|read-only|Detailed information about the Event's secondary entity, which provides additional information<br>for events such as, but not limited to, `linode_boot`, `linode_reboot`, `linode_create`, and `linode_clone` Event actions.<br>|
|seen|boolean|false|read-only|If this Event has been seen.|
|status|string|false|read-only|The current status of this Event.|
|time_remaining|string \| null|false|read-only|The estimated time remaining until the completion of this Event. This value is only returned for some in-progress migration events. For all other in-progress events, the `percent_complete` attribute will indicate about how much more work is to be done.<br>|
|username|string \| null|false|read-only|The username of the User who caused the Event.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Firewall">Firewall</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafirewall"></a>
<a id="schema_Firewall"></a>
<a id="tocSfirewall"></a>
<a id="tocsfirewall"></a>

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "id": 123,
  "label": "firewall123",
  "rules": {
    "inbound": [
      {
        "action": "ACCEPT",
        "addresses": {
          "ipv4": [
            "192.0.2.0/24"
          ],
          "ipv6": [
            "2001:DB8::/32"
          ]
        },
        "description": "An example firewall rule description.",
        "label": "firewallrule123",
        "ports": "22-24, 80, 443",
        "protocol": "TCP"
      }
    ],
    "inbound_policy": "DROP",
    "outbound": [
      {
        "action": "ACCEPT",
        "addresses": {
          "ipv4": [
            "192.0.2.0/24"
          ],
          "ipv6": [
            "2001:DB8::/32"
          ]
        },
        "description": "An example firewall rule description.",
        "label": "firewallrule123",
        "ports": "22-24, 80, 443",
        "protocol": "TCP"
      }
    ],
    "outbound_policy": "DROP"
  },
  "status": "enabled",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "updated": "2018-01-02T00:01:01"
}
```

A resource that controls incoming and outgoing network traffic to a Linode service. Only one Firewall can be attached to a Linode at any given time. [Create a Firewall Device](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-create) to assign a Firewall to a Linode service. Currently, Firewalls can only be assigned to Linode instances.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Firewall was created.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The Firewall's unique ID.<br>|
|label|string|false|none|The Firewall's label, for display purposes only.<br><br>Firewall labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * Must begin and end with an alphanumeric character.<br>  * May only consist of alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`) or periods (`.`).<br>  * Cannot have two dashes (`--`), underscores (`__`) or periods (`..`) in a row.<br>  * Must be between 3 and 32 characters.<br>  * Must be unique.<br>|
|rules|object|false|none|The inbound and outbound access rules to apply to the Firewall.<br><br>A Firewall may have up to 25 rules across its inbound and outbound rulesets.<br>|
|status|string|false|read-only|The status of this Firewall.<br><br>  * When a Firewall is first created its status is `enabled`.<br>  * Use the [Update Firewall](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-update) endpoint to set a Firewall's status to `enabled` or `disabled`.<br>  * Use the [Delete Firewall](/docs/api/networking/#firewall-delete) endpoint to delete a Firewall.<br>|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags applied to this object. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Firewall was last updated.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|enabled|
|status|disabled|
|status|deleted|

<h2 id="tocS_FirewallDevices">FirewallDevices</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafirewalldevices"></a>

```json
{
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "entity": {
    "id": 123,
    "label": "my-linode",
    "type": "linode",

  },
  "id": 123,
  "updated": "2018-01-02T00:01:01"
}
```

Associates a Firewall with a Linode service. A Firewall can be assigned to a single Linode service at a time. Additional disabled Firewalls can be assigned to a service, but they cannot be enabled if another active Firewall is already assigned to the same service.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Device was created.<br>|
|entity|object|false|read-only|The Linode service that this Firewall has been applied to.<br>|
|id|integer|false|none|The Device's unique ID<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Device was last updated.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_FirewallRuleConfig">FirewallRuleConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafirewallruleconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_FirewallRuleConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSfirewallruleconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsfirewallruleconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "action": "ACCEPT",
  "addresses": {
    "ipv4": [
      "192.0.2.0/24"
    ],
    "ipv6": [
      "2001:DB8::/32"
    ]
  },
  "description": "An example firewall rule description.",
  "label": "firewallrule123",
  "ports": "22-24, 80, 443",
  "protocol": "TCP"
}
```

One of a Firewall's inbound or outbound access rules. The `ports` property can be used to allow traffic on a comma-separated list of different ports.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|false|none|Controls whether traffic is accepted or dropped by this rule. Overrides the Firewall's `inbound_policy` if this is an inbound rule, or the `outbound_policy` if this is an outbound rule.<br>|
|addresses|object|false|none|Allowed IPv4 or IPv6 addresses. A Rule can have up to 255 addresses or networks listed across its IPv4 and IPv6 arrays. A network and a single IP are treated as equivalent when accounting for this limit.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|Used to describe this rule. For display purposes only.<br>|
|label|string|false|none|Used to identify this rule. For display purposes only.<br>|
|ports|string|false|none|A string representing the port or ports on which traffic will be allowed:<br><br>- The string may be a single port, a range of ports, or a comma-separated list of single ports and port ranges. A space is permitted following each comma.<br>- A range of ports is inclusive of the start and end values for the range. The end value of the range must be greater than the start value.<br>- Ports must be within 1 and 65535, and may not contain any leading zeroes. For example, port "080" is not allowed.<br>- Ports may not be specified if a rule's protocol is `ICMP` or `IPENCAP`.<br>- At least one port must be specified if a rule's protocol is `TCP` or `UDP`.<br>- The ports string can have up to 15 *pieces*, where a single port is treated as one piece, and a port range is treated as two pieces. For example, the string "22-24, 80, 443" has four pieces.<br>|
|protocol|string|false|none|The type of network traffic to allow.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|action|ACCEPT|
|action|DROP|
|protocol|TCP|
|protocol|UDP|
|protocol|ICMP|
|protocol|IPENCAP|

For SLAAC and link-local addresses, this value may not be changed.<br>|

|public|boolean|false|read-only|Whether this is a public or private IP address.<br>|
|rdns|string \| null|false|none|The reverse DNS assigned to this address. For public IPv4 addresses, this will be set to a default value provided by Linode if not explicitly set.<br>|

|subnet_mask|string(ip)|false|read-only|The mask that separates host bits from network bits for this address.<br>|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of address this is.<br>|

A request object IP Addresses Share (POST /networking/ips/share)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ips|[string(ip)]|true|none|A list of secondary Linode IPs to share with the primary Linode.<br>* Can include both IPv4 addresses and IPv6 ranges (omit /56 and /64 prefix lengths)<br>* Can include both private and public IPv4 addresses.<br>* You must have access to all of these addresses and they must be in the same Region as the primary Linode.<br>* Enter an empty array to remove all shared IP addresses.<br>|
|linode_id|integer|true|none|The ID of the primary Linode that the addresses will be shared with.<br>|

Image object

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Image was created.|
|created_by|string|false|read-only|The name of the User who created this Image, or "linode" for public Images.<br>|
|deprecated|boolean|false|read-only|Whether or not this Image is deprecated. Will only be true for deprecated public Images.<br>|
|description|string \| null|false|none|A detailed description of this Image.|
|eol|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date of the public Image's planned end of life. `None` for private Images.<br>|
|expiry|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Only Images created automatically from a deleted Linode (type=automatic) will expire.<br>|
|id|string|false|read-only|The unique ID of this Image.|
|is_public|boolean|false|read-only|True if the Image is a public distribution image. False if Image is private Account-specific Image.|
|label|string|false|none|A short description of the Image.<br>|
|size|integer|false|read-only|The minimum size this Image needs to deploy. Size is in MB.<br>|
|status|string|false|read-only|The current status of this Image.<br><br>Only Images in an "available" status can be deployed. Images in a "creating" status are being created from a Linode Disk, and will become "available" shortly. Images in a "pending_upload" status are waiting for data to be [uploaded](/docs/api/images/#image-upload), and become "available" after the upload and processing are complete.<br><br>The "+order_by" and "+order" operators are not available for [filtering](/docs/api/#filtering-and-sorting) on this key.<br>|
|type|string|false|read-only|How the Image was created.<br><br>"Manual" Images can be created at any time.<br><br>"Automatic" Images are created automatically from a deleted Linode.<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Image was last updated.|
|vendor|string|false|read-only|The upstream distribution vendor. `None` for private Images.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|status|pending_upload|
|status|available|
|type|manual|
|type|automatic|

A Kubernetes cluster.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|control_plane|object|false|none|Defines settings for the Kubernetes Control Plane. Allows for the enabling of High Availability (HA) for Control Plane Components. Enabling High Avaialability for LKE is an **irreversible** change.<br>|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Kubernetes cluster was created.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This Kubernetes cluster's unique ID.|
|k8s_version|string|false|none|The desired Kubernetes version for this Kubernetes cluster in the format of &lt;major&gt;.&lt;minor&gt;, and the latest supported patch version will be deployed.<br>|
|label|string|false|none|This Kubernetes cluster's unique label for display purposes only.<br>Labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * UTF-8 characters will be returned by the API using escape<br>    sequences of their Unicode code points. For example, the<br>    Japanese character *か* is 3 bytes in UTF-8 (`0xE382AB`). Its<br>    Unicode code point is 2 bytes (`0x30AB`). APIv4 supports this<br>    character and the API will return it as the escape sequence<br>    using six 1 byte characters which represent 2 bytes of Unicode<br>    code point (`"\u30ab"`).<br>  * 4 byte UTF-8 characters are not supported.<br>  * If the label is entirely composed of UTF-8 characters, the API<br>    response will return the code points using up to 193 1 byte<br>    characters.<br>|
|region|string|false|none|This Kubernetes cluster's location.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags applied to the Kubernetes cluster. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Kubernetes cluster was updated.|

The set of Node Pools which are members of the Kubernetes cluster. Node Pools consist of a Linode type, the number of Linodes to deploy of that type, and additional status information.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|autoscaler|object|false|none|When enabled, the number of nodes autoscales within the defined minimum and maximum values.<br>|
|count|integer|false|none|The number of nodes in the Node Pool.|
|disks|[object]|false|none|This Node Pool's custom disk layout.<br>|
|id|integer|false|none|This Node Pool's unique ID.<br>|
|nodes|[[LKENodeStatus](#schemalkenodestatus)]|false|none|Status information for the Nodes which are members of this Node Pool. If a Linode has not been provisioned for a given Node slot, the instance_id will be returned as null.<br>|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags applied to this object. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The Linode Type for all of the nodes in the Node Pool.|

Specifies a collection of Linodes which will be members of a Kubernetes cluster.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|autoscaler|object|false|none|When enabled, the number of nodes autoscales within the defined minimum and maximum values.<br><br>When making a request, `max` and `min` require each other.<br>|
|count|integer|false|none|The number of nodes in the Node Pool.|
|disks|[object]|false|none|**Note**: This field should be omitted except for special use cases. The disks specified here are<br>partitions in *addition* to the primary partition and reduce the size of the primary partition,<br>which can lead to stability problems for the Node.<br><br>This Node Pool's custom disk layout. Each item in this array will create a new disk<br>partition for each node in this Node Pool.<br><br>  * The custom disk layout is applied to each node in this Node Pool.<br>  * The maximum number of custom disk partitions that can be configured is 7.<br>  * Once the requested disk paritions are allocated, the remaining disk space is allocated to the node's boot disk.<br>  * A Node Pool's custom disk layout is immutable over the lifetime of the Node Pool.<br>|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags applied to this object. Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The Linode Type for all of the nodes in the Node Pool.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alerts|object|false|none|none|
|backups|object|false|none|Information about this Linode's backups status. For information about available backups, see [/linode/instances/{linodeId}/backups](/docs/api/linode-instances/#backups-list).<br>|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Linode was created.|
|group|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** A deprecated property denoting a group label for this Linode.<br>|
|host_uuid|string(uuid)|false|read-only|The Linode's host machine, as a UUID.|
|hypervisor|string|false|read-only|The virtualization software powering this Linode.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This Linode's ID which must be provided for all operations impacting this Linode.<br>|
|image|object \| null|false|read-only|none|
|ipv4|[string]|false|read-only|This Linode's IPv4 Addresses. Each Linode is assigned a single public IPv4 address<br>upon creation, and may get a single private IPv4 address if needed. You may need to<br>[open a support ticket](/docs/api/support/#support-ticket-open)<br>to get additional IPv4 addresses.<br><br>IPv4 addresses may be reassigned between your Linodes, or shared with other Linodes.<br>See the [/networking](/docs/api/networking/) endpoints for details.<br>|
|ipv6|string(ipv6/128) \| null|false|read-only|This Linode's IPv6 SLAAC address. This address is specific to a Linode, and may not be shared. If the Linode has not been assigned an IPv6 address, the return value will be `null`.<br>|
|label|string|false|none|The Linode's label is for display purposes only. If no label is provided for a Linode,<br>a default will be assigned.<br><br>Linode labels have the following constraints:<br><br>  * Must begin and end with an alphanumeric character.<br>  * May only consist of alphanumeric characters, dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`) or periods (`.`).<br>  * Cannot have two dashes (`--`), underscores (`__`) or periods (`..`) in a row.<br>|
|region|string|false|read-only|This is the [Region](/docs/api/regions/#regions-list) where the Linode was deployed. A Linode's region can only be changed by initiating a [cross data center migration](/docs/api/linode-instances/#dc-migrationpending-host-migration-initiate).<br>|
|specs|object|false|read-only|Information about the resources available to this Linode.|
|status|string|false|read-only|A brief description of this Linode's current state. This field may change without direct action from you. For example, when a Linode goes into maintenance mode its status will display "stopped".<br>|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags applied to this object.  Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|type|string|false|read-only|This is the [Linode Type](/docs/api/linode-types/#types-list) that this Linode was deployed with.<br>To change a Linode's Type, use [POST /linode/instances/{linodeId}/resize](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-resize).<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Linode was last updated.|
|watchdog_enabled|boolean|false|none|The watchdog, named Lassie, is a Shutdown Watchdog that monitors your Linode and will reboot it if it powers off unexpectedly. It works by issuing a boot job when your Linode powers off without a shutdown job being responsible.<br>To prevent a loop, Lassie will give up if there have been more than 5 boot jobs issued within 15 minutes.<br>|

```json
  "run_level": "default",
  "virt_mode": "paravirt"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|comments|string \| null|false|none|Optional field for arbitrary User comments on this Config.|

|helpers|object|false|none|Helpers enabled when booting to this Linode Config.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The ID of this Config.|
|interfaces|[LinodeConfigInterfaces](#schemalinodeconfiginterfaces)|false|none|An array of Network Interfaces to add to this Linode's Configuration Profile.<br><br>Up to three interface objects can be entered in this array. The position in the array determines the interface to which the settings apply:<br><br>- First/0:  eth0<br>- Second/1: eth1<br>- Third/2:  eth2<br><br>When updating a Linode's interfaces, *each interface must be redefined*. An empty interfaces array results in a default public interface configuration only.<br><br>If no public interface is configured, public IP addresses are still assigned to the Linode but will not be usable without manual configuration.<br><br>**Note:** Changes to Linode interface configurations can be enabled by rebooting the Linode.<br><br>**Note:** Only Next Generation Network (NGN) data centers support VLANs. Use the Regions ([/regions](/docs/api/regions/)) endpoint to view the capabilities of data center regions.<br>If a VLAN is attached to your Linode and you attempt to migrate or clone it to a non-NGN data center,<br>the migration or cloning will not initiate. If a Linode cannot be migrated because of an incompatibility,<br>you will be prompted to select a different data center or contact support.<br><br>**Note:** See the [VLANs Overview](/docs/products/networking/vlans/#technical-specifications) guide to view additional specifications and limitations.<br>|
|kernel|string|false|none|A Kernel ID to boot a Linode with. Defaults to "linode/latest-64bit".|
|label|string|false|none|The Config's label is for display purposes only.<br>|
|memory_limit|integer|false|none|Defaults to the total RAM of the Linode.<br>|
|root_device|string|false|none|The root device to boot.<br>* If no value or an invalid value is provided, root device will default to `/dev/sda`.<br>* If the device specified at the root device location is not mounted, the Linode will not boot until a device is mounted.<br>|
|run_level|string|false|none|Defines the state of your Linode after booting. Defaults to `default`.<br>|
|virt_mode|string|false|none|Controls the virtualization mode. Defaults to `paravirt`.<br>* `paravirt` is suitable for most cases. Linodes running in paravirt mode<br>  share some qualities with the host, ultimately making it run faster since<br>  there is less transition between it and the host.<br>* `fullvirt` affords more customization, but is slower because 100% of the VM<br>  is virtualized.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_LinodeConfigInterface">LinodeConfigInterface</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinodeconfiginterface"></a>
<a id="schema_LinodeConfigInterface"></a>
<a id="tocSlinodeconfiginterface"></a>
<a id="tocslinodeconfiginterface"></a>

```json
{
  "ipam_address": "10.0.0.1/24",
  "label": "example-interface",
  "purpose": "vlan"
}
```

The Network Interface to apply to this Linode's configuration profile.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ipam_address|string(ip/netmask) \| null|false|none|This Network Interface's private IP address in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation.<br><br>Only used for `vlan` purpose interfaces. Must be an empty string or `null` for `public` purpose interfaces.<br><br>The Linode is configured to use this address for the associated interface upon reboot if Network Helper is enabled. If Network Helper is disabled, the address can be enabled with [manual static IP configuration](/docs/guides/manual-network-configuration/).<br><br>Must be unique among the Linode's interfaces.<br>|
|label|string \| null|false|none|The name of this interface.<br><br>Required for `vlan` purpose interfaces. Must be an empty string or `null` for `public` purpose interfaces.<br><br>If the VLAN label is new, a VLAN is created. Up to 10 VLANs can be created in each data center region. To view your active VLANs, use the [VLANs List](/docs/api/networking/#vlans-list) endpoint.<br><br>May only consist of ASCII letters, numbers, and dashes (`-`).<br><br>Must be unique among the Linode's interfaces.<br>|
|purpose|string|false|none|The type of interface.<br><br>* `public`<br>  * Only one `public` interface per Linode can be defined.<br>  * The Linode's default public IPv4 address is assigned to the `public` interface.<br>  * A Linode must have a public interface in the first/eth0 position to be reachable via the public internet upon boot without additional system configuration. If no `public` interface is configured, the Linode is not directly reachable via the public internet. In this case, access can only be established via LISH or other Linodes connected to the same VLAN.<br><br>* `vlan`<br>  * Configuring a `vlan` purpose interface attaches this Linode to the VLAN with the specified `label`.<br>  * The Linode is configured to use the specified `ipam_address`, if any.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|purpose|public|
|purpose|vlan|

<h2 id="tocS_LinodeConfigInterfaces">LinodeConfigInterfaces</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalinodeconfiginterfaces"></a>
<a id="schema_LinodeConfigInterfaces"></a>
<a id="tocSlinodeconfiginterfaces"></a>
<a id="tocslinodeconfiginterfaces"></a>

```json
[
  {
    "ipam_address": "10.0.0.1/24",
    "label": "example-interface",
    "purpose": "vlan"
  }
]
```

An array of Network Interfaces to add to this Linode's Configuration Profile.

Up to three interface objects can be entered in this array. The position in the array determines the interface to which the settings apply:

- First/0:  eth0
- Second/1: eth1
- Third/2:  eth2

When updating a Linode's interfaces, *each interface must be redefined*. An empty interfaces array results in a default public interface configuration only.

If no public interface is configured, public IP addresses are still assigned to the Linode but will not be usable without manual configuration.

**Note:** Changes to Linode interface configurations can be enabled by rebooting the Linode.

**Note:** Only Next Generation Network (NGN) data centers support VLANs. Use the Regions ([/regions](/docs/api/regions/)) endpoint to view the capabilities of data center regions.
If a VLAN is attached to your Linode and you attempt to migrate or clone it to a non-NGN data center,
the migration or cloning will not initiate. If a Linode cannot be migrated because of an incompatibility,
you will be prompted to select a different data center or contact support.

**Note:** See the [VLANs Overview](/docs/products/networking/vlans/#technical-specifications) guide to view additional specifications and limitations.

Common properties for creating and rebuilding Linodes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorized_keys|[string]|false|write-only|A list of public SSH keys that will be automatically appended<br>to the root user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|authorized_users|[string]|false|write-only|A list of usernames. If the usernames have associated SSH keys, the keys will be appended to the root users `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file automatically when deploying from an Image.<br>|
|booted|boolean|false|write-only|This field defaults to `true` if the Linode is created with an Image or from a Backup.<br>If it is deployed from an Image or a Backup and you wish it to remain `offline` after deployment, set this to `false`.<br>|
|image|string|false|none|An Image ID to deploy the Linode Disk from.<br><br>Access the Images List ([GET /images](/docs/api/images/#images-list)) endpoint with authentication to view<br>all available Images. Official Linode Images start with `linode/`, while your Account's Images start with `private/`. Creating<br>a disk from a Private Image requires `read_only` or `read_write` permissions for that Image. Access the User's<br>Grant Update ([PUT /account/users/{username}/grants](/docs/api/account/#users-grants-update)) endpoint to<br>adjust permissions for an Account Image.<br>|
|root_pass|string(password)|false|write-only|This sets the root user's password on a newly-created Linode Disk when deploying from an Image.<br><br>* **Required** when creating a Linode Disk from an Image, including when using a StackScript.<br><br>* Must meet a password strength score requirement that is calculated internally by the API.<br>If the strength requirement is not met, you will receive a `Password does not meet strength requirement` error.<br>|
|stackscript_data|object|false|none|This field is required only if the StackScript being deployed requires input data from the User for successful completion. See [User Defined Fields (UDFs)](/docs/guides/writing-scripts-for-use-with-linode-stackscripts-a-tutorial/#user-defined-fields-udfs) for more details.<br><br>This field is required to be valid JSON.<br><br>Total length cannot exceed 65,535 characters.<br>|
|stackscript_id|integer|false|none|A StackScript ID that will cause the referenced StackScript to be run during<br>deployment of this Linode. A compatible `image` is required to use a<br>StackScript. To get a list of available StackScript and their permitted Images<br>see [/stackscripts](/docs/api/stackscripts/#stackscripts-list).<br>This field cannot be used when deploying from a Backup or a Private Image.<br>|

Returns collection of Linode types, including pricing and specifications for each type. These are used when [creating](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-create) or [resizing](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-resize) Linodes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|addons|object|false|read-only|A list of optional add-on services for Linodes and their associated costs.<br>|
|class|string|false|read-only|The class of the Linode Type. We currently offer five classes of Linodes:<br><br>  * nanode - Nanode instances are good for low-duty workloads,<br>    where performance isn't critical. **Note:** As of June 16th, 2020, Nanodes became<br>    1 GB Linodes in the Cloud Manager, however, the API, the CLI, and billing will<br>    continue to refer to these instances as Nanodes.<br>  * standard - Standard Shared instances are good for medium-duty workloads and<br>    are a good mix of performance, resources, and price. **Note:** As of June 16th, 2020,<br>    Standard Linodes in the Cloud Manager became Shared Linodes, however, the API, the CLI, and<br>    billing will continue to refer to these instances as Standard Linodes.<br>  * dedicated - Dedicated CPU instances are good for full-duty workloads<br>    where consistent performance is important.<br>  * gpu - Linodes with dedicated NVIDIA Quadro &reg; RTX 6000 GPUs accelerate highly<br>    specialized applications such as machine learning, AI, and video transcoding.<br>  * highmem - High Memory instances favor RAM over other resources, and can be<br>    good for memory hungry use cases like caching and in-memory databases.<br>    All High Memory plans contain dedicated CPU cores.<br>|
|disk|integer|false|read-only|The Disk size, in MB, of the Linode Type.<br>|
|gpus|integer|false|read-only|The number of GPUs this Linode Type offers.<br>|
|id|string|false|read-only|The ID representing the Linode Type.|
|label|string|false|read-only|The Linode Type's label is for display purposes only.<br>|
|memory|integer|false|read-only|Amount of RAM included in this Linode Type.<br>|
|network_out|integer|false|read-only|The Mbits outbound bandwidth allocation.<br>|
|price|object|false|read-only|Cost in US dollars, broken down into hourly and monthly charges.<br>|
|successor|string \| null|false|read-only|The Linode Type that a [mutate](/docs/api/linode-instances/#linode-upgrade) will upgrade to for a Linode of this type.  If "null", a Linode of this type may not mutate.<br>|
|transfer|integer|false|read-only|The monthly outbound transfer amount, in MB.<br>|
|vcpus|integer|false|read-only|The number of VCPU cores this Linode Type offers.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|class|nanode|
|class|standard|
|class|dedicated|
|class|gpu|
|class|highmem|

|id|integer|false|read-only|This Issue's unique ID.<br>|
|services|[integer]|false|read-only|An array of Managed Service IDs that were affected by this Issue.<br>|

A service that Linode is monitoring as part of your Managed services. If issues are detected with this service, a ManagedIssue will be opened and, optionally, Linode special forces will attempt to resolve the Issue.

|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Managed Service was created.|

|label|string|false|none|The label for this Service. This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|notes|string \| null|false|none|Any information relevant to the Service that Linode special forces should know when attempting to resolve Issues.<br>|
|region|string|false|none|The Region in which this Service is located. This is required if address is a private IP, and may not be set otherwise.<br>|
|service_type|string|false|none|How this Service is monitored.<br>|
|status|string|false|read-only|The current status of this Service.<br>|
|timeout|integer|false|none|How long to wait, in seconds, for a response before considering the Service to be down.<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this Managed Service was last updated.|

<h2 id="tocS_NodeBalancer">NodeBalancer</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanodebalancer"></a>
<a id="schema_NodeBalancer"></a>
<a id="tocSnodebalancer"></a>
<a id="tocsnodebalancer"></a>

```json
{
  "client_conn_throttle": 0,
  "created": "2018-01-01T00:01:01",
  "hostname": "192.0.2.1.ip.linodeusercontent.com",
  "id": 12345,
  "ipv4": "203.0.113.1",
  "ipv6": null,
  "label": "balancer12345",
  "region": "us-east",
  "tags": [
    "example tag",
    "another example"
  ],
  "transfer": {
    "in": 28.91200828552246,
    "out": 3.5487728118896484,
    "total": 32.46078109741211
  },
  "updated": "2018-03-01T00:01:01"
}
```

Linode's load balancing solution.  Can handle multiple ports, SSL termination, and any number of backends.  NodeBalancer ports are configured with NodeBalancer Configs, and each config is given one or more NodeBalancer Node that accepts traffic.  The traffic should be routed to the  NodeBalancer's ip address, the NodeBalancer will handle routing individual requests to backends.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_conn_throttle|integer|false|none|Throttle connections per second.  Set to 0 (zero) to disable throttling.<br>|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this NodeBalancer was created.<br>|
|hostname|string|false|read-only|This NodeBalancer's hostname, beginning with its IP address and ending with _.ip.linodeusercontent.com_.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This NodeBalancer's unique ID.<br>|
|ipv4|string(ip)|false|read-only|This NodeBalancer's public IPv4 address.<br>|
|ipv6|string(ip) \| null|false|read-only|This NodeBalancer's public IPv6 address.<br>|
|label|string|false|none|This NodeBalancer's label. These must be unique on your Account.<br>|
|region|string|false|read-only|The Region where this NodeBalancer is located. NodeBalancers only support backends in the same Region.<br>|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of Tags applied to this object.  Tags are for organizational purposes only.<br>|
|transfer|object|false|read-only|Information about the amount of transfer this NodeBalancer has had so far this month.<br>|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|When this NodeBalancer was last updated.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_NodeBalancerConfig">NodeBalancerConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanodebalancerconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_NodeBalancerConfig"></a>
<a id="tocSnodebalancerconfig"></a>
<a id="tocsnodebalancerconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "algorithm": "roundrobin",
  "check": "http_body",
  "check_attempts": 3,
  "check_body": "it works",
  "check_interval": 90,
  "check_passive": true,
  "check_path": "/test",
  "check_timeout": 10,
  "cipher_suite": "recommended",
  "id": 4567,
  "nodebalancer_id": 12345,
  "nodes_status": {
    "down": 0,
    "up": 4
  },
  "port": 80,
  "protocol": "http",
  "proxy_protocol": "none",
  "ssl_cert": "<REDACTED>",
  "ssl_commonname": "www.example.com",
  "ssl_fingerprint": "00:01:02:03:04:05:06:07:08:09:0A:0B:0C:0D:0E:0F:10:11:12:13",
  "ssl_key": "<REDACTED>",
  "stickiness": "http_cookie"
}
```

A NodeBalancer config represents the configuration of this NodeBalancer on a single port.  For example, a NodeBalancer Config on port 80 would typically represent how this NodeBalancer response to HTTP requests.

NodeBalancer configs have a list of backends, called "nodes," that they forward requests between based on their configuration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|algorithm|string|false|none|What algorithm this NodeBalancer should use for routing traffic to backends.<br>|
|check|string|false|none|The type of check to perform against backends to ensure they are serving requests. This is used to determine if backends are up or down.<br>* If `none` no check is performed.<br>* `connection` requires only a connection to the backend to succeed.<br>* `http` and `http_body` rely on the backend serving HTTP, and that<br>  the response returned matches what is expected.<br>|
|check_attempts|integer|false|none|How many times to attempt a check before considering a backend to be down.<br>|
|check_body|string|false|none|This value must be present in the response body of the check in order for it to pass. If this value is not present in the response body of a check request, the backend is considered to be down.<br>|
|check_interval|integer|false|none|How often, in seconds, to check that backends are up and serving requests.<br><br>Must be greater than `check_timeout`.<br>|
|check_passive|boolean|false|none|If true, any response from this backend with a `5xx` status code will be enough for it to be considered unhealthy and taken out of rotation.<br>|
|check_path|string|false|none|The URL path to check on each backend. If the backend does not respond to this request it is considered to be down.<br>|
|check_timeout|integer|false|none|How long, in seconds, to wait for a check attempt before considering it failed.<br><br>Must be less than `check_interval`.<br>|
|cipher_suite|string|false|none|What ciphers to use for SSL connections served by this NodeBalancer.<br><br>* `legacy` is considered insecure and should only be used if necessary.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This config's unique ID|
|nodebalancer_id|integer|false|read-only|The ID for the NodeBalancer this config belongs to.<br>|
|nodes_status|object|false|read-only|A structure containing information about the health of the backends for this port.  This information is updated periodically as checks are performed against backends.<br>|
|port|integer|false|none|The port this Config is for. These values must be unique across configs on a single NodeBalancer (you can't have two configs for port 80, for example).  While some ports imply some protocols, no enforcement is done and you may configure your NodeBalancer however is useful to you. For example, while port 443 is generally used for HTTPS, you do not need SSL configured to have a NodeBalancer listening on port 443.<br>|
|protocol|string|false|none|The protocol this port is configured to serve.<br><br>* The `http` and `tcp` protocols do not support `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>* The `https` protocol is mutually required with `ssl_cert` and `ssl_key`.<br><br>Review our guide on [Available Protocols](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/protocols/) for information on protocol features.<br>|
|proxy_protocol|string|false|none|ProxyProtocol is a TCP extension that sends initial TCP connection information such as source/destination IPs and ports to backend devices. This information would be lost otherwise. Backend devices must be configured to work with ProxyProtocol if enabled.<br><br>* If ommited, or set to `none`, the NodeBalancer doesn't send any auxilary data over TCP connections. This is the default.<br>* If set to `v1`, the human-readable header format (Version 1) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>* If set to `v2`, the binary header format (Version 2) is used. Requires `tcp` protocol.<br>|
|ssl_cert|string(ssl-cert) \| null|false|none|The PEM-formatted public SSL certificate (or the combined PEM-formatted SSL<br>certificate and Certificate Authority chain) that should be served on this<br>NodeBalancerConfig's port.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>[Diffie-Hellman Parameters](/docs/products/networking/nodebalancers/guides/ssl-termination/#diffie-hellman-parameters) can be included in this value to enable forward secrecy.<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|ssl_commonname|string|false|read-only|The read-only common name automatically derived from the SSL certificate assigned to this NodeBalancerConfig. Please refer to this field to verify that the appropriate certificate is assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|ssl_fingerprint|string|false|read-only|The read-only SHA1-encoded fingerprint automatically derived from the SSL certificate assigned to this NodeBalancerConfig. Please refer to this field to verify that the appropriate certificate is assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|ssl_key|string(ssl-key) \| null|false|none|The PEM-formatted private key for the SSL certificate set in the `ssl_cert` field.<br><br>Line breaks must be represented as "\n" in the string for requests (but not when using the Linode CLI).<br><br>The contents of this field will not be shown in any responses that display<br>the NodeBalancerConfig. Instead, `<REDACTED>` will be printed where the field<br>appears.<br><br>The read-only `ssl_commonname` and `ssl_fingerprint` fields in a NodeBalancerConfig<br>response are automatically derived from your certificate. Please refer to these fields to<br>verify that the appropriate certificate was assigned to your NodeBalancerConfig.<br>|
|stickiness|string|false|none|Controls how session stickiness is handled on this port.<br>* If set to `none` connections will always be assigned a backend based on the algorithm configured.<br>* If set to `table` sessions from the same remote address will be routed to the same<br>  backend.<br><br>* For HTTP or HTTPS clients, `http_cookie` allows sessions to be<br>  routed to the same backend based on a cookie set by the NodeBalancer.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|algorithm|roundrobin|
|algorithm|leastconn|
|algorithm|source|
|check|none|
|check|connection|
|check|http|
|check|http_body|
|cipher_suite|recommended|
|cipher_suite|legacy|
|protocol|http|
|protocol|https|
|protocol|tcp|
|proxy_protocol|none|
|proxy_protocol|v1|
|proxy_protocol|v2|
|stickiness|none|
|stickiness|table|
|stickiness|http_cookie|

<h2 id="tocS_NodeBalancerNode">NodeBalancerNode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanodebalancernode"></a>
<a id="schema_NodeBalancerNode"></a>
<a id="tocSnodebalancernode"></a>
<a id="tocsnodebalancernode"></a>

```json
{
  "address": "192.168.210.120:80",
  "config_id": 4567,
  "id": 54321,
  "label": "node54321",
  "mode": "accept",
  "nodebalancer_id": 12345,
  "status": "UP",
  "weight": 50
}
```

A NodeBalancerNode represents a single backend serving requests for a single port of a NodeBalancer.  Nodes are specific to NodeBalancer Configs, and serve traffic over their private IP.  If the same Linode is serving traffic for more than one port on the same NodeBalancer, one NodeBalancer Node is required for each config (port) it should serve requests on.  For example, if you have four backends, and each should response to both HTTP and HTTPS requests, you will need two NodeBalancerConfigs (port 80 and port 443) and four backends each - one for each of the Linodes serving requests for that port.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|address|string(ip)|false|none|The private IP Address where this backend can be reached. This _must_ be a private IP address.<br>|
|config_id|integer|false|read-only|The NodeBalancer Config ID that this Node belongs to.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This node's unique ID.|
|label|string|false|none|The label for this node.  This is for display purposes only.<br>|
|mode|string|false|none|The mode this NodeBalancer should use when sending traffic to this backend.<br>* If set to `accept` this backend is accepting traffic.<br>* If set to `reject` this backend will not receive traffic.<br>* If set to `drain` this backend will not receive _new_ traffic, but connections already<br>  pinned to it will continue to be routed to it.<br><br>* If set to `backup`, this backend will only receive traffic if all `accept` nodes<br>  are down.<br>|
|nodebalancer_id|integer|false|read-only|The NodeBalancer ID that this Node belongs to.<br>|
|status|string|false|read-only|The current status of this node, based on the configured checks of its NodeBalancer Config.<br>|
|weight|integer|false|none|Used when picking a backend to serve a request and is not pinned to a single backend yet.  Nodes with a higher weight will receive more traffic.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|accept|
|mode|reject|
|mode|drain|
|mode|backup|
|status|unknown|
|status|UP|
|status|DOWN|

<h2 id="tocS_OAuthClient">OAuthClient</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaoauthclient"></a>
<a id="schema_OAuthClient"></a>
<a id="tocSoauthclient"></a>
<a id="tocsoauthclient"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "2737bf16b39ab5d7b4a1",
  "label": "Test_Client_1",
  "public": false,
  "redirect_uri": "https://example.org/oauth/callback",
  "secret": "<REDACTED>",
  "status": "active",
  "thumbnail_url": "https://api.linode.com/v4/account/clients/2737bf16b39ab5d7b4a1/thumbnail"
}
```

A third-party application registered to Linode that users may log into with their Linode account through our authentication server at <a target="_top" href="https://login.linode.com">https://login.linode.com</a>.  Using an OAuth Client, a third-party developer may be given access to some, or all, of a User's account for the purposes of their application.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|read-only|The OAuth Client ID.  This is used to identify the client, and is a publicly-known value (it is not a secret).<br>|
|label|string|false|none|The name of this application.  This will be presented to users when they are asked to grant it access to their Account.<br>|
|public|boolean|false|none|If this is a public or private OAuth Client.  Public clients have a slightly different authentication workflow than private clients.  See the <a target="_top" href="https://oauth.net/2/">OAuth spec</a> for more details.<br>|
|redirect_uri|string(url)|false|none|The location a successful log in from <a target="_top" href="https://login.linode.com">https://login.linode.com</a> should be redirected to for this client.  The receiver of this redirect should be ready to accept an OAuth exchange code and finish the OAuth exchange.<br>|
|secret|string|false|read-only|The OAuth Client secret, used in the OAuth exchange.  This is returned as `<REDACTED>` except when an OAuth Client is created or its secret is reset.  This is a secret, and should not be shared or disclosed publicly.<br>|
|status|string|false|read-only|The status of this application.  `active` by default.<br>|
|thumbnail_url|string(url) \| null|false|read-only|The URL where this client's thumbnail may be viewed, or `null` if this client does not have a thumbnail set.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|disabled|
|status|suspended|

Limited Access Keys restrict this Object Storage key's access to only the bucket(s) declared in this array and define their bucket-level permissions.<br><br><br>  Limited Access Keys can:<br><br>  * [list all buckets](/docs/api/object-storage/#object-storage-buckets-list) available on this Account, but cannot perform any actions on a bucket unless it has access to the bucket.<br><br><br>  * [create new buckets](/docs/api/object-storage/#object-storage-bucket-create), but do not have any access to the buckets it creates, unless explicitly given access to them.<br><br><br>  **Note:** You can create an Object Storage Limited Access Key without access to any buckets.<br>  This is achieved by sending a request with an empty `bucket_access` array.<br><br><br>  **Note:** If this field is omitted, a regular unlimited access key is issued.<br>|
|id|integer|false|read-only|This keypair's unique ID|
|label|string|false|none|The label given to this key. For display purposes only.|
|limited|boolean|false|read-only|Whether or not this key is a limited access key. Will return `false` if this key grants full access to all buckets on the user's account.|
|secret_key|string|false|read-only|This keypair's secret key. Only returned on key creation.|
